title: Drawing tools
body:
## Context
A charting terminal is judged on two things: how fast it draws price, and how naturally the trader can mark it up. E11 delivers the first; this Epic delivers the second. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 scopes **E14 Drawing tools** as: "Trend line, ray, extended line, horizontal/vertical line, rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, pitchfork, Fibonacci retracement/extension/time-zone, long/short position tool, text/note, measure tool; magnet-to-OHLC; multi-select, drag, resize, clone, lock, delete; per-drawing styling; persistence per symbol and per layout; keyboard-operable creation and nudge for a11y" (47 pts).

The engine contract is already written: `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 (drawing model, two-phase interaction, magnet mode, command-stack undo/redo, instanced thick-line rendering), §3.9 (hit-testing via a 64 px uniform grid, ≤1 ms for 200 drawings + 50 lines), §14 milestone **M7 Drawings**. The persistence contract is `drawings` in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 (migration `0011_workspace`) exposed as `/api/v1/drawings`, `/api/v1/drawings/batch`, `/api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`. The surface is **SCR-037 Drawing toolbar & drawing properties** with the object tree living in **SCR-036**.

The non-negotiable invariant across every ticket here: **drawings are stored in chart space (time + price), never pixels**. Zoom, log/linear scale flips, DPI changes and bar-type changes must not move an anchor. The second invariant is a11y: `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 requires a manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass "on chart and drawing flows", so every tool must be creatable, selectable, nudgeable and deletable without a mouse.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Stories covering every Must/Should DRAW story: **US-DRAW-001** … **US-DRAW-009**.
- Screens: **SCR-037** (toolbar + properties popover), object-tree contribution to **SCR-036**.
- Components: **CMP-223** DrawingToolbar, **CMP-224** (object tree row), CMP-002 IconButton, CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, CMP-010 Slider, CMP-016 Tooltip, CMP-017 Popover, CMP-022 Kbd, CMP-031 ColorSwatch/ThemeChip, CMP-041 Menu, CMP-046 Drawer, CMP-049 Table.
- API: `GET/POST /api/v1/drawings`, `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`, `PUT/DELETE /api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}`.
- Tables: `drawings` (migration `0011_workspace`), soft-delete + 90 d purge per `21-database-schema.md` §retention.
- Engine: drawings layer (layer 3 of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3), object hit-test index, `addDrawing`/`pickAt` worker commands, `drawingChanged` event.

## Out of scope
- Line-cross **alerts** bound to a drawing (`drawings.alert_id`) — **E40 Alerts & notifications**; this Epic only keeps the column nullable and the UI affordance disabled.
- Sending the position tool to a real **order ticket** — **E30**; R1 ships the computation and a disabled/stubbed "send to ticket" behind a feature flag.
- Gann fans, brush/freehand polish and emoji markers beyond the catalogue enum — backlog Could items, not R1 exit criteria.
- Cross-**symbol** synchronisation of drawings (explicitly forbidden by US-DRAW-009 NFR).
- Multi-user/shared drawings — **E-collaboration**, R5.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The advertised tool set exists and persists
  Given a signed-in trader on a BTCUSDT chart
  When they create one drawing of each R1 tool and reload the app
  Then every drawing reappears at the identical time/price anchors on every pane showing BTCUSDT

Scenario: Anchors are chart-space, not pixels
  Given a trendline drawn on a 1m chart in linear scale
  When the trader switches to log scale, changes interval to 1h and changes bar type to range bars
  Then both anchors still resolve to the same timestamps and prices within one tick

Scenario: Interaction stays inside the frame budget
  Given 200 drawings on the chart
  When one drawing is dragged
  Then hit-testing costs ≤1 ms, the price/footprint layers are not re-rendered, and the drag sustains ≥58 fps (benchmark B8)

Scenario: Keyboard-only trader is not excluded
  Given a trader using only the keyboard with a screen reader
  When they enter keyboard drawing mode
  Then they can place both anchors, hear each anchor announced, nudge the result by 1 tick (arrow) and 10 ticks (Shift+arrow), and delete it — with no mouse event at any point

Scenario: Server rejects malformed geometry
  Given a client posts a drawing whose geometry has zero points or a tool outside the enum
  Then the API responds 422 with a field-level error and nothing is persisted
```

## Technical notes / design
Rendering lives in the engine worker as layer 3 (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3) so drags never invalidate the price layer. Lines are instanced quads expanded in the vertex shader (per-instance `p0`, `p1`, `width`, dash pattern index); labels use the shared SDF glyph atlas with a per-pane budget of ≤3 text draw calls. State lives in `DrawingStore` (§3.6) on the main thread, mirrored into the worker as an immutable snapshot per frame. Undo/redo is a 100-entry command stack shared with the toolbar. Persistence is optimistic-local with server reconciliation and a 500 ms debounce that collapses a whole drag into one `/drawings/batch` call.

## Test plan
Unit (engine geometry, magnet snap, fib level maths, R:R maths, command stack), property-based (anchor stability across bar-spec/scale changes, `screenToIndex∘indexToScreen` identity), contract (OpenAPI schemathesis over the four drawing operations), golden-image per tool per theme against SwiftShader (≤0.1 % diff), Playwright E2E for create/drag/undo/redo/lock/hide/keyboard creation, perf benchmark **B8**, axe-core + manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass.

## Security notes
Drawings are user-authored content: `label` and note `text` are sanitised on write and rendered as plain text into the glyph atlas — never as HTML. All endpoints are owner-scoped (`owner_user_id = current user`); a Viewer role may read but not mutate. IDOR on `/drawings/{drawingId}` is an explicit abuse case in the STRIDE model for R1.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA. The canvas surrogate pattern of `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 applies: every drawing has an off-screen focusable DOM node with a composed accessible name ("Trendline, 2026-10-13 14:00 at 64,120 to 2026-10-13 18:00 at 65,400, locked"). Tool selection, creation, nudging, locking and deletion are all keyboard-reachable; magnet snap targets are announced; colour is never the only carrier of state (locked/hidden also carry an icon and text).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 R5 and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037: 200 drawings + 50 order/position lines hit-tested in ≤1 ms; drag at ≥58 fps with 200 drawings; drawings never decimated; drawing memory ≤8 MB; object tree virtualised for ≥500 objects; batch persistence debounced to one call per 500 ms of dragging.

## Observability
Analytics events per SCR-037: `drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`. Engine metrics: `engine_pick_duration_ms`, `engine_drawing_count`, `engine_drawing_layer_frame_ms`. API metrics: `http_request_duration_seconds{route="/drawings*"}`, `drawings_batch_size`, `drawings_conflict_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end-to-end on staging with the Owner present.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% engine + backend packages touched; no open P0/P1 bugs against DRAW scope.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-036/SCR-037 plus one manual NVDA and one VoiceOver pass recorded.
- [ ] Benchmark B8 recorded against budget and wired as a CI regression gate.
- [ ] STRIDE findings for user-authored content triaged and signed off by Security.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 updated to shipped behaviour.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review; QA epic-level regression pass recorded.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (engine core: scene graph, layers, interaction, worker protocol — `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 `E11 --> E14`), **E05** (design-system v0 tokens/primitives for the toolbar and popover), **E09** (auth/RBAC for owner-scoped persistence). Blocks: **E15** (layouts persist drawings), **E40** (line-cross alerts), **E30** (position tool → ticket).

## Branch
`feat/e14-drawing-tools`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW; `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.6; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223, CMP-224; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings*`; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3, §3.9, §3.10, §14 M7; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2, §11.1; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`; `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    K01[E14-K01 Spike: keyboard drawing + surrogate a11y] --> S01
    T01[E14-T01 drawings table + REST API] --> T02[E14-T02 Client DrawingStore, sync, undo/redo]
    T03[E14-T03 Engine drawings layer renderer] --> T04[E14-T04 Hit-test index, handles, multi-select]
    T02 --> S10[E14-S10 Toolbar SCR-037 + properties]
    T04 --> S10
    S10 --> S01[E14-S01 Horizontal/vertical line & ray]
    S01 --> S02[E14-S02 Trendline, ray, extended + magnet]
    S02 --> S03[E14-S03 Rectangle, ellipse, channel, triangle]
    S02 --> S04[E14-S04 Fibonacci retracement/extension/time-zone]
    S02 --> S05[E14-S05 Anchored VWAP + bands]
    S01 --> S06[E14-S06 Text, note, arrow annotations]
    S01 --> S08[E14-S08 Object tree, lock/hide, undo/redo UI]
    S03 --> S07[E14-S07 Long/short position tool]
    S08 --> S09[E14-S09 Templates & cross-pane sync]
```

## Agent guidance

How to pick up work in this epic when multiple agents are running in parallel:

**Dependency order.** Work tickets in `blocked_by` order; a ticket is not pickable until every key in its `blocked_by` list is Done. Design (`-D*`) and spike (`-K*`) tickets generally gate the technical (`-T*`) and story (`-S*`) tickets that consume their output — check each ticket's `blocked_by` field, do not assume numeric or alphabetic order implies dependency order.

**Parallel lanes.** Tickets with disjoint `component` values and no shared `blocked_by` edge can run concurrently. QA (`-Q*`) and security (`-X*`) tickets typically depend on the corresponding `-S*`/`-T*` ticket being Done, so they are the last lane per feature slice, not a separate epic-wide phase.

**Shared interfaces to agree first.** Before two agents touch the same contract (API/WS schema, DB table, or statechart) concurrently, the one opening the PR first must land the contract change (OpenAPI/WS schema/migration) and regenerate `packages/protocol`; the second agent rebases on it rather than proposing a second incompatible shape. Statechart JSON under `machines/` is single-owner per PR — check open PRs touching the same `machines/<name>.machine.json` before starting a `statechart`-labelled ticket.

title: Spike: keyboard-only drawing creation and canvas surrogate a11y pattern
body:
## Context
Every DRAW story carries a keyboard clause (US-DRAW-002 "Keyboard creation", US-DRAW-006 "Screen reader", US-DRAW-008 "navigable by keyboard"), and `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 makes a manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass on drawing flows an R1 quality gate. A WebGL canvas exposes nothing to assistive technology by itself, so the pattern used to mirror hundreds of drawings into the accessibility tree must be settled **before** nine stories each invent their own. `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 names the pattern ("canvas control surrogate") but leaves its application to drawings — a dynamic, unbounded, spatially-addressed object set — open.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A throwaway branch prototype on top of the E11 engine shell demonstrating: tool selection by hotkey (`Alt+T`/`Alt+H`/`Alt+F`/`Alt+R`/`Alt+M` per SCR-037), a keyboard crosshair that steps bar-by-bar and tick-by-tick, anchor confirmation with `Enter`, cancel with `Esc`, and nudge (arrow = 1 tick, Shift+arrow = 10 ticks).
- Measured comparison of **three** surrogate strategies for the accessibility tree: (a) one off-screen DOM node per drawing, (b) a single `application`-role live grid summarising drawings, (c) surrogates materialised only for the currently visible + selected set (virtualised).
- Numbers for each: DOM node count and AT-tree build time at 50 / 200 / 500 drawings, NVDA and VoiceOver announcement latency, and main-thread cost per frame while dragging.
- A written recommendation with the composed accessible-name grammar for each tool, plus the live-region policy (what is announced on create/snap/nudge/delete and at what politeness).
- Decision recorded as an ADR addendum or a section appended to `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1, and the keyboard map appended to `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037.

## Out of scope
- Production implementation of any tool (that is E14-S01…S09).
- Touch/pen input research — separate concern, engine §3.11.
- Voice control.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A recommendation exists and is measured, not asserted
  When the spike closes
  Then the ticket carries a table of DOM node count, AT-tree build time and drag frame cost for all three strategies at 50/200/500 drawings
  And exactly one strategy is recommended with the reason stated

Scenario: The keyboard path is demonstrated end to end
  Given the prototype and a keyboard only
  When a trendline is created, nudged and deleted
  Then no pointer event is recorded and each step is announced by NVDA

Scenario: The pattern degrades gracefully at scale
  Given 500 drawings under the recommended strategy
  Then AT-tree build time stays under 100 ms and drag frame cost stays under 2 ms on the main thread
  Or the strategy is rejected and the fallback documented

Scenario: Timebox is respected
  Given the 2-point timebox is exhausted without a clear winner
  Then the safest strategy (virtualised surrogates) is adopted by default and the residual risk is written on E14-S08
```

## Technical notes / design
Measure with the engine already under load (100k-bar series) so main-thread contention is realistic; screen-reader latency is measured with NVDA speech-viewer timestamps and VoiceOver's log. Virtualisation must reconcile with the engine's own culling: the visible set is already computed for rendering, so the surrogate list can subscribe to the same viewport event rather than recompute it.

## Test plan
Proto-level only: a Playwright keyboard-only script that asserts zero pointer events and the presence of expected `aria-label`s; manual NVDA (Windows) and VoiceOver (macOS) sessions recorded as video and attached.

## Security notes
Surrogate nodes echo user-authored labels and note text into the DOM — the prototype must already prove the sanitised, `textContent`-only path (never `innerHTML`) so the production stories inherit it.

## Accessibility notes
This spike *is* the accessibility work: outputs are the name grammar, the live-region politeness policy, the focus model (roving tabindex vs. single application node) and the keyboard map. WCAG 2.2 criteria in play: 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible, 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value.

## Performance notes
The recommended strategy must add ≤2 ms main-thread cost per frame while dragging and must not push the engine below the 58 fps drag target of SCR-037.

## Observability
None in production. Prototype instrumentation: `perf.mark` around surrogate reconciliation, reported in the spike write-up.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Timeboxed to 2 points; findings written on the ticket even if inconclusive.
- [ ] Comparison table, recommendation and accessible-name grammar published.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 updated with the chosen pattern and keyboard map.
- [ ] Prototype branch linked and explicitly marked throwaway (not merged to `main`).
- [ ] Reviewed by the accessibility lead and the chart-engine lead.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (engine shell with crosshair and viewport events). Blocks **E14-S01** and informs every other DRAW story.

## Branch
`spike/e14-keyboard-drawing-a11y`

## References
`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.11, §3.12; `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-002, US-DRAW-006, US-DRAW-008; `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4.


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries)
4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- packages/chart-engine/src/layers/drawings/**, apps/web/src/** (drawing toolbar/UI bindings), packages/ui/** (shared controls)
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- drawing tool plugin contract, hit-testing API, persistence schema for saved drawings; named identifiers in this ticket: SCR-037
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/chart-engine test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `spike/e14-keyboard-drawing-a11y`
- PR title: `E14-K01: Spike: keyboard-only drawing creation and canvas surrogate a11y pattern`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E14-K01)
- Required reviewers: `packages/chart-engine` (@CandleViewer/chart-engine) and `apps/web` (@CandleViewer/frontend), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/spike, area/charting-ui, priority/p1, a11y, ux-research

**Done means**
- [ ] Timeboxed to 2 points; findings written on the ticket even if inconclusive.
- [ ] Comparison table, recommendation and accessible-name grammar published.
- [ ] `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.1 and `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 updated with the chosen pattern and keyboard map.
- [ ] Prototype branch linked and explicitly marked throwaway (not merged to `main`).
- [ ] Reviewed by the accessibility lead and the chart-engine lead.

**Do NOT**
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E14-K01 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.

title: drawings table migration and owner-scoped /drawings REST endpoints
body:
## Context
Drawings are the first piece of per-user chart state that must survive a reload, a machine change and an interval change. US-DRAW-001 states the requirement plainly: "persistence is server-side per user and symbol". The schema is already specified — `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 `drawings`, shipped in migration `0011_workspace` — and the contract is already drafted in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`DrawingInput`, `Drawing`, and the four operations). This Task implements both, interface-first, so the client work (E14-T02) codes against a merged contract rather than a promise.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Alembic migration adding `drawings` exactly per §3.8.3: `id`, `owner_user_id` (FK → `users`, ON DELETE CASCADE), `symbol`, `tool`, `geometry` jsonb, `style` jsonb, `label`, `locked`, `visible`, `interval_scope`, `z_index`, `anchor_start`, `anchor_end`, `alert_id` (nullable, FK → `alerts` ON DELETE SET NULL — column only, unused until E40), timestamps, `deleted_at`; constraints `dr_tool` and `dr_geom`; indexes `ix_dr_user_symbol` and `ix_dr_range` (both partial on `deleted_at IS NULL`).
- Endpoints in the workspace router: `GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=&layout_id=`, `POST /api/v1/drawings`, `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`, `PUT /api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}`, `DELETE /api/v1/drawings/{drawingId}`.
- Server-side validation of `DrawingInput`: `tool` enum, ≥1 point for `text`/`hline`-family and ≥2 points for two-anchor tools (SCR-037 validation rule), `style` additionalProperties false, `label` ≤120 chars, colour pattern `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`.
- `anchor_start`/`anchor_end` denormalised from `geometry.points` on every write.
- Transactional batch: an ordered list of create/update/delete ops applied atomically, returning `{created, updated, deleted}`; batch size capped (default 200) with 413 beyond it.
- Soft delete (`deleted_at`) plus the 90-day purge job entry per `21-database-schema.md` retention table.
- Owner scoping and RBAC: every read and write filtered by `owner_user_id`; Viewer role read-only.
- Contract tests generated from the OpenAPI document; any drift fails CI.

## Out of scope
- Alert binding behaviour on `alert_id` (**E40**).
- Layout-scoped copy/duplication semantics beyond storing `layout_id` (**E15**).
- Any client code (**E14-T02**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Round-trip persistence per user and symbol
  Given user A creates a trendline on BTCUSDT
  When GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=BTCUSDT is called as user A
  Then the drawing is returned with identical geometry decimals and its id, created_at and updated_at

Scenario: Cross-user access is denied, not merely filtered
  Given user B knows the drawingId created by user A
  When user B calls PUT or DELETE on it
  Then the API responds 404 (not 403, to avoid confirming existence) and the row is unchanged

Scenario: Malformed geometry is rejected
  When a client posts tool=trendline with a single point, or tool="scribble"
  Then the API responds 422 with a field-level error and nothing is persisted

Scenario: Batch is atomic
  Given a batch of 3 creates and 1 update where the update targets a deleted drawing
  When POST /api/v1/drawings/batch is called
  Then the whole batch fails with 409 and none of the 3 creates are visible

Scenario: Deletes are soft and recoverable within retention
  When a drawing is deleted
  Then deleted_at is set, it is absent from GET, and the row still exists until the 90-day purge job removes it

Scenario: Query uses the intended index
  Given 50 000 drawings across users
  When the per-chart load query runs
  Then EXPLAIN shows ix_dr_user_symbol and p99 latency is < 5 ms (query 28 of §query budgets)
```

## Technical notes / design
Prices are `Decimal` end to end — serialised as strings in JSON to avoid float drift on a 0.1-tick instrument. `geometry` is validated by a Pydantic model per tool (a discriminated union on `tool`) before it reaches JSONB, so the CHECK constraint is a backstop rather than the primary defence. The batch endpoint exists because the client collapses a whole drag into one call with a 500 ms debounce (`22-api-openapi.yaml` description); it is therefore latency-sensitive but low-QPS. Concurrent edits use `updated_at` as an optimistic token: a mismatched token returns 409 so the client can re-read rather than silently clobber.

## Test plan
Unit: per-tool geometry validators, anchor denormalisation, decimal serialisation. Contract: schemathesis against the four operations, including negative cases. Integration: Postgres-backed round-trip, atomic batch rollback, soft-delete visibility, purge job. Security: IDOR matrix (owner/other/viewer × read/write/delete). Perf: seeded 50k-row EXPLAIN + latency assertion.

## Security notes
Stored user content: `label`, `geometry.text` and `style.label` are length-capped and stripped of control characters on write; they are never interpolated into HTML anywhere server-side. IDOR is the primary threat (STRIDE: Tampering/Information disclosure) and is covered by an explicit test matrix. RBAC follows E09: Owner/Manager may mutate their own drawings; Viewer is read-only. No secrets or PII touched; data classification: user content, non-sensitive.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — no UI surface. The API returns `label` and `tool` so the client can compose accessible names without extra round-trips.

## Performance notes
Per-chart load < 5 ms p99 (query 28). Batch of 200 ops < 50 ms p99. Config-table growth is bounded by human editing rate (< 100 MB total per `21-database-schema.md` §sizing).

## Observability
`http_request_duration_seconds{route="/api/v1/drawings*"}`, `drawings_batch_size` histogram, `drawings_conflict_total`, `drawings_rows_total{tool}` gauge, `drawings_purged_total`. Structured logs carry `user_id`, `symbol`, `op_count` — never geometry or label content.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the workspace/drawings router and repository.
- [ ] Migration applies and rolls back cleanly on a seeded database; `0011_workspace` documented.
- [ ] `22-api-openapi.yaml` merged and contract tests green; deliberate drift fails CI.
- [ ] Security review comment present; IDOR matrix executed.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

`blocked_by`: **E09** (users table, sessions, RBAC roles). Blocks **E14-T02**, **E14-S01**.

title: Engine drawings layer: instanced thick lines, dashes, fills and SDF labels
body:
## Context
SCR-037's performance clause is explicit: "Drawings render on a separate canvas layer above the price layer; dragging a drawing must not re-render the price/footprint layers (target: drag at >=58 fps with 200 drawings on the chart)." `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.3 already reserves **layer: drawings** in the scene stack and §3.10 specifies the rendering technique: "lines as instanced quads with a geometry-shader-free thick-line expansion done in the vertex shader (per-instance `p0`, `p1`, `width`, dash pattern index); dashes via a distance-along-line varying and a pattern LUT." This Task builds that layer as a primitive renderer — geometry in, pixels out — with no tool semantics, so all nine tool stories share one code path and one set of golden images.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/chart-engine/src/layers/drawings/` renderer producing three primitive batches: **lines** (instanced quads, thick-line vertex expansion, per-instance colour/width/dash index), **quads/fills** (rect, ellipse, channel band, fib level band; per-instance fill colour + opacity), **labels** (SDF glyphs from the shared atlas, ≤3 text draw calls per pane).
- Dash pattern LUT (solid/dashed/dotted per `DrawingInput.style.dash`) driven by a distance-along-line varying so dashes stay uniform under zoom.
- Ellipse and rounded-cap rendering via signed-distance fragment evaluation rather than tessellation.
- Chart-space → screen-space transform applied per frame from the viewport, so anchors are re-projected rather than re-uploaded on pan/zoom; a dirty-flag protocol so only the drawings layer redraws on a drag.
- `degraded-2d` fallback path (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §render profiles): Canvas 2D lines, fills and labels with identical geometry semantics.
- Worker command `addDrawing` / `setDrawings(snapshot)` and event `drawingChanged` wired per §3.13 protocol.
- Benchmark **B8** harness entry: 200 drawings, drag one, assert frame ≤12 ms.
- Golden images per primitive per theme (light/dark) against SwiftShader, ≤0.1 % pixel diff.

## Out of scope
- Hit-testing, grab handles, selection visuals — **E14-T04**.
- Any specific tool's semantics (fib levels, VWAP maths, position tool R:R) — the tool stories.
- Persistence and store wiring — **E14-T02**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Dragging a drawing does not touch the price layer
  Given a chart with 100k bars and 200 drawings
  When one drawing's geometry changes every frame for 3 seconds
  Then only the drawings layer is redrawn, the price and footprint layers report zero redraws, and the frame time stays ≤12 ms (benchmark B8)

Scenario: Thick lines and dashes survive zoom
  Given a 4 px dashed trendline
  When the viewport is zoomed 100x in and 100x out
  Then the stroke stays 4 CSS px at any DPI and dash spacing stays visually uniform along the line

Scenario: Text budget is respected
  Given 200 drawings each carrying a label
  Then the layer issues at most 3 text draw calls per pane per frame

Scenario: WebGL2 unavailable
  Given RenderProfile = degraded-2d
  Then lines, fills and labels still render with the same geometry and a visible capability notice, rather than a blank layer

Scenario: Golden images are deterministic
  When the golden-image suite runs twice on SwiftShader
  Then both runs match the committed references within 0.1 % pixel difference
```

## Technical notes / design
Instance buffers are double-buffered and re-uploaded only when the drawing set or its style changes; viewport changes are handled entirely in the vertex shader by re-projecting `p0`/`p1` from chart space, which keeps pan/zoom allocation-free. Fill opacity composites below the price layer's candle bodies is impossible (the layer is above), so US-DRAW-003's legibility clause is met by premultiplied alpha plus a "flatten opacity" uniform the story can drive. Ellipses and caps use fragment SDFs so there is no tessellation cost at any zoom. Drawing memory stays inside the ≤8 MB bucket shared with profile/indicator geometry (§3.16).

## Test plan
Unit: thick-line expansion maths, dash LUT sampling, chart↔screen projection round-trip. Property-based: for random viewports, projected stroke width in CSS px is invariant. Golden image: each primitive × each theme × WebGL2 and degraded-2d. Perf: benchmark B8 in CI with a regression gate >10 % failing the build.

## Security notes
Label strings come from user content; they are rasterised through the SDF atlas as text only. The atlas must cap glyph count per drawing (label ≤120 chars per the API) so a pathological label cannot exhaust atlas space and degrade other layers — a denial-of-service consideration on the render path.

## Accessibility notes
No DOM surface here, but the layer must expose per-drawing screen-space bounds to the main thread so E14-T04 and the surrogate nodes from E14-K01 can be positioned and focus rings drawn at the right place. Contrast of default stroke/fill tokens against both themes is verified in the golden images.

## Performance notes
Budget: 200 drawings + 50 order/position lines within the R5 overlay budget of `26-chart-engine-design.md` §2; drag frame ≤12 ms (B8); ≤3 text draw calls per pane; drawings never decimated; layer memory ≤8 MB.

## Observability
`engine_drawing_layer_frame_ms` histogram, `engine_drawing_count` gauge, `engine_drawing_instance_uploads_total`, `engine_text_draw_calls` — surfaced through the engine's existing stats channel and the debug overlay.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the drawings layer package.
- [ ] B8 benchmark recorded with before/after numbers and wired as a required check.
- [ ] Golden images committed for both themes and both render profiles.
- [ ] `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 updated if the shipped technique differs.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC (split renderer/shader/bench if needed), merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Branch
`feat/e14-engine-drawings-layer`

title: Hit-test index, grab handles, multi-select and group transform
body:
## Context
Selecting, dragging and resizing is what separates a drawing *renderer* from drawing *tools*. `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.9 specifies the mechanism precisely: "an **object index** — a uniform grid (64 px buckets) over drawings, order lines, position lines, alert lines and bubbles, storing object ids per bucket. Picking queries the bucket under the cursor plus a 1-bucket ring, then tests candidates precisely (distance-to-segment for lines, rect containment for boxes, radius for bubbles), sorted by `zIndex` then proximity", with a **picking budget ≤1 ms for 200 drawings + 50 lines**, edge-triggered result posting, 10 px grab-handle tolerance and 16 px for touch. This Task delivers that index plus the selection/manipulation model every tool story builds on.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Uniform 64 px bucket grid over the drawings layer, rebuilt incrementally on geometry change and re-bucketed on viewport change (buckets are screen-space).
- `pickAt(x, y)` worker command returning the topmost candidate by `zIndex` then proximity, with per-object part identification (body vs. handle index) so a drag knows whether it is moving or resizing.
- Grab handles: one per anchor plus a body-drag region; hit tolerance 10 px pointer / 16 px touch; handles rendered by the T03 primitives at ≥24 px visual target per US-DRAW-001 NFR.
- Edge-triggered hover/selection events to the main thread (post only when the picked object changes), driving cursor changes and the hover highlight.
- Multi-select: additive click (Ctrl/Cmd), rubber-band marquee, `Select all` ; group move and group delete applying one command to N objects.
- Shift-constrained angles during creation/drag (0/45/90°) and axis-locked body drags.
- `locked` objects are pickable for inspection and selection but reject geometry mutation (US-DRAW-008 scenario "Lock and hide all"); `visible=false` objects are excluded from picking.
- Screen-space bounds and focus-ring geometry published per object for the accessibility surrogates chosen in E14-K01.

## Out of scope
- Persistence of selection or of the resulting geometry (**E14-T02**).
- Undo/redo command stack semantics (**E14-T02**); this Task emits the intent, not the history.
- Magnet/snap-to-OHLC (**E14-S02**, which layers snapping on top of the drag pipeline).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Picking stays inside budget
  Given 200 drawings and 50 order/position lines on screen
  When pickAt is called at 120 Hz for 5 seconds
  Then p99 pick duration is ≤1 ms and no frame exceeds the 16.6 ms budget

Scenario: Topmost object wins deterministically
  Given three overlapping drawings with z_index 0, 1 and 2 under the cursor
  When the user clicks
  Then the z_index 2 object is selected, and with equal z_index the nearest by distance wins

Scenario: Locked objects resist mutation but allow inspection
  Given a locked rectangle
  When the user drags its body and then its corner handle
  Then its geometry is unchanged, it can still be selected and its properties inspected, and a non-blocking hint explains it is locked

Scenario: Multi-select group move is one operation
  Given five drawings selected by marquee
  When the group is dragged by 100 px
  Then all five move by the identical chart-space delta and a single change event is emitted covering all five

Scenario: Hidden objects are not pickable
  Given a drawing with visible=false
  When the cursor passes over its former location
  Then nothing is hovered and the cursor does not change

Scenario: Touch tolerance differs from pointer
  Given a coarse-pointer device
  Then handle hit tolerance is 16 px rather than 10 px and handles remain ≥24 px in visual size
```

## Technical notes / design
The index lives in the worker next to the geometry it indexes, so picking never crosses the thread boundary per pointer move; the main thread sends pointer positions and receives only change events. Bucket rebuild on viewport change is O(objects) but bounded (drawings are never decimated because their count is bounded), and is amortised by rebuilding only when the projection changes by more than one bucket. Precise tests: distance-to-segment (lines, rays, channel edges), point-in-rect (boxes, text), point-in-ellipse, distance-to-level-line (fib). Rays and extended lines are clipped to the viewport before testing so an off-screen infinite extension costs nothing.

## Test plan
Unit: each precise test, z-order resolution, tolerance by pointer type, locked/hidden rules. Property-based: for random object sets and cursor positions, grid picking returns the same object as a brute-force scan. Perf: pick benchmark at 200+50 objects asserted in CI. E2E: Playwright select/marquee/group-move/locked-drag.

## Security notes
No new data surface. Picking must be bounded work per pointer event so a pathological drawing set (e.g. thousands of degenerate zero-length segments in one bucket) cannot stall the worker — a per-bucket candidate cap with a documented fallback is required (availability threat).

## Accessibility notes
Selection is not mouse-only: the same selection model is driven by keyboard focus traversal (Tab/arrow through the object set per E14-K01) and must raise identical events. Focus rings use the screen-space bounds published here, honour 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, and handles meet the 24×24 CSS px target size of WCAG 2.5.8.

## Performance notes
Pick ≤1 ms p99 for 200 drawings + 50 lines (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §2 R5 / §3.9); zero allocations on the hover path; events posted only on change.

## Observability
`engine_pick_duration_ms` histogram, `engine_pick_candidates` histogram, `engine_index_rebuild_total`, `engine_selection_size` gauge; visible in the engine debug overlay.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the picking/selection modules.
- [ ] Pick benchmark recorded and wired as a CI regression gate.
- [ ] Keyboard selection parity demonstrated (same events, no pointer dependency).
- [ ] `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.9 updated if tolerances or structure changed.

title: Client DrawingStore: optimistic sync, debounced batch writes and undo/redo stack
body:
## Context
`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6 names `DrawingStore` as a first-class store, and §3.10 sets its behaviour: "optimistic local writes with server reconciliation" and "undo/redo is a command stack of 100 entries, shared with the drawing toolbar". US-DRAW-008 raises the floor further — "undo stack ≥50 operations per symbol, session-scoped" — and US-DRAW-001 requires that a deletion is "removed from all panes showing that symbol and the action is undoable". This Task is the single source of truth between the REST API (E14-T01) and the engine layer (E14-T03), so no tool story has to re-solve sync, history or fan-out to panes.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `apps/web/src/features/drawings/store/` holding drawings keyed by `(symbol)` with derived per-pane views; a pane subscribes by symbol and receives every drawing for that symbol (the mechanism behind US-DRAW-001's "every BTCUSDT chart" and US-DRAW-009's cross-pane sync).
- Command model: every mutation is a reversible command (`create`, `update-geometry`, `update-style`, `delete`, `lock`, `hide`, `group-move`, `clone`) carrying before/after state; a 100-entry stack per symbol, session-scoped, with `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` bindings registered through the app hotkey service.
- Optimistic application: local state and the engine snapshot update on the same frame as the interaction; the network write follows.
- Debounced persistence: mutations coalesce for 500 ms (and flush immediately on pointer-up, tool change, pane close or `beforeunload`) into one `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`.
- Reconciliation: server ids replace optimistic ids; a 409 conflict triggers a re-read of the symbol's drawings and a non-destructive merge (server wins for the conflicting object, local history stays intact); an offline/5xx write is retried with jittered backoff and surfaced as a "changes not saved" chip.
- Initial load on chart mount via `GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=`, with in-memory caching so a second pane on the same symbol issues no second request.
- Engine bridge: publishes an immutable drawing snapshot to the worker per frame and consumes `drawingChanged` / selection events back.

## Out of scope
- Server-side schema and endpoints (**E14-T01**).
- Toolbar and properties UI (**E14-S10**); the object-tree UI (**E14-S08**).
- Per-layout scoping rules and sync toggles (**E14-S09** consumes this store's `layout_id` support).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A drag persists as exactly one request
  Given a trendline is dragged continuously for 3 seconds and released
  When network traffic is inspected
  Then at most one /drawings/batch request per 500 ms of dragging is sent, and a final flush occurs on release

Scenario: Undo restores every property
  Given a styled, labelled rectangle is deleted
  When Ctrl+Z is pressed
  Then it is restored with identical geometry, style, label, lock and visibility, and Ctrl+Shift+Z deletes it again

Scenario: Optimistic write survives a failed save
  Given the API returns 500 for a batch
  Then the drawing remains visible locally, a "changes not saved" chip appears, the write is retried with backoff, and the chip clears on success

Scenario: Conflict does not destroy local history
  Given the server returns 409 because the drawing changed elsewhere
  Then the store re-reads the symbol, adopts the server version of that object, keeps the undo stack usable, and informs the user once

Scenario: Two panes on one symbol stay identical
  Given two panes show BTCUSDT at 1m and 1h
  When a horizontal line is created in the 1m pane
  Then it appears in the 1h pane in the same frame and only one network request is made

Scenario: Stack is bounded and scoped
  Given 150 mutations are performed on BTCUSDT
  Then the undo stack holds the most recent 100 and switching to ETHUSDT presents that symbol's own independent stack
```

## Technical notes / design
State is immutable (structural sharing) so the per-frame worker snapshot is a reference comparison rather than a deep copy — this is what keeps the engine bridge inside the drag frame budget. Optimistic ids are client-generated UUIDv7 so ordering is stable and the server can accept them directly, making reconciliation an id-confirmation rather than an id-swap in the common case. The debounce holds a *coalescing map* keyed by drawing id (last write wins per object), not a queue of every intermediate frame, so a 3-second drag produces one update op, not 180. Prices are carried as strings/`Decimal` end to end; no float arithmetic touches an anchor.

## Test plan
Unit: command invert/apply, stack bounds and scoping, coalescing map, debounce/flush triggers, reconciliation paths (200/409/500/offline). Integration: store + mock server with fake timers proving request counts. E2E: Playwright two-pane sync, undo/redo after reload, offline save chip. Contract: store's request bodies validated against `DrawingInput`.

## Security notes
The store must not persist drawing content to `localStorage` in plaintext beyond the session cache policy agreed for chart state; note text is user content and is escaped at every render boundary. Retries must not replay a delete after a successful re-create (idempotency by op id) — a data-integrity rather than confidentiality concern.

## Accessibility notes
Undo/redo must announce their effect in a polite live region ("Trendline restored", "Delete redone") since the visual change occurs on a canvas that screen readers cannot observe. Hotkeys are registered through the shared hotkey service so they appear in the keyboard-shortcuts help (SCR settings) and can be remapped.

## Performance notes
Store update + worker snapshot publish ≤1 ms on the main thread per interaction frame; at most one network request per 500 ms of dragging; memory bounded by 500 drawings/symbol × 100 undo entries with before/after snapshots held by structural sharing rather than copies.

## Observability
Analytics `drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted` (SCR-037). Client metrics: `drawings_batch_requests_total`, `drawings_batch_retry_total`, `drawings_conflict_total`, `drawings_undo_total`, `drawings_store_apply_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the drawings feature package.
- [ ] Request-count assertions in CI (no chatty-drag regression).
- [ ] Hotkeys registered in the shared service and documented in the shortcuts screen.
- [ ] PR ≤400 LOC, merge queue, 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-T01** (endpoints and schema), **E14-T03** (engine layer and snapshot protocol). Blocks **E14-S10** and every tool story.

## Branch
`feat/e14-drawing-store`

title: Drawing toolbar and properties popover (SCR-037)
body:
## Context
Every DRAW story needs the same chrome: a tool rail to pick a tool, and a properties popover to style what was drawn. **SCR-037** specifies both — the left rail listing cursor/crosshair/trendline/ray/extended/h-line/v-line/rect/ellipse/triangle/fib/pitchfork/VWAP/measure/position/text/arrow/brush plus magnet, lock-all, hide-all and delete-all; and the popover with colour, width, style, extend, magnet and "save as default". Building it once, first, means the nine tool stories add a tool entry and a property schema rather than a UI.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-223 DrawingToolbar** as the left rail of the chart, grouped by tool family, with an overflow menu (CMP-041) for rarely-used tools and a persistent "keep tool active" toggle for repeated drawing.
- Properties popover (CMP-017) bound to the current selection: colour (CMP-031 ColorSwatch, design-token palette), width (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput, 1–8), dash (solid/dashed/dotted), fill colour and fill opacity (CMP-010 Slider) for fill-capable tools, label text, font size, extend-left/extend-right, magnet toggle, lock, visibility, `Save as default`, `Delete`.
- Multi-selection editing: when N drawings are selected, shared properties are editable and mixed values render as an indeterminate state.
- Global toolbar actions wired to store commands: magnet toggle (`Ctrl+M`), lock-all, hide-all, delete-all (with confirmation), and the disabled "alert when price crosses" affordance reserved for E40 with a "coming in a later release" tooltip.
- Hotkeys per SCR-037: `Alt+T` trendline, `Alt+H` horizontal, `Alt+F` fib, `Alt+R` rect, `Alt+M` measure, `Esc` cancel in-progress drawing / clear selection.
- A per-tool registry (`id`, icon, hotkey, anchor count, property schema, default style) that later stories extend — the single extension point for the whole Epic.
- States: no selection (rail only), single selection, multi-selection, locked selection (properties read-only with an unlock action), tool armed (cursor and rail state change).

## Out of scope
- The tools themselves — each is its own Story (S01–S09).
- The object tree (**E14-S08**) and templates (**E14-S09**).
- Alert creation from the popover (**E40**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Arm a tool and draw
  Given the chart has focus
  When the trader presses Alt+T
  Then the trendline tool is armed, the rail shows it as active, the cursor changes, and the status region announces "Trendline tool active"

Scenario: Style a selection
  Given a trendline is selected
  When colour is changed to a token swatch and width to 4 in the popover
  Then the change is visible within one frame and persisted after the 500 ms debounce

Scenario: Mixed multi-selection
  Given a 2 px red line and a 4 px blue line are both selected
  Then width and colour render as indeterminate, and setting width to 3 applies to both while colour stays untouched

Scenario: Locked selection is read-only
  Given a locked drawing is selected
  Then style fields are disabled with an explanatory hint and only "Unlock" is actionable

Scenario: Cancel an in-progress drawing
  Given the first anchor of a rectangle has been placed
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the in-progress drawing is discarded, nothing is persisted, and the tool returns to cursor unless "keep tool active" is on

Scenario: Delete-all is not a one-click accident
  When delete-all is chosen
  Then a confirmation states how many drawings on which symbol will be removed, and the action is undoable as one command
```

## Technical notes / design
The tool registry is a plain data structure consumed by both the rail and the popover, so a new tool is a registry entry plus an engine geometry handler; nothing in the chrome is tool-aware. The popover is anchored to the selection's screen-space bounds published by E14-T04 and repositions on pan/zoom, clamping to the viewport. All styling values come from design-system v0 tokens (E05) — no raw hex in code; the colour swatch offers the token palette plus a custom picker that still writes a `#rrggbb` value matching the API pattern.

## Test plan
Unit: registry resolution, indeterminate-value logic, hotkey dispatch, Esc semantics. Component tests for the popover states (none/single/multi/locked). E2E Playwright: arm→draw→style→persist→reload. a11y: axe-core on SCR-037; keyboard-only traversal of rail and popover; screen-reader announcement of tool arming. design-qa: built screen compared to the signed-off SCR-037 spec.

## Security notes
The label field is user content: length-capped at 120 chars client-side to match the API, rendered as text only, and never passed to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. The delete-all action is destructive and therefore confirmed and undoable, and is scoped to the current user's own drawings only.

## Accessibility notes
The rail is a toolbar (`role="toolbar"`, roving tabindex, arrow-key traversal) with each tool a toggle button exposing pressed state and its hotkey via CMP-022 Kbd in the accessible description. The popover is a standard form (SCR-037 a11y note) with labelled fields, focus trapped while open, `Esc` to close and focus returned to the trigger. Tool arming and cancellation are announced politely. All targets ≥24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8); state is never colour-only.

## Performance notes
Arming a tool or opening the popover must not trigger an engine re-render of the price layer. Popover repositioning during pan is throttled to animation frames. The rail renders once and is memoised; property edits push straight to the store's coalescing map.

## Observability
`drawing.tool_armed{tool}`, `drawing.style_changed{property}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}`, `drawing.delete_all` analytics events; client metric `drawings_popover_open_ms`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by automated tests referenced by name.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% on the toolbar/popover package.
- [ ] SCR-037 design ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints prior (design-ahead rule) and design-qa comparison recorded.

title: Horizontal line, horizontal ray and vertical line with server persistence
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-001 — Horizontal line and ray (Must)**: "As a trader, I want persisted horizontal levels per symbol, so that my key levels are there every session." This is the simplest tool and therefore the one that proves the whole pipeline end to end — registry entry, engine geometry, hit-test, store, batch persistence, keyboard path — before the harder geometries arrive. The vertical line (`vline` in the `drawings.tool` enum, `vertical_line` in the API enum) ships alongside it because it is the same single-anchor problem on the other axis.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `horizontal_line`, `ray` (horizontal ray variant) and `vertical_line` registered in the E14-S10 tool registry with hotkey `Alt+H` for horizontal.
- Single-click creation at the crosshair; a horizontal line spans the full pane width, a horizontal ray extends right only from its anchor, a vertical line spans full pane height at a timestamp.
- Always-visible price label on the price axis for horizontal tools (live during drag) and a time label on the time axis for vertical lines.
- Drag to move (body or handle), with the price label updating live and the value saved on pointer-up per the US scenario "Edit".
- Delete via `Del`/`Backspace` on selection, removed from **all panes showing that symbol**, undoable.
- Keyboard: create at the focused crosshair price with `Enter`; nudge 1 tick with arrow keys, 10 ticks with `Shift+arrow` (US-DRAW-001 NFR); values snapped to the symbol's tick size.
- Persistence through the store to `/api/v1/drawings` with `tool` and `geometry.points = [{t, p}]`; `interval_scope` left NULL (all intervals).
- Grab handles ≥24 px per the NFR.

## Out of scope
- Line-cross alerts on the level (**E40**).
- Two-anchor trendlines and magnet snapping (**E14-S02**).
- Styling templates (**E14-S09**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw and persist
  When I draw a horizontal line on BTCUSDT and reload the app
  Then the line is still there at the same price on every BTCUSDT chart

Scenario: Edit
  When I drag the line
  Then the price label updates live and the new value is saved on release

Scenario: Delete
  When I select it and press Delete
  Then it is removed from all panes showing that symbol and the action is undoable

Scenario: Keyboard nudge respects tick size
  Given a horizontal line at 64,120.5 on a 0.1-tick symbol and keyboard focus on it
  When I press ArrowUp then Shift+ArrowUp
  Then the price becomes 64,120.6 then 64,121.6, each announced, and the final value is persisted

Scenario: Interval and scale changes do not move it
  Given a horizontal line on a 1m linear chart
  When I switch to 1h and to log scale
  Then the line renders at the identical price

Scenario: Save fails
  Given the API is unavailable when the drag is released
  Then the line stays at the new price locally, a "changes not saved" chip appears, and the value is persisted when connectivity returns
```

## Technical notes / design
A horizontal line is a one-point drawing whose `t` is recorded (for the ray variant's origin and for range queries) but whose rendering ignores `t` for the full-width case; `geometry.extend_left/extend_right` distinguishes line from ray, matching `DrawingInput`. Price values are `Decimal` and quantised to the instrument's `tick_size` from the symbol metadata on every mutation, so a drag can never persist an untradeable price. The axis label reuses the crosshair label primitive from E11 so its styling and contrast are already solved.

## Test plan
Unit: tick quantisation, ray vs line geometry, nudge maths. Golden image: line, ray and vertical line in both themes, selected and locked. E2E Playwright: draw → reload → assert price; drag → release → one batch request; delete → undo; keyboard create/nudge/delete with zero pointer events. Contract: persisted payload validates against `DrawingInput`. a11y: axe-core + accessible-name assertion.

## Security notes
No new server surface beyond E14-T01. The optional label is user content, length-capped and rendered as text. Persisted prices are validated server-side as decimals; a crafted payload with a non-numeric price is rejected 422 rather than stored.

## Accessibility notes
Each line exposes a surrogate node per E14-K01 named e.g. "Horizontal line at 64,120.5, unlocked". Creation, nudge and delete are fully keyboard-driven and announced politely. The price label meets 4.5:1 contrast against both themes; the level is distinguishable from indicator lines by more than colour (label text + focus ring).

## Performance notes
Single-anchor tools are the densest in practice (traders keep dozens of levels); creation, drag and delete must each stay within the drawings-layer frame budget with 200 objects present, and picking is unchanged at ≤1 ms.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool}`, `drawing.edited{tool}`, `drawing.deleted{tool}` analytics; the "changes not saved" chip increments `drawings_batch_retry_total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard-only path verified; screen-reader spot-check recorded.
- [ ] design-qa comparison against SCR-037 recorded.
- [ ] Golden images committed; QA black-box plan executed; demoed.
- [ ] Feature flag state recorded.

title: Trendline, ray and extended line with magnet-to-OHLC snapping
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-002 — Trendline (Must), ray (Should), extended line (Could)**. This is the first two-anchor tool and it introduces **magnet mode**, the snapping behaviour the roadmap calls out explicitly in the E14 scope line ("magnet-to-OHLC") and which every later two-anchor tool inherits. The story's NFR is the Epic's core invariant: "anchors stored as (timestamp, price), never pixels; log/linear scale changes must not move them."

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `trendline`, `ray`, `extended_line` in the registry (`Alt+T` for trendline), sharing one two-anchor placement pipeline: click first anchor → rubber-band preview → click second anchor → selected with both handles live.
- `geometry.extend_left` / `extend_right` distinguishing segment, ray and extended line; extended geometry clipped to the viewport before rendering and hit-testing.
- **Magnet mode** (`Ctrl+M`, also a toolbar toggle): during placement and drag, anchors snap to the nearest OHLC value of the bar under the cursor within a configurable snap radius (default 12 px), and the snap target is **highlighted** with a marker plus a textual announcement of which value was hit (open/high/low/close).
- Shift-constrained angles (0/45/90°) while placing or dragging an anchor.
- Anchors stored as `{t, p}` with `barIndex` derived, never stored; re-projection on interval change, bar-type change and log/linear flips leaves them invariant (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10 "time is authoritative across bar-spec changes").
- Live readout during placement: price delta, % change, bar count and elapsed time between anchors.
- Keyboard creation mode: step the crosshair bar-by-bar/tick-by-tick, `Enter` to place each anchor, `Esc` to cancel — per the US scenario "Keyboard creation".

## Out of scope
- Parallel channels (**E14-S03**) and pitchfork (descoped to R2 per `30-release-roadmap.md` §11 descoping ladder row 3 unless capacity allows).
- Fibonacci geometry (**E14-S04**).
- Snap-to-indicator-value or snap-to-drawing — not in R1.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Two-point draw
  When I click a start and end point
  Then the line is created, anchored to bar timestamps and prices, and stays correct through zoom and scale changes

Scenario: Magnet snap
  Given magnet mode is on
  Then anchors snap to the nearest OHLC value within the snap radius and the snap target is highlighted

Scenario: Keyboard creation
  When I use the keyboard drawing mode
  Then I can place both anchors by stepping the crosshair and confirming with Enter

Scenario: Anchors survive a bar-type change
  Given a trendline placed on 1m time bars
  When the chart switches to 500-tick bars and then to range bars
  Then both anchors resolve to the same timestamps and prices, within one tick, and the line is re-projected rather than re-anchored

Scenario: Extended line off-screen costs nothing
  Given an extended line whose projection leaves the viewport
  When the chart is panned far from it
  Then it is clipped before rasterisation and hit-testing, and pick duration is unchanged

Scenario: Degenerate placement is rejected
  Given both anchors land on the same pixel
  Then no drawing is persisted and the tool returns to placement state with a hint
```

## Technical notes / design
Snapping runs in the worker where the bar data already lives: the candidate set is the OHLC of the bar under the cursor plus its immediate neighbours, so the snap test is O(1) per pointer move and adds nothing measurable to the drag budget. The snap decision is recorded in the drawing's style metadata only for the highlight; the persisted anchor is the snapped `{t, p}` itself, so reopening the chart on another device reproduces the same line without re-snapping. Re-projection on bar-spec change uses the time axis's binary search from timestamp to position — the `screenToIndex(indexToScreen(i)) === i` property from §15 covers the identity requirement.

## Test plan
Unit: two-anchor placement state machine, extend flags, snap candidate selection, angle constraint maths. Property-based: for random viewports, bar specs and scale modes, anchor (t, p) is invariant — the explicit "drawing anchors are stable across bar-spec changes" property in `26-chart-engine-design.md` §15. Golden image: segment/ray/extended, selected and hovered, both themes. E2E: mouse placement, magnet snap with highlight assertion, keyboard placement with zero pointer events, scale-flip invariance. Perf: drag with 200 drawings sustains ≥58 fps.

## Security notes
No new server surface. Snap radius and angle constraints are client-side conveniences; server-side validation still enforces the two-point minimum, so a client cannot persist a one-anchor trendline.

## Accessibility notes
Keyboard creation is a first-class path, not a fallback: entering it announces the mode and the current crosshair position; each anchor placement announces price and time; magnet snaps announce the matched value ("snapped to high 65,400"). The completed line's surrogate name composes both anchors. Snap highlight is shape + text, never colour alone.

## Performance notes
Snap test O(1) per pointer move; placement preview redraws only the drawings layer; extended lines clipped before rasterisation; drag at ≥58 fps with 200 drawings (SCR-037) and pick ≤1 ms (engine §3.9).

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=trendline|ray|extended_line}`, `drawing.magnet_toggled`, `drawing.snap_applied{ohlc_field}` analytics; `engine_snap_duration_ms` metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Anchor-invariance property test green over ≥10k generated cases.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% engine on touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard creation verified with a screen reader.
- [ ] Perf benchmark recorded; design-qa and QA sign-offs; demoed.

title: Rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel and triangle zone tools
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-003 — Rectangle (Must), parallel channel (Should), triangle (Could)**, plus `ellipse` from the roadmap's E14 scope line. These are the first *filled* tools, which introduces the legibility problem the story names directly: fills must not make the candles under them unreadable. The NFR is explicit — "fills must respect the minimum contrast of candles drawn over them" — and the story requires a "flatten opacity" toggle for stacked zones.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `rectangle` (`Alt+R`), `ellipse`, `parallel_channel`, `triangle` in the registry, reusing the two-anchor pipeline; the channel adds a **third** drag that sets the band width, and the triangle a third anchor.
- Fill rendering with configurable `fill_colour` + `fill_opacity` (default token, default 0.15) and an independent border colour/width/dash, per `DrawingInput.style`.
- **Flatten opacity** global toggle in the toolbar: when on, overlapping fills composite to a single capped alpha instead of accumulating, so N stacked zones stay legible.
- Tooltip/readout reporting the rectangle's **price height** (absolute and %) and **bar width** (bars and elapsed time), per the US scenario.
- Parallel channel: both edges provably parallel in chart space (not screen space) so they stay parallel across log/linear flips and zoom; the median line is optional.
- Resize from any corner/edge handle; body drag moves the whole shape; Shift constrains to a square/circle or to the channel's angle.
- Keyboard creation: place anchors by stepping the crosshair; resize by focusing a handle and nudging.

## Out of scope
- Pitchfork (R2 per the descoping ladder) and Gann fan.
- Zone-entry alerts (**E40**).
- Auto-detected supply/demand zones — not a drawing tool.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Rectangle zone
  When I draw a rectangle over a consolidation
  Then it renders with configurable fill opacity and border, and reports its price height and bar width in the tooltip

Scenario: Channel
  When I draw a parallel channel
  Then the third drag sets the width, and both edges stay parallel through scale changes

Scenario: Overlap legibility
  Given multiple overlapping zones
  Then fills blend without making price candles unreadable, and a "flatten opacity" toggle exists

Scenario: Channel parallelism survives a log flip
  Given a parallel channel on a linear scale
  When the chart switches to logarithmic
  Then both edges remain parallel in chart space and the band width in price terms is preserved at each anchor

Scenario: Zero-area shape is rejected
  Given a rectangle dragged to zero width or zero height
  Then it is not persisted and the tool returns to placement state with a hint

Scenario: Resize by keyboard
  Given a rectangle is selected and a corner handle is focused
  When arrow keys are pressed
  Then that corner moves 1 tick (10 with Shift), the new dimensions are announced, and the change is persisted on blur
```

## Technical notes / design
Fills are drawn by the T03 quad batch with premultiplied alpha; the flatten-opacity toggle is a single uniform that switches the blend from additive accumulation to a max-alpha composite, so it costs nothing per shape. A parallel channel is stored as three points (two defining the first edge, one defining the offset) and the second edge is derived at render time from the chart-space offset — storing four independent points would let the edges drift apart on a scale change. The ellipse is stored as its bounding box and evaluated by fragment SDF. Contrast: the default fill token is chosen so candle bodies retain ≥3:1 against the filled background in both themes, and the golden images assert it.

## Test plan
Unit: shape geometry, derived channel edge, zero-area rejection, dimension readout maths. Property-based: channel edges remain parallel under random viewport/scale transforms. Golden image: each shape, filled/unfilled, overlapping stack with flatten on and off, both themes; contrast assertion on candles under a fill. E2E: draw, resize, channel third-drag, flatten toggle, keyboard resize. a11y: axe-core, announcements.

## Security notes
No new server surface. Fill opacity is clamped server-side to [0,1] by the `DrawingInput` schema, so a crafted payload cannot produce an opaque full-screen overlay that hides the trading UI (a UI-redress consideration).

## Accessibility notes
Surrogate names compose the shape, its bounds and its dimensions ("Rectangle, 2026-10-13 09:00 to 13:00, 63,900 to 64,400, height 500, 240 bars"). Zones are distinguishable without colour by their border style and label. Fill defaults preserve text and candle contrast per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the flatten-opacity control is keyboard-reachable and its state announced.

## Performance notes
Fills add one quad instance per shape — no tessellation. Flatten mode is a uniform switch, not a second pass. Drag/resize with 200 drawings sustains ≥58 fps; pick for boxes uses rect containment within the ≤1 ms budget.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=rectangle|ellipse|parallel_channel|triangle}`, `drawing.flatten_opacity_toggled`, `drawing.resized{tool}` analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.

- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% engine on touched modules.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard create/resize verified; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

title: Fibonacci retracement, extension and time-zone tools with configurable levels
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-004 — Fibonacci retracement (Must) and extension (Should)** plus `fib_timezone` from the roadmap's E14 scope line. The story's NFR — "level configuration stored in drawing templates" — makes this the first tool whose *configuration*, not just its geometry, is persisted and reusable, which is why it lands before templates (E14-S09) but hands its level-set schema to it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `fib_retracement` (`Alt+F`), `fib_extension`, `fib_timezone` in the registry, built on the two-anchor pipeline (extension takes a third anchor for the projection origin).
- Default level set 0 / 0.236 / 0.382 / 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.786 / 1, rendered as horizontal level lines with **price and percentage labels** per level, stored in `geometry.levels` per `DrawingInput`.
- Level editor in the properties popover: add/remove/reorder levels, per-level visibility, per-level colour, optional per-level fill band between adjacent levels, and "save as default" so new fib drawings adopt the trader's set (US scenario "Customise levels").
- Inverted drag handling: dragging high→low inverts the level ordering correctly and keeps labels readable (no overlapping or upside-down text).
- Label collision handling: when levels crowd at high zoom-out, labels decimate by priority (0, 0.5, 0.618, 1 survive longest) rather than overprinting.
- Fib time-zone: vertical lines at Fibonacci bar counts from the anchor, labelled with the index and the resulting timestamp.
- Extension with both extend-left/extend-right behaviour for the level lines.

## Out of scope
- Auto-fib from detected swings — not R1.
- Fib channels/arcs/fans/spirals.
- Alerts on level touches (**E40**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw retracement
  When I drag from swing low to swing high
  Then levels 0/0.236/0.382/0.5/0.618/0.786/1 render with price and percentage labels

Scenario: Customise levels
  When I add a 0.886 level and save as default
  Then new Fibonacci drawings use my level set

Scenario: Inverted drag
  When I drag high to low
  Then levels invert correctly and labels remain readable

Scenario: Crowded labels decimate rather than overprint
  Given a fib drawing compressed to 60 px of vertical space
  Then only the priority levels keep labels, the rest render as lines, and no two labels overlap

Scenario: Invalid level input is rejected
  Given a level value that is not a finite number, or a duplicate of an existing level
  Then the editor shows a field-level error and the level set is not saved

Scenario: Levels survive persistence
  Given a fib with a custom 0.886 level
  When the app is reloaded
  Then the custom level set is restored exactly, including per-level colours and visibility
```

## Technical notes / design
Level prices are computed as `p0 + (p1 - p0) * level` in `Decimal`, quantised for display to the instrument's tick size but **not** quantised in storage (levels are derived, not anchors). Percentage labels are derived from the level value itself, so an inverted drag needs no special-casing beyond label placement. Level lines are ordinary line instances from T03; the optional bands are quad instances, so a 12-level fib is 12 + 11 instances — well inside the overlay budget. Label decimation reuses the axis-decimation priority mechanism from E11 rather than inventing a second one.

## Test plan
Unit: level price maths including inverted and negative-extension cases, decimal precision, duplicate/NaN rejection, decimation priority. Golden image: default set, custom set with bands, inverted, compressed (decimated), both themes. E2E: draw → customise → save as default → new drawing adopts it → reload persists. Contract: `geometry.levels` round-trips through `/drawings`.

## Security notes
Level arrays are user-controlled: the API and client both cap the level count (default 24) so a crafted payload cannot force thousands of line instances and degrade the render loop (availability). Values are validated as finite numbers server-side.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate exposes the fib as a group with each level as a child ("0.618 at 64,318.4"), so a screen-reader user can read the levels without seeing them. Level colours are supplemented by the numeric label, never colour-alone. The level editor is a standard keyboard-operable list with add/remove buttons, labelled fields and error text tied by `aria-describedby`.

## Performance notes
Level recomputation on drag is O(levels) and runs in the worker; label decimation is computed once per viewport change, not per frame. A fib with the maximum level count stays inside the 200-drawing overlay budget and the ≤3 text draw calls per pane limit.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=fib_retracement|fib_extension|fib_timezone}`, `drawing.fib_levels_changed{count}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}` analytics.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on touched modules.
- [ ] Golden images committed including the decimated state.
- [ ] axe-core green; level editor verified keyboard-only; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] Level-set schema handed to E14-S09 templates and documented.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies

## Branch

`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-004; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `DrawingInput.geometry.levels`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037; `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.10, §3.7 decimation.
