title: Anchored VWAP drawing with standard-deviation bands and incremental update
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-005 — Anchored VWAP drawing (Must)**: "As an order-flow trader, I want to click a bar to anchor a VWAP, so that I can measure value from any event." It is the only DRAW tool that is also a *computation over market data*, which brings two constraints from the story: an incremental update budget ("never recompute the whole series per tick; ≤2 ms update per anchored VWAP") and an honesty requirement — when the anchor precedes recorded tick history, the result must be visibly badged as approximate.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tool `anchored_vwap` in the registry: single click on a bar sets the anchor; the VWAP line is computed from that bar's prints forward and **updates live** as new trades arrive.
- Standard-deviation bands at 1σ / 2σ / 3σ, individually toggleable in the properties popover, rendered as lines with optional fill bands.
- Incremental accumulator state per anchored VWAP (`Σpv`, `Σv`, `Σp²v`) advanced per new bar/trade rather than recomputed; re-anchoring or a history backfill triggers exactly one bounded recompute.
- **Approximation fallback**: when the anchor is earlier than recorded tick history (E16 recorder start), VWAP is computed from bar-approximated volume and the drawing renders a visible "approximate" badge (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge) with a tooltip explaining why and from when real ticks are available.
- Live price/σ readout in the legend; the VWAP value and current σ distance exposed on hover and to the surrogate node.
- Persistence: anchor `{t, p}` plus band configuration in `style`/`geometry`; the computed series is never persisted (derived state).

## Out of scope
- Session/rolling VWAP as an **indicator** — that is **E13** (`IND` domain); this story is the drawing-anchored variant only.
- Profile-derived VWAP and value-area overlays — **E19**.
- Anchoring to a news/derivatives event rather than a bar — R2+.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Anchor
  When I click a bar to anchor
  Then a VWAP is computed from that bar's prints forward and updates live

Scenario: Bands
  When I enable standard-deviation bands
  Then 1/2/3σ bands render and are individually toggleable

Scenario: No tick data
  Given the anchor precedes recorded tick history
  Then VWAP falls back to bar-approximated volume with a visible "approximate" badge

Scenario: Update stays inside budget
  Given an anchored VWAP spanning 50 000 bars
  When a new trade arrives
  Then the update is incremental and costs ≤2 ms, with no full-series recomputation

Scenario: Re-anchoring is bounded
  When the anchor is dragged 10 000 bars earlier
  Then exactly one recompute runs, it reports progress if it exceeds 100 ms, and the UI never blocks

Scenario: Data gap is not hidden
  Given a gap in recorded trades inside the anchored range
  Then the badge and tooltip state that the series is partial, and the numeric readout is not presented as exact
```

## Technical notes / design
The accumulator lives in the engine worker beside the bar/trade series so no market data crosses the thread boundary per tick. σ is derived from the running `Σp²v` via the standard weighted-variance identity, with `Decimal`→`float64` conversion done once at the accumulator boundary and the running sums held in a numerically stable form (compensated summation) — a naive `Σp²v` over 50k bars of a 64,000-priced instrument loses precision fast, and this is risk **R7 Data accuracy**, not a cosmetic concern. The approximate path uses kline `turnover/volume` as the per-bar typical price × volume, and the badge is bound to the *provenance* of the data, matching the pattern already used for profiles in SCR-038.

## Test plan
Unit: accumulator correctness against a brute-force reference over generated series (exact within tolerance), σ identity, compensated-summation precision at 50k bars, approximate-path fallback selection. Integration: recorded Bybit fixture replay with a known VWAP result; gap fixture asserting the partial badge. Perf: 2 ms update budget asserted in CI; re-anchor recompute bounded. E2E: anchor, toggle bands, drag anchor, reload persistence. Golden image: VWAP + 3 bands, both themes, badged state.

## Security notes
No new server surface. The approximate badge is a *correctness-disclosure* control: suppressing it would misrepresent derived data to a trader making sizing decisions, which the advice-boundary policy (R9) treats as a real risk — the badge is therefore covered by an automated test, not only a design note.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate exposes "Anchored VWAP from 2026-10-13 09:00, current 64,180.2, price 1.4 sigma above" and the approximate state in text ("approximate: computed from bars, tick history starts 2026-10-11"). Band toggles are keyboard-operable checkboxes. The badge is text + icon, never colour-alone, and meets contrast in both themes.

## Performance notes
≤2 ms per update per anchored VWAP (story NFR); incremental only; bounded recompute on re-anchor with progress reporting beyond 100 ms; multiple simultaneous anchored VWAPs share the trade iteration pass rather than each scanning the series.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=anchored_vwap}`, `drawing.vwap_bands_toggled{sigma}`, `drawing.vwap_approximated` analytics; metrics `engine_vwap_update_ms`, `engine_vwap_recompute_total`, `engine_vwap_approx_active` gauge.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Accuracy validated against a brute-force reference on a recorded fixture.
- [ ] 2 ms update budget asserted in CI with a regression gate.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% on the engine accumulator, ≥80% frontend.
- [ ] axe-core green; approximate-state announcement verified; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S02** (anchor placement pipeline); requires the trade/bar series from **E12** and recorder provenance from **E16** (US-DRAW-005 deps: US-MKT-006).

## Branch
`feat/e14-anchored-vwap`

title: Text note, callout, arrow and measure tool annotations
body: ## Context Implements **US-DRAW-006 — Text, note and price label annotations (Must)**: "I want to attach notes to the chart, so that my reasoning stays with the price action", and adds the `arrow`, `callout` and `measure` tools from the roadmap's E14 scope line. This is the only DRAW story with a genuine **injection surface** — the NFR says it outright: "text sanitised before storage and rendering" — and the only one whose output flows into another product surface ("notes are included in journal snapshots", E41). ## Scope / Deliverables - Tools `text`, `callout`, `arrow`, `measure` in the registry (`Alt+M` for measure). - Text/callout: place at a bar+price anchor, inline edit with a plain-text editor, font size (8–48 per `DrawingInput.style`), colour, optional background box and border; the callout adds a leader line to a second anchor. - **Overflow handling**: text exceeding its box truncates with an expand affordance and a full-text tooltip (US scenario "Long text"); the expanded view is a popover, not an unbounded canvas box. - Arrow: two-anchor directional marker reusing the trendline pipeline with a head glyph. - **Measure tool**: transient by default — drag between two points and read price delta, %, bar count, elapsed time and (when available) traded volume in the range; `Enter` pins it as a persisted `measure` drawing, `Esc` discards. - Sanitisation: control characters and bidi-override characters stripped, length capped (120 chars for labels, a configured maximum for note bodies), content stored and rendered as **plain text only** at every boundary (canvas glyphs, DOM surrogate, journal snapshot, tooltip). - Every annotation appears in the object tree (E14-S08) with its text and anchor and is keyboard-reachable — the US "Screen reader" scenario. ## Out of scope - Rich text, markdown, links or images in notes. - Emoji-marker library beyond the plain text path. - Journal integration itself (**E41**) — this story only guarantees the sanitised, plain-text contract it will consume. ## Acceptance criteria ```gherkin Scenario: Add note When I place a note and type text Then it anchors to a bar and price and persists per symbol Scenario: Long text Given the text exceeds the box Then it truncates with an expand affordance and a full-text tooltip Scenario: Screen reader Then each annotation is listed in the object tree with its text and anchor, and is reachable by keyboard Scenario: Markup is never interpreted Given a note whose text is "" When it renders on the canvas, in the object tree, in the tooltip and in a journal snapshot Then the literal characters are displayed in every surface and no script executes Scenario: Bidi and control characters are neutralised Given a note containing bidi-override or control characters Then they are stripped on write, so the stored and displayed text cannot spoof surrounding UI text Scenario: Measure is transient unless pinned When I drag a measurement and release without confirming Then the readout disappears and nothing is persisted; pressing Enter instead pins it as a drawing ``` ## Technical notes / design Sanitisation happens **on write, server-side** (E14-T01 validation) and defensively on render; the client never trusts stored text either, because a drawing may predate a sanitiser change. Canvas text goes through the SDF atlas as glyph indices, which is inherently inert, but the DOM surrogate and the tooltip use `textContent` assignment exclusively. Text boxes size to their content up to a max box, then truncate at a glyph boundary with an ellipsis; measurement of the truncation point happens in the worker using atlas metrics so no DOM reflow is involved. The measure tool's volume readout is only shown when recorded trade data covers the range, otherwise the field is omitted rather than estimated. ## Test plan Unit: sanitiser (XSS payload corpus, bidi/control characters, length caps), truncation at glyph boundaries, measure maths (delta, %, bars, elapsed). Security: the XSS corpus asserted across all four render surfaces. Golden image: note, callout, arrow, truncated note, measure readout, both themes. E2E: place note → type → reload → text intact; long text expand; measure transient vs pinned; keyboard placement and editing. a11y: axe-core, object-tree listing assertion, screen-reader read-out of note text. ## Security notes Primary threat: stored XSS via user-authored note text reaching a DOM surface (chart surrogate, object tree, tooltip, journal export) — STRIDE Tampering/Elevation. Controls: server-side sanitisation and length caps on write, plain-text-only rendering with no `innerHTML` anywhere on the path, a CSP that forbids inline script as defence in depth, and an automated XSS-corpus test that must run on every one of the four surfaces. Secondary: text spoofing via bidi overrides, mitigated by stripping those characters. Data classification: user content; notes may contain trading rationale and are therefore owner-scoped like all drawings. ## Accessibility notes Note text is the accessible name of its surrogate; long text is fully available to assistive technology even when visually truncated (the surrogate carries the full string). The inline editor is a real focusable text control with a label, `Esc` to cancel and `Ctrl+Enter` to commit. Font-size minimum of 8 pt is paired with a warning below 11 pt about legibility; text contrast against both themes and against any background box is validated. ## Performance notes Annotations share the ≤3 text draw calls per pane budget; glyph atlas usage is capped per drawing so a long note cannot evict other layers' glyphs. Truncation metrics are computed once per text change, not per frame. ## Observability `drawing.created{tool=text|callout|arrow|measure}`, `drawing.note_expanded`, `drawing.measure_pinned` analytics; metric `drawings_text_sanitised_total{reason}` to show the sanitiser is actually firing in production. ## Definition of Done - [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests. - [ ] XSS corpus test green across canvas surrogate, object tree, tooltip and journal-snapshot paths. - [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% on the backend sanitiser. - [ ] Security engineer review comment present; SAST/SCA clean. - [ ] axe-core green; screen-reader pass on note reading; design-qa recorded. - [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed. ## Dependencies `blocked_by`: **E14-S01** (single-anchor pipeline, persistence proven). Feeds **E14-S08** (object tree lists annotations) and **E41** (journal snapshots). ## Branch `feat/e14-annotations` ## References `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-006; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `DrawingInput.style.label`, `geometry.text`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md`; `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`. ## Agent execution brief **Read first** 1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction) 2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries) 3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries) 4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path) 5. title: Long/short position tool with R:R, risk sizing and send-to-ticket handoff
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-007 — Long/short position tool (Must)**: "I want a drag-based long/short tool showing risk, reward and size, so that I plan the trade before I place it." It is the highest-stakes drawing in the Epic because its numbers influence real position sizing, and its NFR is unambiguous: "identical sizing maths as US-PROF-002 (shared implementation)". Two implementations of sizing that disagree by a rounding step is a money bug, so this story **imports** the sizing module rather than reimplementing it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Tools `long_position` and `short_position`: three draggable levels — entry, stop, target — plus a time extent, rendered as the familiar two-tone box (risk zone / reward zone) with handles per level.
- Readout on the drawing and in the properties popover: **R:R ratio**, risk in USDT, reward in USDT, stop distance in ticks and %, target distance, and the **position size implied by the active account profile** (leverage, sizing rule, risk cap).
- Shared sizing implementation: the same module used by US-PROF-002 (per-account profile sizing), imported — not copied — with a contract test asserting both call sites produce identical output for a shared fixture table.
- Tick/lot validation per SCR-037 ("the position tool validates against tick/lot"): entry/stop/target quantised to tick size, size quantised to lot size and floored to `min_qty`, with the residual shown rather than silently rounded away.
- **Risk-cap error state**: when implied risk exceeds the profile cap, the tool renders its error state and "send to ticket" is **disabled with the reason stated** (US scenario).
- "Send to ticket" handoff: emits a typed intent `{side, entry, stop, target, qty, symbol, profile_id}` on the app bus. In R1 the consumer (**E30 order ticket**) does not exist yet, so the action is gated by the `trading.ticket` feature flag — flag off renders it disabled with "available when trading ships"; the intent contract and its tests ship now.
- No-profile fallback: with no account profile selected, size is shown as "—" with an explanatory chip, and R:R/risk-in-ticks still compute.

## Out of scope
- Placing any order (**E30/E29**) — this story never touches the OMS.
- Fan-out sizing across multiple accounts (**E34**).
- Fee/funding-adjusted PnL projection — R3.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag entry, stop and target
  Then the tool shows R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT and the position size implied by the account profile

Scenario: Send to ticket
  When I choose "send to ticket"
  Then the order ticket opens pre-filled with entry, stop, target and the computed size

Scenario: Risk exceeds cap
  Given the implied risk exceeds the profile cap
  Then the tool highlights it in the error state and the "send to ticket" action is disabled with the reason

Scenario: Sizing matches the profile implementation exactly
  Given the shared sizing fixture table
  When sizing is computed through the position tool and through the per-account profile path
  Then every row produces byte-identical quantities, and any divergence fails the contract test

Scenario: Tick and lot rounding is visible, not silent
  Given a stop distance that implies 0.0137 BTC on a 0.001 lot instrument
  Then the tool shows 0.013 with the rounding direction indicated, and never shows an unplaceable quantity

Scenario: Trading not yet enabled
  Given the trading.ticket feature flag is off
  Then "send to ticket" is disabled with an explanatory label, the intent is not emitted, and all readouts still compute

Scenario: Inverted levels
  Given a long position whose stop is dragged above its entry
  Then the tool shows an invalid state with the reason and does not report a negative risk as a positive reward
```

## Technical notes / design
All money maths is `Decimal` with the instrument's tick/lot metadata; no float ever touches risk or quantity. The sizing module is a pure function `(entry, stop, profile, instrument) -> {qty, risk_usdt, capped: bool, reason}` living in a shared package consumed by both this tool and the profile screen, with a golden fixture table (CSV) as the single source of truth for both — that table *is* the contract test. Levels are stored as three anchor points so the drawing survives interval changes like any other; the derived numbers are never persisted. The error state uses the design-system error token plus an icon and text, so it is not a colour-only signal.

## Test plan
Unit: R:R maths, risk/reward in USDT, inverted-level detection, tick/lot quantisation and floor-to-min-qty. Contract: the shared fixture table asserted through both call sites. Integration: profile changes (leverage, risk cap) update the readout live. E2E: drag all three levels, exceed the cap, observe the disabled action and reason; flag on/off behaviour. a11y: axe-core, announcements of each readout change. Golden image: long and short, valid/invalid/capped states, both themes.

## Security notes
The displayed size is decision-grade information: an incorrect or stale profile silently applied would misinform sizing, so the readout names which profile it used and invalidates immediately when the profile changes. The send-to-ticket intent carries no credentials and is validated by the consumer independently — the receiving ticket must re-derive size server-side rather than trusting the client-sent quantity (documented here so E30 inherits the requirement). Risk-cap enforcement in this tool is advisory UI only; the authoritative cap lives in **E39** and must never be assumed enforced by this drawing.

## Accessibility notes
The surrogate composes "Long position, entry 64,000, stop 63,700, target 64,900, R:R 3.0, risk 150 USDT, size 0.5 BTC, within cap". Each level handle is individually focusable and nudgeable by tick, with the recomputed R:R announced politely (debounced so a nudge-hold does not flood the live region). The capped/invalid state is conveyed by text and icon, and the disabled action states its reason in its accessible description, not only in a tooltip.

## Performance notes
Recomputation on drag is O(1) and runs on the main thread inside the interaction frame; live-region announcements are debounced to 300 ms. The tool renders as two quads, three lines and one label group — negligible against the overlay budget.

## Observability
`drawing.created{tool=long_position|short_position}`, `drawing.position_tool_capped`, `drawing.send_to_ticket{enabled}` analytics; metric `position_tool_sizing_divergence_total` (must stay zero; alerts if the shared module ever disagrees at runtime).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Shared-sizing contract test green against the fixture table used by the profile implementation.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend / ≥85% on the shared sizing package.
- [ ] Security review comment present covering the "client-sent quantity is never authoritative" note.
- [ ] axe-core green; screen-reader pass on readouts; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] Feature flag `trading.ticket` state recorded per environment.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S03** (box/handle model). Cross-epic: shared sizing from **E28** (US-PROF-002) — if E28 lands later, the module is authored here to the agreed signature and E28 imports it; consumer **E30** (US-ORD-001) is R3 and gated by flag.

## Branch
`feat/e14-position-tool`

title: Object tree, lock/hide, clone, z-order and undo/redo UI (SCR-036)
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-008 — Object management: undo/redo, lock, hide, layers (Must/Should/Could)**: "I want to undo, lock, hide and manage drawing objects, so that my chart stays under control." This is the story that makes a chart with 500 objects usable, and it is also the story where the accessibility promise of the whole Epic is cashed: the object tree is the non-visual representation of the canvas. Its NFRs are hard numbers — "undo stack ≥50 operations per symbol, session-scoped; tree is virtualised for ≥500 objects" — and its home is **SCR-036** (shared with the indicator manager from E13).

## Scope / Deliverables
- The drawings section of **SCR-036** object tree (CMP-049 Table in a CMP-046 Drawer): one row per drawing showing **type, anchor time/price, label, visibility and lock state**, grouped by tool family, sorted by z-order or creation time.
- Row actions: select (highlights and scrolls the chart to it), rename label, toggle visibility, toggle lock, clone, delete, bring-forward / send-backward (z-order), with multi-row selection and bulk actions.
- Global actions surfaced both here and in the toolbar: lock-all, hide-all, delete-all — with lock-all behaving exactly as the US requires: "they cannot be moved by dragging but remain visible and selectable for inspection".
- Undo/redo UI: toolbar buttons with tooltips naming the next operation ("Undo: delete trendline"), `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z`, stack depth ≥50 per symbol (target 100 per the engine design), session-scoped, cleared on symbol change but independent per symbol within a session.
- **Virtualisation**: the tree renders only visible rows and stays responsive at ≥500 objects; filter-by-type and free-text filter on label.
- Clone semantics: a cloned drawing is offset slightly, retains style, gets a new id, and is a single undoable command.
- Empty state (CMP-026) when a symbol has no drawings, with a hint pointing at the toolbar hotkeys.

## Out of scope
- Indicator rows in SCR-036 (**E13** owns them; this story only composes into the same screen).
- Cross-pane sync toggles and templates (**E14-S09**).
- Persisted (cross-session) undo history — explicitly session-scoped by the NFR.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Undo/redo
  When I press Ctrl+Z after deleting a drawing
  Then it is restored with all properties; Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes

Scenario: Lock and hide all
  When I lock all drawings
  Then they cannot be moved by dragging but remain visible and selectable for inspection

Scenario: Object tree
  Then an object list shows every drawing on the symbol with type, anchor time/price, visibility and lock state, navigable by keyboard

Scenario: Tree stays responsive at scale
  Given 500 drawings on the symbol
  Then the tree renders in under 100 ms, scrolls at 60 fps, and only visible rows exist in the DOM

Scenario: Undo stack is bounded and per-symbol
  Given 120 operations on BTCUSDT and 5 on ETHUSDT
  Then BTCUSDT offers at least the most recent 50 undos, ETHUSDT offers its own 5, and neither affects the other

Scenario: Bulk delete is one undoable command
  Given 20 rows selected
  When they are deleted and Ctrl+Z is pressed once
  Then all 20 are restored together with their properties

Scenario: Selecting a row reveals the drawing
  Given a drawing anchored outside the current viewport
  When its row is activated
  Then the chart scrolls to bring it into view and the drawing is selected and announced
```

## Technical notes / design
The tree is a virtualised list over the same immutable store state the engine renders, so there is no second source of truth and no synchronisation code — a row is a projection of a drawing. Bulk operations compose into one composite command so undo is symmetric with the user's mental model. Scroll-to-drawing uses the chart-space anchor and the existing viewport animation from E11 rather than a jump cut, and respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. Z-order writes `z_index` (smallint per the schema) with a normalisation pass to avoid unbounded growth on repeated bring-forward.

## Test plan
Unit: command composition for bulk ops, stack bounds/scoping, z-order normalisation, filter logic. Perf: render and scroll benchmark at 500 and 1000 rows; DOM node count assertion proving virtualisation. E2E: undo/redo across every operation type, lock-all then attempt drag, hide-all then attempt pick, bulk delete + single undo, row → chart reveal. a11y: axe-core, full keyboard traversal, screen-reader row announcements.

## Security notes
Rows display user-authored labels — same plain-text-only rendering contract as E14-S06, re-asserted by the XSS corpus test on the tree surface. Delete-all and bulk delete are destructive: confirmed, scoped to the current user's own drawings, undoable, and never triggered by a single unmodified keystroke.

## Accessibility notes
This is the Epic's primary non-visual surface. The tree is a real table (CMP-049) with row headers, sortable columns, and per-row controls that are buttons with explicit accessible names ("Hide trendline at 64,120") — not icon-only ambiguity. Keyboard: arrow navigation, `Space` to toggle visibility, `L` to lock, `Delete` to remove, `Enter` to reveal on the chart. Lock and visibility state are text + icon, never colour-alone. Undo/redo announce the operation they performed. Focus returns predictably after a row is deleted (to the next row).

## Performance notes
Virtualised for ≥500 objects (NFR); initial render <100 ms at 500 rows; scrolling at 60 fps; toggling visibility on 100 rows applies as one store update and one engine snapshot, not 100.

## Observability
`drawing.locked`, `drawing.hidden`, `drawing.cloned`, `drawing.zorder_changed`, `drawing.bulk_deleted{count}`, `drawings_undo_total`, `drawings_redo_total` analytics/metrics; `drawings_tree_render_ms` client metric.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests.
- [ ] Virtualisation proven by a DOM-node-count assertion at 500 rows.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on the tree and command modules.
- [ ] axe-core green on SCR-036; full keyboard traversal and a screen-reader pass recorded (this is the Epic's headline a11y evidence).
- [ ] design-qa comparison against SCR-036 recorded; QA black-box plan executed; demoed.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S01** (drawings exist to manage), **E14-S06** (annotation text in rows). Composes with **E13** on SCR-036. Blocks **E14-S09**.

## Branch
`feat/e14-object-tree`

title: Drawing style templates and cross-pane level sync
body:
## Context
Implements **US-DRAW-009 — Drawing templates and cross-chart sync (Should)**: "I want drawing styles saved as templates and levels synced across panes, so that multi-chart layouts stay consistent." It closes the Epic by making the previous eight stories consistent and reusable, and it carries one hard safety rule from the NFR: "sync is per-layout and per-symbol; **never** syncs across different symbols."

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Style templates**: save the current drawing's style (colour, width, dash, fill, label settings, and for fib the level set from E14-S04) as a named template per tool; apply a template to a selection or set it as the tool's default for new drawings.
- Template management UI in the properties popover: save, rename, apply, set-default, delete, with a preview swatch (CMP-228 PreviewTile pattern).
- **Cross-pane sync**: a per-pane toggle (part of the layout's sync-axis group from E15); with sync on, a drawing created or edited on symbol S in one pane appears in every other pane showing symbol S in the same layout, instantly.
- Sync-off panes keep their drawings **local to that pane** (scoped by `layout_id`) and the object tree marks them as pane-local, per the US scenario.
- Hard guard: sync is keyed on `(layout_id, symbol)`; a pane showing a different symbol never receives another symbol's drawings, enforced by an assertion in the store and an explicit test.
- Migration behaviour: toggling sync off on a pane converts nothing retroactively; toggling on offers an explicit "copy existing pane-local drawings to the symbol" action rather than doing it silently.

## Out of scope
- Sharing templates between users (**collaboration, R5**).
- Layout persistence itself (**E15**) — this story consumes it.
- Syncing indicators (**E13/E15**).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Style template
  When I save a style as "key level" and apply it
  Then colour, width, style and label settings apply to new drawings of that type

Scenario: Cross-pane sync
  Given two panes show BTCUSDT at different intervals and level-sync is on
  Then a level drawn in one appears in the other instantly

Scenario: Sync off
  Given sync is off for a pane
  Then drawings made there remain local to that pane and are marked as such in the object tree

Scenario: Symbols never cross
  Given one pane shows BTCUSDT and another shows ETHUSDT with sync on
  When a level is drawn on BTCUSDT
  Then the ETHUSDT pane is unchanged, and an assertion prevents any code path from delivering it there

Scenario: Template deletion does not orphan drawings
  Given drawings created from the "key level" template
  When the template is deleted
  Then existing drawings keep their concrete style values unchanged and only the reusable template disappears

Scenario: Enabling sync is explicit, never silent
  Given a pane with 4 pane-local drawings
  When sync is enabled for it
  Then nothing changes until the user confirms "copy 4 drawings to the symbol", and that action is undoable
```

## Technical notes / design
Templates are style snapshots, not references — applying a template copies concrete values into the drawing, which is why deleting a template cannot orphan anything. They persist alongside other chart config (the `chart_templates` family in migration `0011_workspace`) scoped to the owner. Sync is a *query-scope* decision, not a replication mechanism: a synced pane subscribes to `(symbol)` and a pane-local one to `(symbol, layout_id)`, so there is no copying, no conflict resolution and no chance of divergence — and the symbol guard is a single filter that cannot be bypassed per-pane.

## Test plan
Unit: template save/apply/set-default/delete, fib level-set inclusion, scope-key resolution. Property-based: for any random pane/symbol/layout combination, a drawing is delivered only to panes whose symbol matches exactly. E2E: two-pane sync on/off, enable-sync confirmation flow, template apply and default, template delete leaving drawings intact. a11y: axe-core on the template UI, keyboard operation, announcements.

## Security notes
Templates are owner-scoped like drawings; template names are user content, sanitised and length-capped on the same path as labels (E14-S06). The symbol guard is also a correctness control — a level from another instrument rendered on a chart could directly cause a mis-priced trade, so it is asserted rather than assumed.

## Accessibility notes
Template list is a keyboard-operable listbox with named actions per item; the preview swatch has a text description of the style ("2 px dashed, accent colour") because a swatch alone is colour-only information. The sync toggle states its scope in its accessible description ("Sync drawings across panes showing BTCUSDT in this layout"). Pane-local drawings are marked with text in the object tree, not only an icon.

## Performance notes
Sync adds no per-frame cost (it is a subscription scope). Applying a template to a multi-selection is one store command and one engine snapshot regardless of selection size.

## Observability
`drawing.template_saved{tool}`, `drawing.template_applied{tool}`, `drawing.default_saved{tool}`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts` (the SCR-037 analytics event), `drawing.sync_toggled{enabled}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin scenarios covered by named automated tests, including the cross-symbol guard property test.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80% frontend on templates and scope resolution.
- [ ] axe-core green; keyboard-only template management verified; design-qa recorded.
- [ ] `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 updated with the template UI as shipped.
- [ ] QA black-box plan executed; demoed. Epic-level acceptance can now be run.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E14-S08** (object tree marks pane-local drawings), **E14-S04** (fib level sets are part of a template). Cross-epic: **E15** (US-LAY-003) provides the layout and sync-axis model.

## Branch
`feat/e14-templates-sync`

## References
`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-009, US-LAY-003; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037; `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-228; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8 (`chart_templates`, `drawings.layout_id`); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings?layout_id=`.

title: UX research: drawing, magnet and object-management mental models
body:
## Context
Drawing tools are the single most muscle-memory-bound surface in any charting product. The Owner and the account managers arrive with years of TradingView habits: `Alt+T` for a trendline, magnet snapping to OHLC, click-click for two-point tools, drag-drag for zones, `Esc` to cancel, `Ctrl+Z` to undo. E14 delivers thirteen-plus tools (US-DRAW-001..009) onto SCR-037 and SCR-036 in Sprints 06-09; every millimetre of divergence from that muscle memory is felt as a defect, and every divergence we *deliberately* keep must be justified by evidence rather than by a designer's preference.

Three things are genuinely unknown and cannot be settled from the catalogue. First, **magnet behaviour**: CMP-223 exposes `magnetMode: "off"|"weak"|"strong"`, US-DRAW-002 requires anchors to snap to nearest OHLC within a radius with the snap target highlighted - but the default mode, the radius in px, and whether the highlight is enough feedback are unresolved. Second, **precision versus speed**: US-DRAW-001 requires drag handles >=24 px, which on a dense footprint chart is a large target that may cover the very cells the user is reading. Third, **object management at scale**: US-DRAW-008 expects the object tree to be virtualised for >=500 objects, yet we do not know whether users actually curate drawings or simply accumulate them until the chart is unreadable and then delete-all.

This research runs in Sprint 02, four sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story, so that wireframes (E14-D02) and the hi-fi decks are drawn against observed behaviour rather than assumption.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions, 60 minutes: the Owner plus up to 2 prospective account managers (P1/P2 personas in `docs/plan/10-personas.md`), each run half as a **contextual inquiry** on their current tool and half against a greyscale clickable prototype of SCR-037.
- Probe set A - **tool selection**: how the participant picks a tool today (rail click, hotkey, right-click menu); which tools they actually use weekly versus never; expected hotkeys for trendline / horizontal / fib / rectangle / measure (compare against SCR-037's `Alt+T`/`Alt+H`/`Alt+F`/`Alt+R`/`Alt+M`); whether a tool should stay active after one use or revert to cursor.
- Probe set B - **magnet & precision**: place a horizontal level at a specific swing high with magnet off, weak and strong; observe mis-snaps and corrections; establish the preferred default and whether snapping must be visible before commit (US-DRAW-002 snap-target highlight).
- Probe set C - **editing & undo**: move, clone, lock, delete; deliberate mis-drag then recovery (does the participant reach for `Ctrl+Z`, the object tree, or redraw?); expectations of what undo restores (US-DRAW-008 requires all properties restored).
- Probe set D - **accumulation**: show a chart pre-loaded with 120 drawings; observe the curation strategy; test whether "hide all" or "lock all" (US-DRAW-008) is the instinct; test the object-tree concept (SCR-036) as a management surface.
- Probe set E - **position tool**: US-DRAW-007's long/short tool drag order (entry -> stop -> target vs entry -> target -> stop), what numbers must be visible without hovering (R:R, risk USDT, reward USDT, size), and reaction to the risk-cap error state.
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e14-drawing-mental-models.md`: ranked friction list, verbatim quotes, an observed-hotkey table versus the SCR-037 proposal, and 8-12 **adopted decisions** each phrased as a testable statement that a wireframe can satisfy or violate.
- Explicit recommendation on five open questions: (1) default magnet mode and snap radius; (2) sticky-tool versus revert-to-cursor after a completed drawing; (3) handle size versus occlusion on dense footprint charts; (4) whether cross-chart level sync (US-DRAW-009) defaults on or off; (5) the position tool's drag order and its primary read-out.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design, colour or token decisions - greyscale only; hi-fi begins at E14-D03.
- Indicator management (E13) even though it shares SCR-036; only the drawings branch of the tree is probed here.
- Chart trading order lines (CMP-192, E30-series) - visually adjacent but a different epic and a different safety model.
- Backend persistence design for `/api/v1/drawings` - engineering concern, E14 engineering chunk.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Hotkey expectations are evidenced against the catalogue
  Given all three participants have been asked to invoke each of the five primary tools without looking at the rail
  When docs/design/research/e14-drawing-mental-models.md is reviewed
  Then it contains a table of expected hotkey per participant per tool
  And every divergence from SCR-037's documented hotkeys is either adopted as an amendment proposal or recorded as a deliberate keep with a reason

Scenario: Magnet default is chosen from observation
  Given each participant has placed the same level with magnet off, weak and strong
  Then the report records mis-snap counts and correction time per mode
  And it recommends a default mode and a snap radius in pixels backed by those observations

Scenario: A participant cannot recover from a mis-drag
  Given a participant accidentally moves an existing drawing while aiming at another
  When they attempt recovery
  Then the attempted recovery path is recorded verbatim
  And if recovery failed, the failure is raised as a ranked friction item that E14-D02 must resolve in the wireframes

Scenario: Screen-reader participant path is covered
  Given at least one session is run with a screen reader and no mouse
  When the participant attempts to create a horizontal line via the keyboard-draw flow described in CMP-191
  Then the report records whether the flow was completable unaided, where it broke, and what was announced at each step

Scenario: A finding contradicts a locked document
  Given a finding contradicts SCR-037 in 14-screens-catalogue.md or an NFR in US-DRAW-001..009
  Then it is filed as an explicit amendment proposal against that document
  And no wireframe is drawn against the contradicted behaviour until the amendment is accepted or rejected
```

## Technical notes / design
The prototype is a Figma clickable greyscale flow plus a small throwaway canvas harness for the magnet probes - snapping cannot be evaluated in a static prototype because the whole question is about continuous feedback during a drag. The harness renders a static candle series at a realistic density and implements the three magnet modes only; it is explicitly throwaway code and is not promoted.

Probe D uses a seeded 120-drawing fixture generated from the same generator the engine benchmark harness (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 14, B8) uses, so the density shown to participants matches the density engineering will benchmark against.

Sessions are recorded with consent; recordings are stored on the Tailscale-only internal share and deleted after the findings doc is signed off.

## Test plan
Not an engineering deliverable; validation is methodological. Pilot the script with one internal participant before the first real session and correct leading questions. Each adopted decision must be traceable to at least two observations or one strong Owner directive, and this traceability is checked in the CDO review. The findings doc is reviewed by the Architect for anything that implies an engine capability not in `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.10.

## Security notes
No production data, no live accounts and no API keys are used in any session; the harness is fed a recorded BTCUSDT fixture. Session recordings may contain participants' own screens during contextual inquiry - participants are instructed to close broker windows first, and any incidental account identifier captured is redacted before the recording is stored. Drawing text notes (US-DRAW-006) are user-authored content that will later be sanitised before storage and render; the research must record whether participants expect to paste rich text or links, because that expectation drives the sanitisation requirement rather than the other way round.

## Accessibility notes
One full session is run keyboard-only with a screen reader, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` section 9. The keyboard-draw flow in CMP-191 (activate tool -> `Enter` places first point at the crosshair -> arrows move -> `Enter` commits) is a hard CI gate later, so its usability must be established now, not discovered during design QA. The research also establishes what the announcement of a mode change should say, since an active drawing tool is invisible to a screen-reader user.

## Performance notes
The magnet harness must itself run at >=58 fps so that latency in the harness is not mistaken for a UX finding; frame time is logged during each probe and any session with dropped frames is annotated. Observed tolerance for snap feedback latency is captured as an input to the engine's <=1 ms picking budget (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.9).

## Observability

title: Wireframes: drawing toolbar, canvas interaction model and object tree
body:
## Context
Before any pixel of SCR-037 is styled, the *interaction model* for drawings has to be settled end to end, because every tool in the kit shares it: how a tool is armed, how points are placed, how an in-progress drawing is cancelled, how an existing object is selected, moved, resized, cloned, locked and deleted, and how all of that is also reachable without a mouse. Thirteen tools with thirteen ad hoc behaviours would be unlearnable and untestable; one model instantiated thirteen times is both.

This ticket produces the greyscale wireframe set that fixes that model using E14-D01's adopted decisions. It covers SCR-037 (the left rail plus the properties popover), the drawings branch of SCR-036 (object tree), and the keyboard-creation path that connects to SCR-045's data-table grid ("create horizontal line at focused price"). It runs in Sprint 03, three sprints ahead of the first consuming FE story in Sprint 06.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Tool rail (SCR-037 / CMP-223)** wireframes: full tool inventory drawn - cursor, crosshair, trendline, ray, extended line, horizontal line/level, vertical line, rectangle, ellipse, triangle, parallel channel, Fibonacci retracement / extension / time zones, pitchfork, anchored VWAP, measure, long/short position tool, text note, arrow, brush, emoji marker - plus the magnet toggle, lock-all, hide-all and delete-all controls; grouping and overflow behaviour at short viewport heights; the sticky-versus-revert tool decision from E14-D01 drawn explicitly.
- **Creation state machine** drawn as a state diagram and as frames: armed -> first anchor -> (n-th anchor) -> committed; `Esc` at each state; what the cursor and the rail show at each state; the three-drag parallel-channel case (US-DRAW-003) and the click-once anchored-VWAP case (US-DRAW-005) as the two shape-of-interaction outliers.
- **Selection and edit model**: hover, selected, multi-select, locked, hidden and error states for a generic object; handle placement and hit tolerance annotated (>=24 px per US-DRAW-001 NFR, 10 px grab / 16 px touch tolerance per `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.9); drag, resize, clone, nudge (arrow = 1 tick, Shift+arrow = 10 ticks), delete.
- **Properties popover (SCR-037)**: the shared frame - colour, width, style, extend left/right, snap-to-OHLC, "alert when price crosses", save-as-default, delete - plus the per-tool extension slots (fib level list, VWAP band toggles, position-tool sizing read-out, text note content).
- **Object tree, drawings branch (SCR-036)**: rows showing type, anchor time/price, visibility, lock; grouping by type; multi-select and bulk actions; the virtualised >=500-object case; the empty state; and the pane-local versus synced marker required by US-DRAW-009.
- **Keyboard-creation path**: the full no-mouse flow from CMP-191, drawn frame by frame, including the entry point from SCR-045.
- Wireframes published in Figma (`CandleViewer / E14 Drawings / Wireframes`) and the interaction model written up as `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-interaction-model.md` so engineering has a normative text source, not only frames.

## Out of scope
- Colour, type, iconography, elevation and motion - greyscale boxes only; those are E14-D03..D06 and E14-D09.
- Indicator rows in SCR-036 (E13 owns those); this ticket draws only the drawings branch and must not change the tree's shell.
- Order/position lines (CMP-192) and alert lines - different epics, though the wireframes must show how a drawing selection behaves when an order line is underneath it.
- Drawing templates management UI beyond the "save as default" affordance; the template library is drawn in E14-D04.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every tool in SCR-037 is represented
  Given the wireframe set is reviewed against SCR-037's tool inventory
  When each listed tool is looked for
  Then every tool has a rail entry, a documented arming shortcut and a creation state sequence
  And any tool deliberately deferred out of R1 is marked as deferred with the sprint it returns in

Scenario: A drawing can be created without a mouse
  Given the keyboard-creation frames are walked in order
  When a horizontal line and a trendline are created using only the documented keys
  Then every step has a defined focus target, a defined announcement and a defined escape
  And no step requires a pointer position that cannot be reached by the keyboard crosshair

Scenario: In-progress drawing is cancelled
  Given a two-point tool with its first anchor placed
  When Esc is pressed
  Then the wireframes define that the in-progress geometry is discarded, the tool returns to its armed or cursor state per the E14-D01 decision, and nothing is persisted
  And the same behaviour is defined for losing focus, switching symbol and switching interval mid-draw

Scenario: Object accumulation is handled
  Given the 500-object object-tree frame
  Then the wireframes show virtualisation, grouping, bulk selection and a delete-all confirmation
  And the chart frame shows what the canvas looks like at that density, including the hide-all escape hatch

Scenario: An interaction conflicts with an existing chart gesture
  Given a proposed drawing gesture collides with a gesture already documented on SCR-030 (pan, zoom, Ctrl+drag chart trading, Alt+click market order)
  Then the collision is listed in the interaction-model document with the chosen resolution
  And the resolution is reviewed by the Architect and the chart-trading design owner before sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
The interaction model is written as an explicit state machine because the engine implements it as one (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.10: two-phase place-then-adjust, command stack of 100 entries shared with the toolbar). Wireframe frames and the state diagram must not disagree; the diagram is the normative artefact and the frames illustrate it.

Anchors are (timestamp, price) always, never pixels - the wireframes annotate this on every tool because it determines what "drag" means at the edges of the viewport and what happens on a log/linear scale flip (US-DRAW-002 NFR: anchors must not move).

Gesture collisions with SCR-030 are the main risk: `Ctrl+drag` on the price axis is chart trading, `Alt+click` is a market order, `Esc` already cancels an in-progress drawing, and `Del` already deletes the selected drawing. The model must keep those meanings and route around them, not redefine them.

## Test plan
Validation is a structured walkthrough rather than automated test. (1) Tool-inventory diff against SCR-037. (2) State-machine dry run: two engineers and one QA/SDET walk every tool through create, cancel, edit, undo, delete and report any undefined transition - an undefined transition is a blocking defect. (3) Keyboard-only walkthrough of the no-mouse frames. (4) Gesture-collision audit against SCR-030's documented hotkeys. (5) A 5-participant unmoderated first-click test on the rail grouping, run on the greyscale prototype. Results are recorded in the ticket.

## Security notes
Two surfaces carry security weight even at wireframe stage. The text-note tool (US-DRAW-006) accepts arbitrary user content that will be stored in `drawings.geometry` JSONB and rendered back onto a canvas and into the object tree - the wireframes must show the truncation/expand affordance and state that content is plain text, sanitised on write and on render, with no link auto-activation. The position tool (US-DRAW-007) can hand values to the order ticket; the wireframes must show it as a *pre-fill* that still passes through the ticket's own validation and arming, never as a path that places an order.

## Accessibility notes
Every frame carries focus-order annotation and an accessible-name annotation for each control, per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5 and 8. The rail is drawn as a vertical `role="toolbar"` with roving tabindex (CMP-223). Because an armed tool is invisible to a screen reader, the wireframes specify the mode-change announcement text. The object tree is drawn as the normative accessible equivalent for manipulating canvas objects, which means every canvas-only action must have a tree-side equivalent - any action that does not is a blocking defect at review.

## Performance notes
The wireframes annotate the layer model they assume: drawings render on a separate canvas layer above the price layer, and dragging a drawing must not re-render price/footprint (SCR-037 performance note; engine layer list in `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.2). Any proposed interaction that would force a full-scene re-render - for example a live-updating full-width measurement ribbon behind the candles - is flagged during the walkthrough and either redesigned or accepted with the Architect.

## Observability
The wireframes annotate where each SCR-037 analytics event fires (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) and add any event E14-D01 recommended, so instrumentation is designed in rather than retrofitted.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Wireframe set complete for the rail, the creation state machine, selection/edit states, the properties popover, the object-tree drawings branch and the keyboard path.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-interaction-model.md` merged with the normative state diagram and the gesture-collision resolutions.
- [ ] State-machine dry run executed with two engineers and one QA/SDET; no undefined transitions remain.
- [ ] Keyboard-only walkthrough passed; every step has focus, announcement and escape defined.
- [ ] Tool-inventory diff against SCR-037 clean or deferrals explicitly marked.
- [ ] Architect review of engine implications recorded.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the Sprint 06 FE stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D01** - adopted decisions on magnet defaults, sticky tools, handle size, sync default and position-tool drag order.
- **E11** engine core interaction/hit-testing capabilities as documented in `26-chart-engine-design.md` sections 3.9-3.10 (reference only, not a delivery dependency).

title: Hi-fi design: drawing tool rail & tool palette (SCR-037, CMP-223)
body:
## Context
The tool rail is the permanent, always-visible chrome of the charting workspace: a vertical strip that sits beside the most information-dense surface in the product and must be legible without competing with it. It is also the primary discovery surface for a kit of twenty-plus tools, which means iconography, grouping and state feedback carry the whole learnability burden. This ticket takes the greyscale model from E14-D02 to a signed-off hi-fi specification for SCR-037's rail and CMP-223 DrawingToolbar, in Sprint 04 - two sprints before the Sprint 06 stories that consume it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for **CMP-223 DrawingToolbar** in both themes (dark default, light) and both densities (`16-design-system-brief.md` density scale): default, tool-active (`aria-pressed`), hover, focus-visible, disabled, magnet off/weak/strong, all-locked, all-hidden.
- Complete **icon set** for every tool in SCR-037's inventory, drawn on the design-system grid, with an explicit legibility check at the smallest supported rail size and at 200% zoom; each icon paired with its text label for the tooltip and its accessible name.
- **Grouping and overflow**: the rail's section order (cursor/crosshair · lines · shapes · fib family · analysis: VWAP, measure, position · annotation: text, arrow, brush, emoji · object controls: magnet, lock-all, hide-all, delete-all), separators, and the overflow menu (CMP-041 Menu) used when viewport height cannot show all sections.
- **Hotkey surfacing** via CMP-022 Kbd in every tooltip, using the hotkeys confirmed in E14-D02 (`Alt+T`, `Alt+H`, `Alt+F`, `Alt+R`, `Alt+M`, `Ctrl+M` magnet).
- **Token usage spec**: which tokens each element consumes (`color.surface.raised`, `space.1`, `color.drawing.default`, `color.drawing.selected`, focus ring, radius), with no raw values anywhere.
- Storybook story list agreed with engineering: Default, ToolActive, MagnetStrong, AllLocked, Overflowing, Light, Zoom200 - matching CMP-223's documented story set plus the two new cases.
- Redlines and a spec page in `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-toolbar.md`.

## Out of scope
- The properties popover (E14-D04) and per-tool visual language for fib/VWAP/measure (E14-D05) and the position tool (E14-D06).
- Object tree styling (E14-D07).
- Motion (E14-D09) beyond stating which transitions exist.
- Any new design-system token or component - if the rail needs one, it is raised into E14-D08 rather than invented here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every state in the matrix is drawn in both themes
  Given the hi-fi file is reviewed
  When the state matrix (default, active, hover, focus, disabled, magnet x3, locked, hidden, overflow) is walked in dark and light
  Then every cell exists as a frame
  And no cell is represented by a note saying "same as dark"

Scenario: Active tool is distinguishable without colour
  Given the tool-active frame is rendered in greyscale and through a protanopia simulation
  Then the active tool remains identifiable by shape, fill or indicator, not by hue alone
  And the same is true of the three magnet modes

Scenario: Contrast passes over the chart background
  Given the rail is placed over the darkest and the lightest chart backgrounds in use
  When contrast is measured for icons, separators and the focus ring
  Then every measurement meets WCAG 2.2 AA (>=3:1 for UI components and graphics, >=4.5:1 for text)
  And the measured values are recorded in the spec page

Scenario: Rail does not fit the viewport
  Given a viewport height that cannot show all rail sections
  Then the overflow frame shows which sections collapse, in what order, and how the active tool stays visible even when its section is collapsed

Scenario: A tool has no distinguishable icon
  Given two icons in the same section are confusable at the smallest supported size
  Then the confusion is recorded as a defect and resolved before sign-off
  And the resolution is verified by a 5-participant icon-recognition check
```

## Technical notes / design
The rail is chrome, not content: it uses `color.surface.raised` and must recede visually so the canvas dominates. Icon strokes align to the same grid as the rest of the design system so the rail does not read as a foreign object next to CMP-221 ChartToolbar.

The active-tool indicator must survive the theme flip and the colour-blind simulation because a user who cannot tell which tool is armed will place a wrong object on a live chart; that is why a non-hue channel is mandatory rather than preferred.

The overflow behaviour deliberately keeps the *active* tool pinned visible - an armed tool that scrolls out of sight is the same failure as an invisible mode.

## Test plan
(1) State-matrix walk in dark, light, 125% and 200% zoom. (2) Automated contrast measurement of every icon/separator/focus-ring pair against both chart backgrounds, results pasted into the spec. (3) Colour-vision simulation pass (protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia, greyscale). (4) 5-participant unmoderated icon-recognition test: name the tool from the icon alone; anything below 4/5 recognition is redrawn. (5) Token audit - every value in the file resolves to a token. (6) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer who rebuilds one state from the spec alone.

## Security notes
The rail includes destructive controls (delete-all drawings) next to frequently used ones. The design must place delete-all outside the primary tap/click flow, give it a distinct treatment, and route it through a confirm step specified here (CMP-042 ConfirmDialog usage) - an accidental delete-all destroys server-persisted user content across every pane on that symbol. No credential, account or key data appears on this surface; the rail is RBAC-neutral (a Viewer may draw locally but, per E09's RBAC model, persistence is governed by the API, not by hiding the rail - the design must therefore not rely on rail visibility as an access control).

## Accessibility notes
Specified as a vertical `role="toolbar"` with roving tabindex; exactly one rail item is tabbable and arrows move within it. Each tool button has a stable accessible name that includes the tool name and its shortcut. The active tool carries `aria-pressed="true"` and its change is announced politely, since the canvas cannot convey mode to a screen reader. Focus-visible styling is specified explicitly and must be visible against both chart backgrounds. Targets are >=24x24 CSS px with >=44 px recommended for touch, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
Icons are specified as a sprite or inline SVG set that costs no layout work per frame; the rail must not re-render on chart frames. The spec states that hover/active feedback is CSS-only and must not trigger a canvas repaint, protecting the SCR-037 budget of >=58 fps while dragging a drawing with 200 objects present.

## Observability
The spec annotates `drawing.tool_selected` (tool id, entry method: rail click vs hotkey vs overflow menu) and `drawing.magnet_mode_changed`, both recommended by E14-D01, so that post-release we can tell which of twenty tools are actually used and which should be demoted in the rail.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Full state matrix drawn in dark and light, at 100/125/200% zoom.

title: Hi-fi design: drawing properties popover, styling & template library
body:
## Context
Every drawing in the kit is configurable, and US-DRAW-009 requires those configurations to be saveable as named templates and applied to future drawings. The properties popover is therefore not a minor detail panel: it is the surface through which a user's chart becomes *their* chart, and it is shared by twenty-plus tools whose property sets differ. Designing it once as a shared frame with per-tool extension slots is what keeps the kit coherent and keeps the engineering cost linear instead of quadratic.

This ticket delivers the hi-fi spec for the popover (SCR-037), the per-tool property schemas, and the drawing-template library, in Sprint 04 - two sprints ahead of the Sprint 06 stories.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for the **shared properties popover** (CMP-017 Popover): header with tool name and object id affordance, colour (CMP-031 ColorSwatch), line width (CMP-008 NumericStepperInput), line style, extend-left/extend-right, opacity (CMP-010 Slider) for filled shapes, snap-to-OHLC toggle, "alert when price crosses" toggle, lock and visibility toggles, `Save as default`, `Save as template...`, `Delete`.
- **Per-tool property schema table**: for each tool, which of the shared fields apply plus its extension slot - fib level list (add/remove/reorder levels, per-level colour and label format, the 0.886 case from US-DRAW-004), channel width read-out, VWAP band toggles (1/2/3 sigma) deferred visually to E14-D05, text-note content field, measure units.
- **Filled-shape legibility controls**: fill opacity and the "flatten opacity" toggle required by US-DRAW-003, with frames showing three overlapping zones before and after flattening, and the stated rule that fills must preserve candle contrast.
- **Template library** frames: save-as-template dialog (name, scope: this tool / this tool family), the template picker on the popover, apply-to-existing versus apply-to-new semantics, rename/delete, and the empty state. Per US-DRAW-009 templates are per user; the frames state that a template never crosses symbols implicitly.
- **Multi-select properties**: what the popover shows when several objects of mixed types are selected (common fields only, mixed-value indicator, bulk apply).
- States: default, edited-unsaved, invalid value, saving, save failed (offline/server error), read-only because the object is locked.
- Redlines plus `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-properties.md`.

## Out of scope
- The tool rail itself (E14-D03) and the object tree (E14-D07).
- Fib/VWAP/measure on-canvas visual language (E14-D05) and the position tool's read-out (E14-D06).
- Alert configuration depth - the popover only offers the "alert when price crosses" toggle; the alert editor belongs to E40.
- Server-side template storage design; engineering decides the persistence shape against `21-database-schema.md` section 3.8.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Shared frame covers every tool
  Given the per-tool property schema table
  When every tool in SCR-037's inventory is checked
  Then each has a defined field set, and every field is either a shared field or a declared extension slot
  And no tool requires a bespoke popover layout

Scenario: A property change is applied live and persisted on release
  Given an object is selected and its colour is changed
  Then the frames define that the canvas updates immediately, and that persistence happens on commit, with an explicit saving and save-failed state
  And the save-failed frame states that the local value is retained and retried, not silently reverted

Scenario: Overlapping zones stay legible
  Given three overlapping rectangles at default opacity over candles
  When the flatten-opacity toggle is enabled
  Then the frames show the resulting composite
  And the spec states the maximum default fill opacity that keeps candle contrast above the documented threshold

Scenario: Invalid property value
  Given a line width outside the allowed range or an empty template name
  Then the field shows an inline error with text, the save action is disabled, and the error is associated with the field for assistive technology

Scenario: Locked object is edited
  Given the selected object is locked
  Then the popover renders read-only with an explicit explanation and an unlock affordance
  And no field silently discards input
```

## Technical notes / design
The popover is a standard form (SCR-037 a11y note) and must behave like one - it is not a canvas surface. That is deliberate: it makes the entire configuration path keyboard- and screen-reader-native for free, and it is why the extension slots are specified as form rows rather than bespoke canvas widgets.

Property changes are optimistic: the canvas reflects them instantly (the engine's drawing layer re-renders independently of price/footprint), and the server write is reconciled afterwards per `26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.10. The design must therefore always have a visible answer to "did this save?" without blocking the interaction.

Templates carry style only, never geometry. The frames state this explicitly because "save as template" invites the opposite assumption.

## Test plan
(1) Schema completeness diff: every tool x every field. (2) State-matrix walk in dark/light, including saving, save-failed and locked-read-only. (3) Keyboard-only walkthrough: open popover from a selected object, traverse every field, commit, close, and confirm focus returns to the object's DOM mirror. (4) Screen-reader script for the popover including the mixed-value multi-select case. (5) Contrast check of the colour swatch set against both themes, including the selected-swatch indicator. (6) Content review of every error and empty-state string. (7) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer rebuilding the popover from the spec.

## Security notes
The text-note field (US-DRAW-006) is the only free-text input in the drawing kit and its content is persisted server-side in `drawings.geometry` and re-rendered on canvas and in the object tree. The spec states: plain text only, no HTML/markdown rendering, no auto-linkification, length-capped with the cap shown in the UI, and sanitised on both write and render - the design must not offer any affordance (rich-text toolbar, paste-as-HTML) that implies otherwise. Template names are equally user content and appear in menus, so the same plain-text rule and length cap apply. The "alert when price crosses" toggle creates a server-side object with notification side-effects; the spec notes it must respect the alert quota defined by E40 and shows the quota-exceeded state rather than failing silently.

## Accessibility notes
The popover uses the design system's dialog/popover semantics: focus moves into it on open, is trapped while open, `Esc` closes and returns focus to the originating object or tree row. Every control has a visible label, not a placeholder. Colour swatches are named by token name, not by hue, and the selected swatch carries a non-colour indicator. The mixed-value state in multi-select is conveyed in text, not only visually. Errors use `aria-describedby` association. All specified against `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 7 and 8.

## Performance notes
Property edits must repaint only the drawings layer; the spec forbids any property whose change would force a price/footprint re-render. Live-dragging the opacity slider is specified to coalesce to the engine's frame cadence rather than firing per input event, protecting the SCR-037 budget (>=58 fps with 200 drawings). The template picker is specified to render lazily since a user may accumulate many templates.

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.edited` (with the changed property key, never the note's text content), `drawing.template_saved`, `drawing.template_applied` and the save-failure event, so that template adoption and property-save reliability are measurable after release.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Shared popover frames complete for all states in dark and light.
- [ ] Per-tool property schema table complete and diffed against SCR-037's tool inventory.
- [ ] Flatten-opacity study done and a maximum default fill opacity stated with the contrast evidence.
- [ ] Template library frames complete including empty, rename, delete and apply semantics.
- [ ] Multi-select mixed-value behaviour specified.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed; focus-return behaviour defined.
- [ ] Content review of all strings completed.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-properties.md` merged; catalogue entries updated where they diverged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the Sprint 06/07 consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D02** - the interaction model and the tool inventory.
- Design-system components CMP-008, CMP-010, CMP-017, CMP-031, CMP-041 as catalogued.
- E40 alert quota semantics are referenced, not blocking; the toggle degrades to disabled-with-reason if E40 has not landed.

## Branch

## References

title: Hi-fi design: Fibonacci, anchored VWAP and measure tool visual language
body:
## Context
Most drawings are one or two strokes. Three are not: a Fibonacci retracement paints up to a dozen labelled levels across the chart, an anchored VWAP paints a curve plus up to six band lines that update on every tick, and the measure tool paints a transient ribbon with four numbers in it. Each of these puts a lot of ink over price at exactly the moment the user is trying to read price. Getting their visual language right - label placement, collision behaviour, line weight hierarchy, how much of the chart they may cover - is what separates a usable analysis tool from noise.

This ticket specifies that visual language in hi-fi for US-DRAW-004 (fib retracement/extension), US-DRAW-005 (anchored VWAP with sigma bands) and the measure tool, in Sprint 05, ahead of the Sprint 07-08 stories that build them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Fibonacci retracement & extension**: level line weight hierarchy (0/0.5/1 emphasised, intermediate levels lighter), per-level colour defaults from tokens, label content (price and percentage per US-DRAW-004) and its placement rules (left/right/inside, follow-viewport behaviour when an anchor is off-screen), label collision handling when levels compress at low price range, the inverted high-to-low drag case, and the custom level set (0.886) rendered.
- **Fibonacci time zones** frames: vertical level rendering against the time axis and its label strategy.
- **Anchored VWAP (US-DRAW-005)**: anchor marker on the anchored bar, the VWAP curve weight relative to indicator lines from E13 so the two are distinguishable, 1/2/3 sigma band strokes and optional fills, the individually-toggleable band state, the live-updating tail, and the **approximate badge** (CMP-227 EstimatedBadge) required when the anchor precedes recorded tick history.
- **Measure tool**: transient ribbon showing price delta, percentage, bar count and elapsed time; its dismissal rule; and its behaviour when dragged across a gap.
- **Density study**: each of the three rendered over a dense footprint chart at the density used in the engine benchmark, demonstrating that candles and cells remain readable; the maximum ink budget stated as a rule (e.g. maximum simultaneous labelled levels before auto-thinning).
- Dark and light frames for every above; colour-blind simulation pass for the level palette.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-fib-vwap-measure.md` with redlines and the label-collision algorithm described in words precise enough to implement.

## Out of scope
- The properties popover chrome for these tools (E14-D04 owns the shared frame; this ticket only supplies the on-canvas rendering and the extension-slot content requirements).
- Session/rolling VWAP as an indicator - that is E13's `VWAP (+session/anchored)` indicator entry; this ticket covers only the *drawing* form, though the two must be visually consistent and the spec states how.
- Pitchfork - deferred per the roadmap descoping ladder (section 12, item 3: pitchfork and fib time-zone tools may move to R2); frames are produced for fib time zones but pitchfork is explicitly marked deferred.
- Backend VWAP computation semantics - the incremental kernel is shared with US-IND-00x and is an engineering concern.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Levels stay labelled when they compress
  Given a Fibonacci retracement drawn over a narrow price range at a zoomed-out scale
  When levels come within one label height of each other
  Then the spec's collision rule produces a deterministic result (thinning, stacking or abbreviating) that is drawn as a frame
  And the 0, 0.5 and 1 levels are never the ones dropped

Scenario: VWAP is distinguishable from an indicator line
  Given an anchored VWAP drawing and an E13 EMA overlay on the same pane in the same theme
  Then the two are distinguishable by weight or style as well as colour
  And the spec states the rule that keeps them distinct as more overlays are added

Scenario: Anchor precedes recorded tick history
  Given the anchor bar is older than the recorded tick range for the symbol
  Then the approximate badge is shown on the drawing and repeated in its object-tree row and its tooltip
  And the frames show the badge's wording and its placement so it cannot be mistaken for an error state

Scenario: Ink budget is respected on a dense chart
  Given a footprint chart at benchmark density with a fib, an anchored VWAP with three bands and a measure ribbon active
  When the composite frame is reviewed
  Then candle bodies and footprint cell text remain readable against the documented contrast threshold
  And any element that fails is redesigned or placed behind the flatten-opacity control

Scenario: Inverted drag
  Given the user drags from high to low
  Then levels invert correctly, labels remain right-way-up and readable, and the frames show both orientations
```

## Technical notes / design
Label collision is specified as an algorithm, not a vibe, because the engine will implement it in the drawings layer with a text budget: all drawing labels together are one of the <=6 text draw calls per pane per frame (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.7). A design that needs unbounded labels is a design the engine cannot honour, so the spec caps simultaneous labelled levels and defines the thinning order.

The VWAP tail updates live (<=2 ms per anchored VWAP per US-DRAW-005 NFR). The design must therefore not require any per-tick text layout beyond the single value label at the tail.

The measure ribbon is transient and must never persist to the server - that is stated here because it is the one tool whose output looks like a drawing but is not one.

## Test plan
(1) Composite density frames reviewed against contrast thresholds with measured values. (2) Collision rule dry run: apply the written rule by hand to five compressed-level cases and confirm the drawn frames match. (3) Colour-vision simulation of the level palette and the band palette. (4) Side-by-side with E13 indicator overlays to confirm distinguishability. (5) Screen-reader script covering how a fib's levels and a VWAP's bands are exposed in the object tree and the data-table alternative. (6) Handoff dry run with the chart-engine engineer confirming the label budget is implementable.

## Security notes
No credentials, account data or secrets appear on these surfaces. The one integrity concern is the approximate badge on anchored VWAP: it communicates that a displayed number is derived from bar-approximated volume rather than recorded prints. Presenting an approximation as exact would mislead a trading decision, so the badge is a correctness requirement rather than a nicety - the spec forbids any state in which a fallback VWAP renders without it, and design QA (E14-D11) verifies that explicitly. Custom fib level sets are user content persisted server-side and are numeric-only with a bounded count; the spec states the bound so the UI cannot be used to persist an unbounded list.

## Accessibility notes
None of these three tools may rely on colour alone: fib levels carry numeric labels, VWAP bands are named (1/2/3 sigma) in the object tree and the tooltip, and the measure ribbon states its units in text. Each object's accessible name is specified (for example "Fibonacci retracement, 64 000 to 65 200, 7 levels"), and the per-level values are exposed through the object tree (SCR-036) and the data-table alternative (SCR-045), which are the normative accessible equivalents for canvas content. Reduced-motion users must still see the live VWAP tail update - the spec states that value updates are not animated.

## Performance notes
The spec carries three explicit budgets forward from the engine design: drawing labels share a single text draw call per pane; the anchored VWAP update is <=2 ms; and dragging any of these must not re-render the price/footprint layers. The density study doubles as the evidence that the design is inside the B8 benchmark envelope (200 drawings, drag one, <=12 ms frame, <=1 ms pick).

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.created`/`drawing.edited` payload fields for these tools (level-set id, band toggles, anchor bar time) and a `drawing.vwap_approximate_shown` event so we can measure how often users are looking at approximated VWAP and decide whether to extend tick retention.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Hi-fi frames complete for fib retracement/extension, fib time zones, anchored VWAP with bands, and the measure tool, in dark and light.
- [ ] Label-collision rule written precisely enough to implement and validated on five compressed cases.
- [ ] Density study complete with measured contrast values on a benchmark-density footprint chart.
- [ ] Approximate-badge behaviour specified and unavoidable in the fallback path.
- [ ] Distinguishability from E13 indicator overlays demonstrated.
- [ ] Chart-engine engineer has confirmed the label/text budget is implementable.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-fib-vwap-measure.md` merged; pitchfork explicitly marked deferred.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming Sprint 07-08 stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D02** interaction model, **E14-D03** rail and token baseline.
- E13 indicator visual language for the distinguishability check (reference only).

## Branch
`design/e14-fib-vwap-measure`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-004, US-DRAW-005
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-030, SCR-036, SCR-037, SCR-045
