title: Hi-fi design: long/short position tool and its send-to-ticket handoff
body:
## Context
The long/short position tool (US-DRAW-007) is the only drawing that produces numbers a user will act on with real money. Drag an entry, a stop and a target and it tells you your risk in USDT, your reward in USDT, your R:R and the position size implied by the active account profile - and then offers to open the order ticket pre-filled with all of it. That makes it a drawing in mechanics and a trading surface in consequence, and it is the reason this design ticket carries the `security` label while the rest of the drawing kit does not.

Two invariants drive the design. First, the sizing maths must be *identical* to US-PROF-002's (shared implementation, per the story's NFR) - the tool may not become a second, subtly different risk calculator. Second, when the implied risk exceeds the profile's cap, the tool must show it and disable send-to-ticket with the reason stated, rather than letting an over-risk trade flow onward.

Designed in Sprint 05, ahead of the Sprint 08-09 story that builds it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for the **long** and **short** variants: entry band, stop zone, target zone, the three drag handles, and the fill treatments that make risk-versus-reward readable at a glance without relying on red/green alone.
- **Read-out panel**: R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT, implied size in contracts and in USDT notional, entry/stop/target prices, and the account profile the sizing came from - with the primary read-out determined by E14-D01's findings and the rest secondary.
- **Drag order** frames following E14-D01's recommendation, including the intermediate states where only entry-and-stop exist and the reward side is still undefined.
- **State matrix**: default, dragging, selected, locked, risk-within-cap, **risk-exceeds-cap (error)**, no-account-profile-selected, symbol-not-tradable, stop-on-the-wrong-side-of-entry (invalid geometry), and tick/lot rounding applied (SCR-037 validation note).
- **Send-to-ticket handoff** frames: the affordance, the disabled state with its reason text, and the resulting pre-filled order ticket showing exactly which fields were populated and which the user must still confirm.
- **Multi-account context**: what the read-out shows when the active context is a trade group rather than a single account (either a stated per-account breakdown or an explicit statement that sizing shown is for the primary account only).
- Copy deck for every number label, unit and error string, reviewed for the advice boundary (R9) - the tool describes arithmetic, never a recommendation.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-position-tool.md` with redlines and the read-out field table.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket itself (E29/E30 series) - this ticket specifies only what is handed to it and what the handoff frame looks like.
- Risk-cap definition, lockouts and the kill switch (E39) - consumed here, not designed here.
- Placing an order from the drawing directly; the tool never places orders, and the design must make that impossible to misread.
- Native SL invariant enforcement (E32) - a backend guarantee, referenced in the copy but not designed here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Risk, reward and size are visible without hovering
  Given a completed long position tool on the chart
  When the frame is reviewed at default zoom and density
  Then R:R, risk in USDT, reward in USDT and implied size are all legible without any hover or click
  And each number carries its unit

Scenario: Implied risk exceeds the profile cap
  Given the dragged stop implies a loss greater than the active profile's risk cap
  Then the tool renders in its error state, the offending number is called out in text (not colour alone)
  And send-to-ticket is disabled with a reason string that names the cap and the computed value

Scenario: Invalid geometry
  Given the user drags the stop above the entry on a long
  Then the frames define whether the tool auto-flips to short or refuses with an inline explanation
  And whichever is chosen, no read-out ever displays a negative or nonsensical R:R

Scenario: No account profile is active
  Given no per-account profile is selected for the current context
  Then size is shown as unavailable with an explanation and a path to select a profile
  And send-to-ticket is disabled rather than defaulting to an assumed size

Scenario: Send to ticket pre-fills, it does not place
  Given send-to-ticket is used
  Then the frames show the order ticket opening pre-filled and unarmed
  And the spec states explicitly that no order is placed by this action under any circumstance
```

## Technical notes / design
The read-out is DOM, not canvas text: the numbers must be selectable, copyable, screen-reader readable and precisely typeset, and rendering them into the canvas would forfeit all four. The geometry (bands, handles, fills) is canvas; the panel is an anchored DOM overlay. The spec states this split because it determines the engineering shape.

Sizing values are *displayed* results of the shared US-PROF-002 implementation. The design annotates every number with its source so an implementer is never tempted to recompute locally: entry/stop/target from the drawing's anchors, tick/lot rounding from the instrument, size and risk from the profile engine.

Rounding is shown, not hidden: if lot rounding changes the implied size, the panel shows the rounded value as the operative one, because that is the number that would actually be traded.

## Test plan
(1) State-matrix walk in dark and light including every error state. (2) Number-formatting review against the product's number/locale rules for price, contracts and USDT notional, including very small and very large values. (3) Copy review against the advice boundary (R9) - no string may read as a recommendation. (4) Keyboard-only walkthrough: create by keyboard, move each handle by arrow keys with tick stepping, reach the read-out, reach send-to-ticket. (5) Screen-reader script covering the announcement of live-changing numbers during a drag (polite, coalesced - not a flood). (6) A cross-check session with the E39 risk-caps and E29 order-ticket design owners to confirm the handoff contract and the cap semantics match. (7) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer.

## Security notes
This is the drawing kit's sole safety-critical surface and is treated as such. The design forbids any path from the drawing to order placement: send-to-ticket produces an unarmed, pre-filled ticket that still passes the ticket's own validation, confirmation and arming, and the spec says so in normative language. The risk-cap error state is a *hard* gate in the design, not a warning that can be dismissed - a design that allows send-to-ticket while over cap is a design defect of the highest severity. The panel displays account-derived values (profile name, risk cap, size); it must show only the active context's account and must not enumerate other accounts a Viewer-role user cannot see, so RBAC filtering of the profile selector is stated as a requirement. Values in the read-out are display-only and never become a source of truth for the order - the ticket re-derives from the profile engine. Finally, the tool's inputs are user-dragged geometry, so the spec requires the ticket handoff to carry prices, not pixel positions, eliminating any scale-dependent mis-transfer. These items feed the E14 STRIDE session.

## Accessibility notes
Every handle is a focusable DOM-mirrored control with a name stating what it is and its current price; arrow keys move it by one tick, Shift+arrow by ten (US-DRAW-001 NFR, applied here). The read-out is a definition-list-shaped region whose values update politely and are coalesced so a drag does not flood the screen reader. Risk and reward are never distinguished by colour alone - each carries a text label and a direction word. The error state is announced when it is entered and its reason is programmatically associated with the disabled send-to-ticket control, so a screen-reader user learns why the action is unavailable. Specified against `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 7, 8.

## Performance notes
Dragging a handle recomputes size and risk on every frame; the spec requires the recomputation to be coalesced to the engine frame cadence and the DOM panel to update at no more than the documented rate, so the drag stays inside SCR-037's >=58 fps budget with 200 drawings present. The canvas geometry is part of the drawings layer and must not trigger a price/footprint re-render.

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.position_tool_created`, `drawing.position_tool_sent_to_ticket` (audit-relevant: it precedes a trading action) and `drawing.position_tool_blocked_by_cap` with the cap value and computed risk, so blocked-by-cap frequency is measurable and can inform whether caps are set sensibly.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Long and short frames complete with the full state matrix in dark and light.
- [ ] Read-out field table complete, each field annotated with its source of truth.
- [ ] Risk-exceeds-cap gate specified as hard and non-dismissible; send-to-ticket disabled with reason.
- [ ] Send-to-ticket handoff contract agreed in writing with the E29 order-ticket and E39 risk-cap design owners.
- [ ] Copy deck reviewed against the advice boundary and the number-formatting rules.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader walkthroughs passed, including live-value announcement coalescing.
- [ ] Security engineer has reviewed the surface as an input to the E14 STRIDE model.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-position-tool.md` merged; SCR-037 and US-DRAW-007 amended if anything diverged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D01** (drag order and primary read-out), **E14-D02** (interaction model).
- Sizing semantics from US-PROF-002 and risk caps from E39; order-ticket handoff shape from E29/E30 (contract agreement, not delivery).

## Branch

title: Hi-fi design: drawings branch of the object tree & cross-chart sync (SCR-036)
body:
## Context
SCR-036's object tree is described in the catalogue as "the a11y-complete alternative to manipulating canvas objects by mouse". For drawings that is not a courtesy - it is the mechanism by which the entire kit becomes operable without a pointer, and it is also the only practical way to manage a chart that has accumulated hundreds of objects (US-DRAW-008: virtualised for >=500 objects). This ticket designs the drawings branch of that tree in hi-fi, together with the cross-pane sync markers required by US-DRAW-009.

It is deliberately scoped to the drawings branch: E13 owns indicators and the tree's shell, and two epics editing one component's shell concurrently is how design systems fracture.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi frames for the **drawings branch**: group header with count, per-row content (type icon, accessible label, anchor time and price, visibility toggle, lock toggle, delete), grouping by tool type, sort order, and the selected/hovered/locked/hidden row states.
- **Bulk operations**: multi-select (shift/ctrl and a keyboard equivalent), the bulk action bar (hide, show, lock, unlock, delete, apply template), and the delete-all confirmation (CMP-042 ConfirmDialog) with its exact copy.
- **Scale frames**: 0 objects (empty state with a hint pointing at the rail), ~20 objects, and 500 objects showing the virtualised list, the group collapse behaviour and the search/filter affordance that makes 500 navigable.
- **Sync markers (US-DRAW-009)**: how a row indicates that its object is synced across panes on the same symbol versus pane-local; the per-pane sync-off case marked in the tree; and the rule - stated on the frame - that sync never crosses symbols.
- **Selection coupling**: selecting a row highlights and optionally scrolls the object into view on the canvas, and selecting on canvas reveals and focuses the row; both directions drawn.
- **Undo/redo surfacing**: where the user learns that `Ctrl+Z` restored an object (US-DRAW-008 requires all properties restored), including the toast or tree-flash treatment and its reduced-motion variant.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-object-tree-drawings.md` with redlines and the row anatomy table.

## Out of scope
- The tree shell, indicator rows and pane rows (E13).
- Alert rows in the tree (E40).
- Drawing templates management (E14-D04) beyond the "apply template" bulk action entry point.
- Motion detail (E14-D09), which this ticket references but does not specify.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every canvas action has a tree equivalent
  Given the list of actions available on a drawing on the canvas (select, move, edit properties, clone, lock, hide, delete)
  When each is looked for in the tree design
  Then every action is reachable from the tree by keyboard alone
  And any action that is not is recorded as a blocking defect and resolved before sign-off

Scenario: Five hundred objects remain navigable
  Given the 500-object frame
  Then the list is virtualised, grouped and filterable, and the frame states the keyboard path to reach an arbitrary object in a bounded number of keystrokes
  And the row height and density keep at least the documented minimum target size

Scenario: A synced object is deleted
  Given an object that is synced across two panes on the same symbol
  When it is deleted from the tree
  Then the frames define that it is removed from every pane showing that symbol, and that the action is undoable
  And the confirmation copy states the multi-pane effect

Scenario: Empty state
  Given a chart with no drawings
  Then the drawings branch shows an empty state that names the rail shortcut for creating the first drawing
  And the branch is still present and focusable rather than hidden

Scenario: A row's label is ambiguous
  Given two objects of the same type at similar anchors
  Then the row label includes enough anchor detail to distinguish them
  And the spec defines the label template per tool type
```

## Technical notes / design
Row labels are generated from a per-tool template (for example "Horizontal line at 64 010", "Trendline 12:30 63 900 to 14:05 64 420", "Fibonacci retracement, 7 levels"). The spec gives the template for every tool because these strings are simultaneously the visible label and the accessible name of the canvas object - they cannot be improvised per implementation.

The tree is DOM and virtualised; the canvas is not. The selection-coupling design must therefore tolerate the case where the selected object is outside the visible time range - the spec defines whether the chart scrolls to it, offers to, or simply marks the row as off-screen.

Sync markers reflect a per-layout, per-symbol setting (US-DRAW-009 NFR) that is owned by the sync-group UI (CMP-217, SCR-023). The tree only *reports* the state and links to where it is changed; it does not become a second place to configure sync.

## Test plan
(1) Action-parity audit: canvas actions versus tree actions, one row per action, gaps are blocking. (2) Keyboard-only walkthrough at 0, 20 and 500 objects, counting keystrokes to reach an arbitrary object. (3) Screen-reader script: tree navigation, group expansion, toggling visibility and lock, bulk selection, delete with confirmation. (4) Label-template review for every tool type, including the ambiguity case. (5) State-matrix walk in dark and light at both densities. (6) Content review of the delete-all and delete-synced confirmation strings. (7) Handoff dry run with an FE engineer.

## Security notes
The tree renders user-authored content - text-note bodies and template names - in a dense list. The spec requires these to be rendered as plain text, truncated to a stated length with the full value available via a non-activating tooltip, with no markup interpretation and no link activation, matching the sanitisation rule fixed in E14-D04. Destructive bulk actions (delete-all, delete-selected across panes) are the highest-consequence controls on this surface: each is specified behind an explicit confirmation whose copy names the count and the multi-pane effect, and the spec forbids placing them adjacent to routine toggles where a mis-click would reach them. The tree must show only objects owned by the current user, since `/drawings` is scoped per user and per symbol; the design must not imply any shared or cross-user visibility.

## Accessibility notes
This surface is the normative accessible equivalent for canvas drawings, so its requirements are stricter than usual: a real tree pattern (`role="tree"`/`treeitem`) with documented arrow-key navigation, expand/collapse and typeahead; per-row controls as separately named buttons rather than one ambiguous row click; multi-select with an explicit keyboard mechanism; the visibility and lock state conveyed in text as well as icon; and the label templates above serving as the accessible names. Deletion is announced, and undo restoration is announced politely. Verified against `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 8 and 9, and re-verified in E14-D10.

## Performance notes
Virtualisation is specified as a requirement, not an optimisation: US-DRAW-008's NFR is >=500 objects. The spec states that tree updates are batched and that a canvas drag must not re-render the tree per frame - the row's live values update on commit, not continuously - protecting both the tree's scroll smoothness and the chart's >=58 fps drag budget.

## Observability
Annotates `drawing.removed`, `drawing.visibility_toggled`, `drawing.locked`, `drawing.bulk_action` (action, count) and `drawing.tree_filtered`, so we can see whether users actually curate objects or rely on delete-all, which was an open question in E14-D01.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Drawings-branch frames complete for all row and bulk states, dark and light, both densities.
- [ ] Scale frames complete at 0, 20 and 500 objects with virtualisation, grouping and filtering shown.
- [ ] Sync markers and the sync-off case drawn; the no-cross-symbol rule stated.
- [ ] Label templates defined for every tool type.
- [ ] Action-parity audit clean - every canvas action has a keyboard-reachable tree equivalent.
- [ ] Screen-reader script written and walked; tree pattern semantics specified.
- [ ] Confirmation copy reviewed for destructive actions.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-object-tree-drawings.md` merged; SCR-036 updated where it diverged; no change made to the tree shell owned by E13 without that epic's design owner agreeing.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming story.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D02** - interaction model and the object-tree wireframes.
- E13's SCR-036 tree shell design (coordination, not delivery); CMP-217/SCR-023 sync-group semantics for the markers.

## Branch
`design/e14-object-tree-drawings`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-023, SCR-036, SCR-037
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-002, CMP-016, CMP-042, CMP-046, CMP-049, CMP-217, CMP-224
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-006, US-DRAW-008, US-DRAW-009
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 8, 9


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**

title: Design-system contribution: drawing primitives, tokens & CMP-191/CMP-223 entries
body:
## Context
E14 introduces a whole visual vocabulary that did not exist before: drawing strokes, fills, handles, anchors, selection affordances, locked treatments, snap indicators and label chips - applied consistently across twenty-plus tools and two themes. If each hi-fi ticket invents its own values, the kit will look assembled rather than designed and every later epic that draws on the chart (alerts lines, order lines, replay markers) will have nothing to inherit. This ticket folds E14's output back into the design system: new tokens, the formal catalogue entries for CMP-191 DrawingToolOverlay and CMP-223 DrawingToolbar, and the Storybook contract engineering will build against.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Token additions** proposed and reviewed with the design-system team, extending the existing `color.drawing.default` / `color.drawing.selected` pair: the drawing palette (the set of user-selectable colours, defined as tokens so themes remap them), `color.drawing.locked`, `color.drawing.handle`, `color.drawing.handle.active`, `color.drawing.snap`, fill-opacity tokens for zones, stroke-width scale, and the label-chip surface/typography tokens. Each with dark and light values and a measured contrast note.
- **Catalogue updates** to `15-component-catalogue.md`: CMP-191 (props, states, a11y contract, Storybook stories, test expectations) extended to the full tool set delivered by E14 rather than the five tools the current sketch lists, and CMP-223 updated with the rail's final grouping, overflow and magnet-mode states.
- **Handle and anchor system**: one specification of handle shape, size (>=24 px target per US-DRAW-001), hit tolerance (10 px grab, 16 px touch per the engine design), hover/active/locked treatments and the snap indicator - used identically by every tool.
- **Label chip**: the shared treatment for any text a drawing paints onto the chart (price labels, fib level labels, measure ribbon numbers, VWAP tail value), including its background, contrast rule over both chart backgrounds, and its truncation behaviour.
- **Storybook contract**: the agreed story list per component, including the keyboard-draw demo story that CMP-191 already designates a CI gate.
- A one-page "how to add a new drawing tool" note so future tools inherit the system instead of re-deriving it.

## Out of scope
- Any per-screen layout (owned by E14-D03..D07).
- Order-line and alert-line visual language (E30/E40), though this ticket must leave room for them and states how they differ from drawings.
- Engine implementation of the primitives - this is the design contract, not the code.
- Global theme changes; if a proposed token forces a theme-level change it is escalated to the design-system epic rather than made here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every value used by E14 resolves to a token
  Given the E14 hi-fi files
  When they are audited for raw colour, spacing, radius, opacity and stroke values
  Then every value resolves to an existing or newly proposed token
  And the audit result is recorded in the ticket

Scenario: Drawing colours survive both themes
  Given the proposed drawing palette
  When each colour is measured against the darkest and lightest chart backgrounds
  Then every colour meets at least 3:1 against both, or is excluded from the palette
  And the light-theme remapping is specified per token rather than computed ad hoc

Scenario: A selected object is identifiable without colour
  Given the selection and locked treatments
  When rendered in greyscale
  Then selection and lock remain identifiable by handle shape, stroke treatment or an added indicator

Scenario: A proposed token duplicates an existing one
  Given a proposed token whose value matches an existing design-system token
  Then the proposal is rejected in favour of the existing token
  And the catalogue records the alias so the intent is not lost

Scenario: Catalogue and hi-fi disagree
  Given a discrepancy between an E14 hi-fi frame and the CMP-191/CMP-223 catalogue entry
  Then the discrepancy is resolved before sign-off and the catalogue is updated
  And no engineering handoff is issued against an unresolved discrepancy
```

## Technical notes / design
The drawing palette is deliberately a *token set*, not a colour picker with arbitrary hex input. That keeps user-chosen colours theme-aware (a colour picked in dark mode must still be legible in light mode), keeps them contrast-guaranteed against chart backgrounds, and keeps stored drawings portable when the theme changes - the stored value is a token id, not a hex string, which is a persistence consequence engineering must know before `drawings.geometry` is finalised.

Handles are one system because hit-testing is one system: the engine's object index applies a 10 px grab tolerance and 16 px for touch uniformly (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.9), and a design with per-tool handle sizes would break that assumption.

The label chip exists because drawing labels compete with candles for the same pixels; a single specified treatment with a contrast guarantee is cheaper to police than per-tool judgement calls.

## Test plan
(1) Token audit across every E14 design file - zero raw values. (2) Contrast measurement of the full palette against both chart backgrounds in both themes, table recorded. (3) Greyscale and colour-vision simulation of selection, lock and snap treatments. (4) Duplicate-token check against the current Style Dictionary output. (5) Review with the design-system team and the chart-engine engineer; the latter confirms the handle/hit-tolerance spec and the token-id persistence model are implementable. (6) Storybook story list agreed and written into the catalogue entries.

## Security notes
No user data on this surface. One integrity point: because drawing colour is persisted as a token id rather than a raw value, a malformed or unknown token id arriving from storage must degrade to the default drawing colour rather than to an unstyled or invisible object - the spec states this fallback so a corrupted or hand-edited record cannot produce an invisible drawing that the user believes was deleted. The palette must also not include any colour reserved for the product's status semantics (error, warning, live-trading indicators), so a user-coloured drawing can never be mistaken for a system state or an order line.

## Accessibility notes
The contribution carries the a11y contract for both components: CMP-223's toolbar semantics with roving tabindex and `aria-pressed` active tool, and CMP-191's DOM mirroring with a focusable handle per control point and the keyboard-draw flow (activate -> `Enter` -> arrows -> `Enter`) that the catalogue already designates an explicit CI gate. Every token that conveys state has a non-colour partner treatment. The label chip specifies a minimum contrast and a minimum text size that hold at 200% zoom. Aligned with `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 5, 6, 8.

## Performance notes
The primitives are specified with the engine's budgets attached so they cannot be implemented in a way that violates them: drawing labels share a single text draw call per pane (<=6 text draw calls per pane per frame), drawings render on their own layer, and the object index must satisfy <=1 ms picking for 200 drawings plus 50 order lines. The handle specification explicitly avoids per-handle text and per-handle shadows, which are the two treatments that would break the batching.

## Observability
Not an instrumented surface. The contribution does specify that the Storybook stories double as the visual-regression baseline set, which is the mechanism by which drift in these primitives is detected after release.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Token proposals reviewed and accepted by the design-system team; dark and light values with measured contrast recorded.
- [ ] `15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-191 and CMP-223 entries updated to the full E14 scope.
- [ ] Handle/anchor/snap system and label-chip treatment specified once and referenced by every E14 hi-fi file.
- [ ] Token audit across all E14 design files clean.
- [ ] Duplicate-token check clean; aliases recorded where applicable.
- [ ] Chart-engine engineer has confirmed the handle, batching and token-id persistence implications.
- [ ] Storybook story lists agreed, including the keyboard-draw CI-gate story.
- [ ] "How to add a new drawing tool" note merged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming stories.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D03**, **E14-D04** - the hi-fi surfaces whose values this contribution normalises.
- Design-system tokens and Style Dictionary pipeline per `16-design-system-brief.md` section 11.

## Branch

title: Motion spec: drawing creation, selection, snap feedback and undo
body:
## Context
Motion on a trading chart is a liability unless it is doing work. Every animated pixel competes for the same frame budget as the candles, the footprint cells and the DOM heatmap, and every animation that outlasts a user's intent makes a precision tool feel imprecise. At the same time, three moments in the drawing kit genuinely need motion to be comprehensible: the snap feedback that tells you an anchor has latched onto an OHLC value, the selection feedback that tells you which of several overlapping objects you grabbed, and the undo restoration that tells you *what* came back.

This ticket specifies motion for exactly those moments and explicitly forbids it everywhere else in the kit.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec for: tool arm/disarm (rail feedback), in-progress drawing rubber-band, **snap latch feedback** (magnet weak/strong), selection and deselection, handle hover/grab, lock/unlock, hide/show, delete, **undo restore**, properties-popover open/close, and the object-tree row reveal when selection is coupled from the canvas.
- For each: duration, easing token, the property animated, and the explicit statement of whether it runs on the canvas layer or in DOM.
- A **do-not-animate list**: price-anchored geometry never eases to a new position (it would misrepresent where the object is), live VWAP values never count up, drag never has inertia, and nothing in the kit animates during an active drag except the snap indicator.
- **Reduced-motion variants** for every entry, each of which must still convey the same information by a non-motion channel (state change, outline, or a static indicator) - not merely "animation removed".
- Prototypes for the three information-bearing moments (snap, selection, undo) so they can be judged in time rather than as frames.
- `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-motion.md`, referencing the motion tokens in `16-design-system-brief.md`.

## Out of scope
- Chart pan/zoom/kinetic-scroll motion (E11 engine core).
- Order-line and alert animations (E30/E40).
- Loading and skeleton motion for the drawings fetch - covered by the design system's standard patterns.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every animation earns its place
  Given the motion spec
  When each entry is reviewed
  Then it states the information the motion conveys and why a static treatment would be worse
  And any entry that cannot answer is removed

Scenario: Reduced motion preserves meaning
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When snap, selection and undo restore occur
  Then each is still unambiguously perceivable through a non-motion channel
  And the spec names that channel per entry

Scenario: Motion never runs during a drag
  Given an object is being dragged
  When the frame-by-frame behaviour is reviewed
  Then no easing or transition is applied to the dragged geometry
  And only the snap indicator may animate, within its stated budget

Scenario: A specified animation exceeds the frame budget
  Given a prototype measured on the reference machine at benchmark chart density
  When the animation causes any frame to exceed the engine's budget
  Then the animation is shortened, simplified or removed before sign-off
  And the measurement is recorded in the spec

Scenario: Anchored geometry is asked to animate
  Given a proposal to ease a drawing into a new position after an undo or a scale change
  Then it is rejected by the do-not-animate rule and the rationale is recorded
```

## Technical notes / design
Snap feedback is the one animation that runs *during* interaction, so it is specified to the tightest budget in the kit: a short, single-property indicator change on the drawings layer, no new text, no new draw call. Everything else is either pre-interaction (arm) or post-interaction (select, undo, popover).

Canvas-layer motion and DOM motion are specified separately because they are implemented differently and have different costs: DOM transitions on the popover and the tree cost nothing per chart frame, canvas motion costs a repaint of the drawings layer. The spec labels every entry accordingly so engineering can see the cost before building.

Undo restore is the one place where motion carries real information - after `Ctrl+Z` the user needs to know *which* object returned, especially on a chart with many. The spec pairs a brief canvas emphasis with the object-tree row highlight so the answer is available on both surfaces.

## Test plan
(1) Prototype review of snap, selection and undo in motion, on the reference machine, at benchmark chart density. (2) Frame-time measurement of each canvas-layer animation with 200 drawings present; results recorded. (3) Reduced-motion walkthrough of every entry confirming the non-motion channel exists. (4) A short comprehension check with 3 participants: after an undo, can they name which object returned. (5) Review with the chart-engine engineer that each canvas entry fits the layer and draw-call model.

## Security notes
Motion carries no data, but it can mislead. The spec forbids any animation that implies a state the system has not reached - most concretely, a drawing must not animate into existence before its server write is acknowledged in a way that implies persistence, and a delete must not animate away before the delete is accepted unless the design also specifies the failure-restore path. This matters because drawings are server-persisted per user and a user who believes a level was saved will trade against it.

## Accessibility notes
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured for every entry, and the reduced variant must preserve information rather than simply omitting it - this is the WCAG 2.2 requirement that E14-D10 re-verifies. No animation flashes more than three times per second. Motion is never the sole indicator of a state change: every animated transition has a corresponding static end state and, where the change matters to a screen-reader user (selection, restore, delete), a polite announcement specified alongside. Per `05-accessibility-standard.md` sections 6 and 7.

## Performance notes
The governing budgets are the engine's: <=12 ms frame while dragging one of 200 drawings (benchmark B8) and >=58 fps for SCR-037's drag target. Every canvas-layer animation is measured against them rather than assumed to be cheap, and each entry in the spec carries its measured cost. DOM-layer entries state that they must not trigger layout on the chart container.

## Observability
Not instrumented directly. The spec notes that the diagnostics overlay (SCR-046) is the tool used to verify in production builds that drawing interactions are not costing frames, and that any regression shows up as dropped frames there.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Motion spec complete with duration, easing token, property and layer for every entry.
- [ ] Do-not-animate list written and agreed with the chart-engine engineer.
- [ ] Reduced-motion variant specified for every entry with its non-motion information channel named.
- [ ] Prototypes for snap, selection and undo reviewed in motion and measured at benchmark density.
- [ ] Comprehension check on undo restore passed with 3 participants.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-drawing-motion.md` merged and referenced from the E14 hi-fi specs.

title: Accessibility design review & keyboard-draw screen-reader script for E14
body:
## Context
Drawing tools are the hardest accessibility problem in the product. Every other surface is DOM; this one asks a user to place geometry on a canvas with a pointer, which is precisely the interaction pattern WCAG's dragging-movements and pointer-gestures criteria exist to constrain. The catalogue has already committed to the answer - CMP-191 DOM-mirrors every object with a focusable handle per control point and defines a keyboard-draw flow that the component's own test list marks an **explicit CI gate**, while SCR-036's object tree is declared the accessible equivalent for manipulating canvas objects. This ticket is where those commitments are checked as a whole, before engineering builds against them, rather than discovered to be incomplete during design QA.

It runs in Sprint 05, one sprint before the first FE story, as the gate on the whole E14 design set.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Cross-surface a11y review** of E14-D03..D07 against `05-accessibility-standard.md`: rail, popover, on-canvas tools, position tool, object tree - one review, because the failures in this epic are seams between surfaces, not defects inside them.
- **Focus-continuity map**: where focus lives and where it goes for every transition - arming a tool from the rail, placing anchors, committing, selecting an object on canvas, opening the popover, closing it, deleting an object, undoing a delete, jumping from the object tree to the canvas and back, and entering the drawing flow from SCR-045's data-table grid.
- **Screen-reader script** covering: arm a trendline by keyboard, place both anchors, commit; nudge a horizontal line by tick and by ten ticks; change a colour via the popover; lock an object; find and delete an object from the tree; undo that delete; read a fib's levels and a VWAP's bands; read the position tool's risk read-out. Written for NVDA and VoiceOver, with expected announcements at every step so it is a pass/fail script, not a walkthrough.
- **Announcement vocabulary**: the exact strings for mode changes (armed tool), anchor placement, snap latch, commit, selection, lock/hide, delete and undo - agreed once so three implementations do not invent three vocabularies.
- **Target-size and tolerance audit**: handles >=24 px, the 10 px grab / 16 px touch tolerances, rail buttons, tree row controls, popover controls - each measured against the standard at 100% and 200% zoom.
- **Criterion mapping**: each relevant WCAG 2.2 AA criterion (notably 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7/2.4.11 Focus Appearance, 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size, 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value, 4.1.3 Status Messages) mapped to the specific E14 surface that satisfies it and the artefact that proves it.
- Findings tracked to closure against the owning design ticket; `docs/design/specs/e14-a11y-review.md` merged.

## Out of scope
- Implementation or automated-test authoring - the script is executed against the built app in E14-D11 and by QA in the engineering chunk.
- The chart canvas's own a11y layer (E11's DOM-mirror and data cursor) and SCR-045's grid (E11/E12) - consumed and referenced here, not designed.
- Indicator rows in SCR-036 (E13).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every drawing tool is creatable without a pointer
  Given the keyboard-draw flow specified in CMP-191
  When each tool in SCR-037's inventory is walked through creation using only the keyboard
  Then every tool has a complete, defined keyboard path from arming to commit
  And any tool that does not is a blocking finding against its owning design ticket

Scenario: No function requires dragging
  Given WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.5.7 Dragging Movements
  When every drag interaction in E14 is enumerated (create, move, resize, position-tool handles, opacity slider)
  Then each has a documented single-pointer and keyboard alternative
  And the alternative is drawn in an E14 design artefact, not merely asserted

Scenario: Focus is never lost
  Given the focus-continuity map
  When each transition is walked
  Then focus has a defined destination at every step, including after an object is deleted and after an undo restores it
  And no transition leaves focus on a removed element or on the document body

Scenario: A status change is announced
  Given a tool is armed, an anchor snaps, an object is deleted and an undo restores it
  Then each has a specified announcement with agreed wording and an agreed politeness level
  And the announcements are coalesced so a drag cannot flood the screen reader

Scenario: A criterion has no owning surface
  Given the WCAG criterion map
  When a criterion has no artefact proving it
  Then it is recorded as a blocking gap and assigned to the owning design ticket before E14 design sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
The review treats the object tree and the canvas as one system with two front ends, because that is what the catalogue promises. The practical consequence is a parity rule: any action available on the canvas must exist in the tree, and any object visible on the canvas must appear in the tree. Parity is checked here as a matrix, not sampled.

The announcement vocabulary is fixed in this ticket rather than in each hi-fi ticket because announcements are the only way a screen-reader user perceives modal state on a canvas, and inconsistent phrasing across tools is indistinguishable from a bug.

The keyboard-draw flow leans on the engine's keyboard crosshair (`26-chart-engine-design.md` section 3.11, arrow-key bar/price stepping). The review confirms the drawing flow's key bindings do not collide with the crosshair's or with SCR-030's existing chart gestures.

## Test plan
(1) Criterion-by-criterion map with the proving artefact named for each. (2) Tool-by-tool keyboard-creation walkthrough (full inventory, not a sample). (3) Focus-continuity walk of every transition. (4) Target-size measurement at 100% and 200% zoom. (5) Screen-reader script dry-run against the prototypes with NVDA and VoiceOver, recording actual versus expected announcements. (6) Parity matrix: canvas actions versus tree actions. (7) Findings triaged with owners and re-checked at closure.

## Security notes
The review confirms that the accessible surfaces do not leak more than the visual ones: the object tree and any announcement must expose only the current user's drawings, and the position tool's announced read-out must not name accounts outside the active RBAC context. It also confirms that text-note content is announced as plain text with no markup interpretation, consistent with the sanitisation rule fixed in E14-D04 - an accessible name is another rendering surface and is subject to the same rule.

## Accessibility notes
This ticket *is* the accessibility deliverable for the epic and produces one of the two evidences the Epic DoD requires (the manual one; axe-core CI is the automated one). The standard applied is `05-accessibility-standard.md` in full, with particular weight on 2.5.1, 2.5.7 and 2.5.8 because a drawing kit is the canonical case those criteria were written for. The screen-reader script produced here is reused verbatim by E14-D11 against the built app and by QA in the engineering chunk, so it is written as an executable pass/fail artefact.

## Performance notes
The review checks that the accessible mirror is not a performance trap: CMP-191 DOM-mirrors every object with a handle per control point, which at 500 objects is a large DOM. The review confirms the design's mirroring is windowed to visible/nearby objects (consistent with E11's windowed DOM-mirror a11y layer) and that announcements are coalesced, so the a11y layer cannot be the thing that breaks the >=58 fps drag budget.

## Observability
Recommends that the keyboard-draw path emit a distinguishable entry-method value on `drawing.created` (rail/hotkey/keyboard-flow), so post-release we can tell whether the keyboard path is actually usable in practice or merely present.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 AA criterion map complete with a proving artefact named for every relevant criterion; no unassigned gaps.
- [ ] Keyboard-creation path verified for every tool in the SCR-037 inventory.
- [ ] Focus-continuity map merged; every transition has a destination.
- [ ] Announcement vocabulary agreed and written into the E14 specs.
- [ ] Target-size and tolerance audit passed at 100% and 200% zoom.
- [ ] Canvas-versus-tree parity matrix clean.
- [ ] NVDA and VoiceOver dry-runs executed against the prototypes; script finalised as a pass/fail artefact.
- [ ] All findings closed against their owning design tickets, or accepted with a recorded CDO/Architect waiver.
- [ ] `docs/design/specs/e14-a11y-review.md` merged.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done) before the Sprint 06 FE stories begin.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D03, E14-D04, E14-D05, E14-D06, E14-D07** - the full hi-fi set under review.
- E11's DOM-mirror a11y layer and keyboard crosshair, and SCR-045's data-table grid, as consumed context.

title: Design QA of the built drawing tools, object tree and position tool
body:
## Context
Design QA is the gate that decides whether what shipped is what was designed. For E14 it is unusually load-bearing, because most of this epic's output is drawn by a WebGL engine rather than composed from DOM components - which means the design system's normal safety net (shared components carrying the tokens) does not apply to the on-canvas half of the work. Stroke weights, handle sizes, label chips, fill opacities and snap indicators are all re-implemented in shader and geometry code, and every one of them can drift silently.

This pass runs in Sprint 09, after the E14 stories have landed and been deployed to a testable build, and it verifies the built app against E14-D03..D10.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Mechanical token diff** for the DOM surfaces (rail, popover, object tree): computed styles compared against the Style Dictionary output rather than judged by eye, so near-miss values are caught.
- **Canvas fidelity pass** for the on-canvas surfaces: measured screenshots compared against the redlines for stroke weights, handle size and hit tolerance, fill opacity, label-chip contrast and the snap indicator - measured in pixels at 1x and 2x DPI, both themes.
- **State-matrix walk** across every state specified in E14-D03..D07 in dark, light, at 100/125/200% zoom: tool states, magnet modes, selection/lock/hidden, popover saving/failed/read-only, position-tool error states, tree at 0/20/500 objects.
- **Copy diff** of every string against the E14 decks, with the position tool's advice-boundary wording and the anchored-VWAP approximate badge checked specifically.
- **Interaction-model conformance**: the state machine from E14-D02 walked tool by tool in the real build - arm, place, cancel with `Esc`, commit, select, move, nudge, clone, lock, hide, delete, undo, redo - with every undefined or divergent transition logged as a defect.
- **Accessibility re-run**: the E14-D10 screen-reader script executed verbatim against the build on NVDA and VoiceOver, plus confirmation that axe-core CI covers the DOM surfaces and is green.
- **Motion pass** including the reduced-motion variants and the do-not-animate list from E14-D09.
- **Performance measurement** against the stated budgets on the reference machine.
- Defect log kept with the ticket; every entry a real ticket with an owner and a priority, not a spreadsheet row.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of persistence, sync and undo semantics - QA's black-box plan in the engineering chunk owns that; design QA reports what it happens to see but does not duplicate the coverage.
- Backend `/drawings` API behaviour.
- Re-opening design decisions: a divergence is either a build defect or an accepted amendment to the spec, never a redesign inside this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Canvas rendering matches the redlines
  Given the on-canvas drawing primitives in the built app at 1x and 2x DPI
  When stroke weight, handle size, fill opacity and label-chip contrast are measured
  Then each is within the tolerance stated in the E14-D08 specification
  And every out-of-tolerance value is logged as a defect with an owner

Scenario: A token has drifted on a DOM surface
  Given the computed styles of the rail, popover and object tree
  When they are diffed against the Style Dictionary output
  Then any value not resolving to the specified token is a defect
  And near-miss values are treated identically to obvious ones

Scenario: The keyboard-draw path works in the build
  Given the E14-D10 screen-reader script
  When it is executed verbatim on NVDA and on VoiceOver against the deployed build
  Then every step's actual announcement is recorded against its expected announcement
  And any missing or incorrect announcement is a blocking defect

Scenario: A performance budget is missed
  Given a chart with 200 drawings on the reference machine
  When one drawing is dragged
  Then the measured frame rate and frame time are recorded against the >=58 fps / <=12 ms budgets
  And a missed budget is filed as a defect with an owner, not recorded as an observation

Scenario: Approximate VWAP renders without its badge
  Given an anchored VWAP whose anchor precedes recorded tick history
  When the built drawing is inspected
  Then the approximate badge is present on the canvas, in the tooltip and in the object-tree row
  And its absence anywhere is a P1 defect, because it presents an approximation as exact
```

## Technical notes / design
The pass runs against a deployed build on the target browsers and in the Electron shell, not against Storybook alone: the seams this epic fails at - focus returning from the popover to a canvas object, the tree revealing an off-screen object, a drag not re-rendering the price layer - exist only in the integrated app.

Canvas fidelity is measured, not eyeballed. Screenshots are taken at fixed zoom and DPI with a known fixture so the same measurement can be repeated in later releases as a regression baseline.

The defect log's entries are tickets. A design-QA finding that lives only in a document is a finding that does not get fixed.

## Test plan
Structured pass in this order, each step recorded pass/fail with evidence: (1) mechanical token diff on DOM surfaces; (2) canvas fidelity measurement at 1x/2x, dark and light; (3) state-matrix walk at three zoom levels; (4) copy diff; (5) interaction-model conformance walk per tool; (6) focus-continuity walk from E14-D10's map; (7) screen-reader script re-run on NVDA and VoiceOver; (8) axe-core coverage confirmation on the DOM surfaces; (9) motion and reduced-motion pass; (10) performance measurement with the 200-drawing fixture.

## Security notes
Three checks in this pass are security checks rather than cosmetic ones, and findings in this class are escalated to the Security engineer immediately rather than queued. First, the position tool: verify in the build that send-to-ticket never places an order, that it opens the ticket unarmed, and that it is genuinely disabled - not merely styled as disabled - when implied risk exceeds the profile cap. Second, text notes and template names: verify that markup pasted into a note is rendered as literal text on the canvas, in the tooltip, in the object-tree row and in the accessible name, and that no link is auto-activated. Third, scope: verify that the drawings list and the object tree show only the current user's objects and that no other account's profile data appears in the position tool's read-out for a Manager or Viewer role.

## Accessibility notes
The E14-D10 script re-run against the build is the manual evidence the Epic DoD requires, paired with a green axe-core CI run on the DOM surfaces. Any regression against the focus-continuity map is a blocker, as is any tool whose keyboard-creation path is incomplete in the build - CMP-191 already designates the keyboard-draw interaction test an explicit CI gate, and this pass confirms that gate is genuinely exercising the shipped flow rather than a simplified harness.

## Performance notes
Measured on the reference machine with the 200-drawing benchmark fixture: drag one drawing at >=58 fps with <=12 ms frame time and <=1 ms picking (SCR-037 budget; `26-chart-engine-design.md` B8); property edits and popover interactions cause no price/footprint re-render; the object tree scrolls without jank at 500 objects; the anchored VWAP update stays <=2 ms. Each measurement is recorded in the ticket and becomes the baseline for later regression checks.

## Observability
Verifies that the analytics events annotated on the designs are actually emitted with the expected keys and payloads - `drawing.created` (with entry method), `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`, `drawing.tool_selected`, `drawing.magnet_mode_changed`, `drawing.position_tool_blocked_by_cap` - and that no event carries the body text of a user's note. Cheap to check here, expensive to retrofit after release.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All ten pass steps executed with recorded evidence.
- [ ] Defect log complete; every entry classified, ticketed and owned.
- [ ] Canvas fidelity measurements recorded and within tolerance, or defects filed.
- [ ] Screen-reader script re-run on NVDA and VoiceOver; axe-core green on the DOM surfaces.

title: Engineering handoff pack for the drawing-tools band
body:
## Context
The E14 design set spans seven hi-fi tickets, a design-system contribution, a motion spec and an accessibility review, and it will be consumed by frontend and chart-engine engineers across four sprints (06-09). Without a single assembled entry point, each story starts with an archaeology exercise across Figma pages and spec files, and each engineer resolves the same ambiguities differently. The handoff pack is the artefact that makes the design set *usable*: one index, one set of redlines, one asset export, one contract per component, and one list of the decisions that are deliberately open.

It is produced in Sprint 05 so that it exists before the first consuming story is pulled in Sprint 06, satisfying the design-ahead rule with the pack itself rather than only with the underlying decks.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Index**: every E14 design artefact - Figma pages, spec documents, prototypes - mapped to the stories and components that consume it (US-DRAW-001..009, SCR-036, SCR-037, CMP-191, CMP-223), so an engineer picking up a story reaches the right frame in one hop.
- **Redline bundle**: measurements, spacing, token references and state definitions for the rail, the popover, the object-tree drawings branch, and the on-canvas primitives (handles, strokes, fills, label chips, snap indicator) - with the canvas primitives given in device-independent pixels and with their hit tolerances, since the engine cannot infer them from a frame.
- **Asset export**: the complete tool icon set in the agreed format and grid, plus any canvas glyphs, named to the convention engineering uses.
- **Component contracts**: the final prop/state tables for CMP-191 and CMP-223 as agreed in E14-D08, the Storybook story list per component (including the keyboard-draw CI-gate story), and the accessible-name/announcement vocabulary from E14-D10.
- **Interaction-model reference**: the E14-D02 state machine, restated as the implementation contract with the gesture-collision resolutions against SCR-030.
- **Behaviour table for every tool**: anchor count, creation gesture, keyboard creation sequence, editable properties, persistence shape expectations against `drawings` (`21-database-schema.md` 3.8.3) and the `/drawings` endpoints, label template and accessible name.
- **Open-decisions register**: anything deliberately unresolved (for example pitchfork's deferral to R2 per the roadmap's descoping ladder), each with an owner and the sprint by which it must close.
- A 60-minute walkthrough session with the frontend and chart-engine engineers, recorded, with the Q&A captured back into the pack.

## Out of scope
- New design decisions - if the pack surfaces a gap, it is filed against the owning design ticket rather than resolved here.
- Backend API or schema design for `/drawings` - the pack states what the UI needs to persist, not how.
- Test authoring; the pack informs the test plans but QA and engineering own them.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: An engineer can build a surface from the pack alone
  Given a frontend engineer who has not attended the design reviews
  When they rebuild the tool rail and the properties popover using only the pack
  Then they complete both without asking a clarifying question that the pack should have answered
  And any question they do ask is added to the pack before sign-off

Scenario: Every consuming story has an entry point
  Given US-DRAW-001..009
  When each is looked up in the index
  Then it maps to specific frames, a spec section and a component contract
  And no story maps to "see the Figma file"

Scenario: Canvas primitives are specified numerically
  Given the chart-engine engineer reviewing the redline bundle
  When handle size, hit tolerance, stroke weights, fill opacities and label-chip metrics are looked for
  Then each is given as a number with its unit and DPI behaviour
  And none requires measuring a screenshot

Scenario: An open decision is discovered late
  Given a decision not recorded in the open-decisions register is found missing during implementation
  Then it is added to the register with an owner and a due sprint
  And the pack's index is updated so the next engineer does not rediscover it

Scenario: A spec and a frame disagree
  Given a conflict between the redline bundle and a hi-fi frame
  Then the pack names which artefact is normative for that element
  And the conflict is resolved in the source artefact rather than annotated around
```

## Technical notes / design
The pack names a normative source per concern, because the commonest handoff failure is two artefacts that both look authoritative: the interaction state machine is normative for behaviour, the design-system contribution is normative for values, the hi-fi frames are normative for composition, and the accessibility review is normative for names, focus and announcements. Where a frame and a spec disagree, the spec wins and the frame is corrected.

Canvas primitives get numeric treatment because the engine draws them from code, not from CSS: a stroke weight expressed as "looks like this" will be implemented three different ways across the tool kit.

The behaviour table doubles as the checklist engineering uses to know a tool is finished, which is why it includes persistence and accessible-name columns rather than only visual ones.

## Test plan
(1) Coverage diff: every story, screen and component in E14's scope has an index entry. (2) Rebuild test - an FE engineer rebuilds the rail and the popover from the pack alone; unanswered questions are defects against the pack. (3) Engine review - the chart-engine engineer confirms every canvas primitive is numerically specified and implementable within the layer and draw-call model. (4) Walkthrough session held and Q&A folded back in. (5) Link check - every reference in the pack resolves.

## Security notes
The pack carries forward, in normative language, the three security-relevant design rules of this epic so they cannot be lost in translation: text-note and template-name content is plain text, length-capped, sanitised on write and on render, and never auto-linkified on any surface including the accessible name; the position tool's send-to-ticket produces an unarmed pre-filled ticket and never places an order, and is hard-disabled when implied risk exceeds the profile cap; and drawing colour persists as a token id with a defined fallback so a malformed record cannot yield an invisible object. The pack also states that drawings are per-user, per-symbol scoped and that the UI must never imply cross-user visibility. These rules are listed as a short "must not regress" section rather than buried in the specs, and they are the same items tracked in the E14 STRIDE session.

## Accessibility notes
The pack includes the E14-D10 outputs as first-class contents, not appendices: the focus-continuity map, the announcement vocabulary, the accessible-name templates per tool, the target-size and tolerance numbers, and the pass/fail screen-reader script. The keyboard-draw flow is called out as an explicit CI gate so the team plans for it during estimation rather than treating it as polish.

## Performance notes
The pack restates the budgets engineering must design to from the first commit: drag one of 200 drawings at >=58 fps and <=12 ms frame time with <=1 ms picking; drawings on their own layer with no price/footprint re-render on drawing interactions; drawing labels within the pane's text draw-call budget; anchored-VWAP update <=2 ms; object tree virtualised for >=500 objects.

## Observability
Lists the analytics and audit events the designs assume, with their payload fields and the explicit exclusion of user note text, so instrumentation lands with the feature rather than in a follow-up.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Index complete; every US-DRAW story and both screens map to specific artefacts.
- [ ] Redline bundle complete, with canvas primitives specified numerically including hit tolerances and DPI behaviour.
- [ ] Icon and glyph assets exported and named to convention.
- [ ] Component contracts for CMP-191 and CMP-223 finalised with Storybook story lists.
- [ ] Per-tool behaviour table complete (anchors, gestures, keyboard sequence, properties, persistence, label template, accessible name).
- [ ] Open-decisions register written with owners and due sprints.
- [ ] Rebuild test passed by an FE engineer who did not attend the reviews.
- [ ] Chart-engine engineer sign-off on implementability.
- [ ] Walkthrough session held and recorded; Q&A folded into the pack.
- [ ] CDO sign-off recorded (Status Done) before the Sprint 06 FE stories begin.

## Dependencies
- **E14-D03..E14-D08** - the hi-fi set and the design-system contribution.
- **E14-D09**, **E14-D10** outputs are folded in as they complete; the pack is re-issued if either lands after the first cut.

## Branch
`design/e14-drawing-handoff-pack`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037, SCR-045
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-191, CMP-223
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-001..009
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` section 3.8.3 (`drawings`)
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`, `/drawings/{drawingId}`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` sections 3.2, 3.7, 3.9, 3.10, 14
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` section 3.1 (design-ready gate)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
2. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md + 16-design-system-brief.md (tokens, components)
3. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md (relevant sections)
4. docs/plan/20-architecture.md (apps/web module map)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- apps/web/src/routes/** (per Scope screen), apps/web/src/lib/state/**, packages/ui/** (components), apps/web/e2e/**
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

**Interfaces you must not break**
- apps/web route contracts, Zustand/Jotai store shapes consumed by other routes; named identifiers in this ticket: CMP-191, CMP-223, SCR-030, SCR-036, SCR-037, SCR-045
- Any interface named in this ticket's **Dependencies** section (consumed from an upstream ticket) or referenced by tickets this one blocks.

**Commands**
- pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test · pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web build · pnpm e2e · pnpm test:a11y
- Full local gate before opening a PR: `pnpm verify` (JS/TS) and/or `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict . && pytest` (Python), whichever this ticket's paths touch (AGENTS.md §11).

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `design/e14-drawing-handoff-pack`
- PR title: `E14-D12: Engineering handoff pack for the drawing-tools band`
- Body includes `Closes #<issue>` (placeholder — set to the tracking issue for E14-D12)
- Required reviewers: `apps/web` (@CandleViewer/frontend), plus 2 approvals total per CODEOWNERS/C-10.1
- Labels: type/design, area/charting-ui, priority/p0, design, handoff, a11y

**Done means**
- [ ] Index complete; every US-DRAW story and both screens map to specific artefacts.
- [ ] Redline bundle complete, with canvas primitives specified numerically including hit tolerances and DPI behaviour.
- [ ] Icon and glyph assets exported and named to convention.
- [ ] Component contracts for CMP-191 and CMP-223 finalised with Storybook story lists.
- [ ] Per-tool behaviour table complete (anchors, gestures, keyboard sequence, properties, persistence, label template, accessible name).
- [ ] Open-decisions register written with owners and due sprints.

**Do NOT**
- Do not ship a hover-only or drag-only interaction; every affordance needs a keyboard path (05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6).
- Do not widen this ticket's scope beyond the Scope / Deliverables and Out of scope sections above — file a new ticket instead of silently expanding.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the tracking GitHub issue for E14-D12 stating the blocking condition and the key of the ticket/decision it depends on.
- Move the issue's Status to `Blocked` in the project board; do not leave it silently `In Progress`.
- Never silently work around a failing gate (lint, test, coverage, benchmark, security scan) to make the ticket appear done — escalate per AGENTS.md §9.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.

- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).

title: Black-box test plan for the E14 drawing-tools story groups
body:
## Context
E14 delivers the whole drawing surface of the terminal: twelve-plus tools, magnet snapping, multi-select and group transform, per-drawing styling, server persistence per user and symbol, an object tree, templates and cross-pane sync. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.2 sizes it at 47 points across S07-S08, and two R1 exit criteria depend on it directly: criterion 5 ("chart state — symbol, timeframe, indicators, **drawings**, layout — survives reload, app restart and Electron relaunch with zero loss") and criterion 9 ("drawings can be created and adjusted by keyboard, and a screen-reader pass is signed off").

The E14 child tickets describe *what* to build (`E14-T01`..`E14-T04`, `E14-S01`..`E14-S10`). Nothing today tells a QA engineer how to sit in front of a staging build and declare "drawings are correct, durable and operable". `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` requires a written black-box plan per feature and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded QA sign-off non-skippable. This ticket produces that artefact, written purely against `SCR-036`, `SCR-037`, the REST contract in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and observable canvas behaviour — no knowledge of `DrawingStore` internals or the engine's hit-test index — so it survives refactors of `E14-T02`/`E14-T04`.

The defining property under test is **anchoring**: `21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 stores geometry as `{"points":[{"t","p"}]}` in chart space, never pixels, and `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings` states drawings must survive "zoom, bar-type changes and DPI changes". Almost every interesting E14 defect is an anchoring or persistence defect, so the plan is built around that.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md`, with seven executable groups mapped one-to-one onto the story groups:
  1. **Toolbar, tool selection and properties** (US-DRAW-001 partial, SCR-037, `CMP-223 DrawingToolbar`, `CMP-017 Popover`, `CMP-031 ColorSwatch`, `CMP-041 Menu`, `CMP-008 NumericStepperInput`, `CMP-022 Kbd`) — covers `E14-S10`.
  2. **Line family** (US-DRAW-001, US-DRAW-002) — horizontal line/ray, vertical line, trendline, ray, extended line, magnet-to-OHLC; covers `E14-S01`, `E14-S02`.
  3. **Zone family** (US-DRAW-003) — rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, triangle, fill opacity, flatten-opacity toggle; covers `E14-S03`.
  4. **Projection family** (US-DRAW-004, US-DRAW-005) — fib retracement/extension/time-zone with custom level sets, anchored VWAP with σ bands and the "approximate" badge; covers `E14-S04`, `E14-S05`.
  5. **Annotation and planning tools** (US-DRAW-006, US-DRAW-007) — text/note/price label with sanitisation, long/short position tool with R:R, USDT risk/reward, implied size and the send-to-ticket handoff; covers the annotation and position stories.
  6. **Object management** (US-DRAW-008) — undo/redo ≥50 ops, lock, hide, delete-all, z-order, multi-select, group transform, object tree `SCR-036` (`CMP-046 Drawer`, `CMP-049 Table`, `CMP-224 IndicatorChips`); covers `E14-T04`, `E14-T02`.
  7. **Templates, persistence and cross-chart sync** (US-DRAW-009) — style templates, per-layout vs per-symbol scope, sync groups, reload/restart durability; covers `E14-T01`, `E14-T02`.
- Per case: id `E14-TC-<group><nn>`, preconditions (named fixture symbol-day + seeded drawing set), steps, single unambiguous expected result, the `US-DRAW-*` id verified, the child ticket covered, and automation status (automated in `E14-Q02`/`E14-Q03`/`E14-Q04`, or manual-only).
- A **cross-cutting invariants section** that no single child ticket owns, executed against every tool:
  - *Anchor invariance*: zoom in/out, pan, switch linear↔log↔percent price scale, switch 1m↔1h↔1D, switch bar type time↔tick↔renko, change DPI/monitor, resize window — the drawing's `(t, p)` anchors must be unchanged in `GET /drawings` and must render over the same bars/prices.
  - *Round-trip fidelity*: create → `GET /drawings` → reload → compare geometry, style, `locked`, `visible`, `z_index`, `interval_scope` field by field.
  - *Multi-pane identity*: a symbol-scoped drawing appears in every pane showing that symbol; a `layout_id`-scoped one appears only in its pane and is marked as local in the object tree.
  - *Deletion semantics*: delete is a soft delete (`deleted_at`), disappears from every pane, is undoable, and a deleted drawing never reappears after reload.
  - *Handle ergonomics*: every grab handle has a hit area ≥24 px per US-DRAW-001 NFR, verified at 100%, 150% and 200% zoom.
- A **fixture & test-data appendix** naming the seeded sets used across all E14 QA: `draw-empty` (no drawings), `draw-mixed-24` (two of every tool, spanning a 3-day window), `draw-dense-500` (500 drawings on one symbol, for tree virtualisation and drag FPS), `draw-locked-hidden` (mixed lock/visible states), `draw-legacy-geometry` (a row whose `tool` is valid but whose geometry has an extra unknown key, for forward-compat), and `draw-hostile-text` (annotation payloads from `E14-X02`).
- A **traceability table** US-DRAW-001..009 × test cases × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, proving no story is untested.
- **Defect conventions for E14**: any case where a drawing moves relative to price/time after a view change, or where a persisted drawing is lost, is filed `priority/p0-critical` by definition — a trader treats a level as a decision record, and a silently drifted level is worse than no level.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automation: geometry conformance suite (`E14-Q02`), Playwright E2E (`E14-Q03`), contract tests (`E14-Q04`).
- Execution of perf (`E14-Q05`), chaos (`E14-Q06`) and the a11y audit (`E14-Q07`).
- Security-owned artefacts (`E14-X01`..`E14-X03`).
- Indicator behaviour (E13), layout/workspace persistence (E15), alert creation from a drawn line (E40) — referenced only at the seam.
- Order-ticket internals behind the position tool's send-to-ticket action (E29/E32); the plan verifies the handoff payload, not the ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E14 story is covered by at least one executable case
  Given the plan is merged at qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009
  Then every story id maps to at least one E14-TC case
  And every case names the child ticket it covers and its automation status

Scenario: A QA engineer can execute the plan without asking questions
  Given a fresh staging build with the seeded fixture drawing sets loaded
  When an engineer who did not write the plan executes group 4 end to end
  Then every precondition is satisfiable from the fixture appendix alone
  And each step has exactly one expected result with no interpretation needed

Scenario: Failure case - an anchoring regression is caught by the plan
  Given a build where trendline anchors are cached in pixel space after the first render
  When the anchor-invariance invariant cases are executed with a linear-to-log scale switch
  Then the case fails with observed-vs-expected anchor values quoted from GET /drawings
  And the plan's defect convention classifies it as priority/p0-critical

Scenario: Edge case - a drawing that predates recorded history
  Given an anchored VWAP whose anchor bar precedes the recorder start for the symbol
  When the projection-family cases are executed
  Then the plan requires the visible "approximate" badge and a documented fallback value
  And a missing badge is a functional failure, not a cosmetic one
```

## Technical notes / design
- The plan is markdown with one table per group; each row is a case. No prose-only cases — every case has preconditions/steps/expected.
- Anchor verification is done through the API, not the canvas: the tester reads `GET /api/v1/drawings?symbol=BTCUSDT`, records the `geometry.points` array, performs the view change, re-reads, and diffs. This keeps the check exact rather than "it looks the same".
- Handle-size checks use the browser's own devtools measurement or the engine's debug overlay (if `E14-T04` ships one); the plan states the method so results are reproducible.
- Seeded fixture sets are created by a small script that posts to `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch`, checked in under `qa/fixtures/drawings/`, so a tester can rebuild state in one command. `draw-dense-500` deliberately sits at the 500-operation `maxItems` cap of the batch endpoint so the cap itself is exercised.
- Where a tool is marked Should/Could in `11-user-stories.md` (rays, extended lines, channels, triangles, fib extension), the plan marks the case `conditional` and records the descope decision reference rather than failing the run if the tool was descoped per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying artefact: review by the E14 tech lead and the a11y specialist; a dry run of one group by an engineer who did not author it (this is scenario 2, and its result is recorded in the ticket).
- Traceability table cross-checked mechanically against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows 148-156 to catch a story the plan forgot.
- The plan is re-run in full as the regression pack input for `E14-Q08`.

## Security notes
- The plan must not embed real user ids, session tokens or Bybit credentials in preconditions; fixtures use seeded test users (`qa-owner`, `qa-manager`, `qa-viewer`) created by the harness.
- Group 5 cases for text annotations reference the hostile-input corpus owned by `E14-X02` rather than duplicating payloads, so there is one source of truth for XSS vectors.
- Cross-user isolation is *named* in the plan (a Manager must not see the Owner's drawings) but its adversarial depth belongs to `E14-X02`; the QA case is the benign one.

## Accessibility notes
- Every group carries at least one keyboard-only case: select the tool by hotkey (`Alt+T`, `Alt+H`, `Alt+F`, `Alt+R`, `Alt+M`, magnet `Ctrl+M` per SCR-037), place anchors via the keyboard drawing mode, nudge with arrows (1 tick, Shift = 10 ticks), and delete — no mouse.
- The object tree `SCR-036` is designated in the plan as *the* accessible equivalent for canvas objects, so every canvas-only operation in groups 2-6 has a paired tree-based case.
- Deep audit (screen-reader transcripts, axe-core, focus order) is `E14-Q07`; this plan only ensures no group is mouse-only.

## Performance notes
- Each group names a perf-sensitive case handed to `E14-Q05`: drag with 200 drawings on screen (SCR-037 target ≥58 fps), object tree with 500 objects (US-DRAW-008 virtualisation NFR), anchored VWAP incremental update (≤2 ms per US-DRAW-005 NFR), and the 500-op batch write.
- The plan states that perf cases are *observed* here (obvious jank is a defect) and *measured* in `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- The plan instructs testers to capture the analytics events named in SCR-037 (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) and SCR-036 (`drawing.removed`) alongside each case, so a missing event is caught as part of functional QA rather than at release.
- Failing cases must attach: the `GET /drawings` payload before and after, a screen recording, browser console output and the `X-Request-Id` of the failing REST call.

## Definition of Done
- Plan merged at `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md` with all seven groups, the invariants section, the fixture appendix and the traceability table.
- Reviewed and approved by the E14 tech lead, a QA peer and the a11y specialist.
- Dry run of one group executed by a non-author with the result recorded on this ticket.
- Every case tagged with its automation destination ticket or an explicit `manual-only` reason.
- Linked from `18-traceability-matrix.md` and from the E14 epic ticket.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T02` (DrawingStore + sync semantics), `E14-T04` (hit-test, multi-select, group transform) and `E14-S10` (toolbar + properties popover) must be at least demo-able so the plan describes real UI, not a proposal.
- Consumes the fixture harness conventions established in `E12-Q01`.

## Branch
`chore/e14-qa-test-plan`

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW (US-DRAW-001..009)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223, CMP-224, CMP-008, CMP-010, CMP-017, CMP-022, CMP-031, CMP-041, CMP-046, CMP-049
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` rows 148-156, 549-550

## Agent execution brief
