1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries)
4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

title: Geometry & persistence conformance suite for drawing anchoring
body:
## Context
The single invariant that makes drawings trustworthy is that they live in **chart space**. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3 stores `geometry` as a JSONB point list of `{t, p}`; `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings` states drawings "survive zoom, bar-type changes and DPI changes"; US-DRAW-002's NFR is blunt — "anchors stored as (timestamp, price), never pixels; log/linear scale changes must not move them".

This is exactly the class of bug that manual QA misses: a level that drifts by two pixels after a scale change looks fine in a screenshot and is catastrophic in a trade review. It is also the class of bug that a refactor of `E14-T03` (instanced line rendering) or `E14-T04` (hit-test index) reintroduces easily, because both are tempted to cache screen coordinates. This ticket builds the automated suite that makes the invariant permanent and cheap to check.

The suite is deliberately split in two layers so a failure localises: a **projection-level property suite** in the engine package (no DOM, no server — pure `(t,p) ↔ (x,y)` round-trips across scale modes) and an **integration-level golden suite** driving the real store and the real `/drawings` API against seeded fixtures.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Layer 1 — property-based projection tests** in `packages/chart-engine/test/drawings/projection.prop.test.ts`:
  - For randomly generated `(t, p)` anchors, viewports, DPRs and scale modes (`linear`, `logarithmic`, `percent`, inverted), assert `unproject(project(t, p)) ≈ (t, p)` within one device pixel, and that `project` is monotonic in both axes.
  - Assert scale-mode independence: changing the price-scale mode changes `y` but never the stored `p`.
  - Assert bar-type independence: the same `t` maps onto the bar containing it whether the series is time, tick, volume, range, delta or renko (E12 bar families), because `bar_type_binding` is null for an unbound drawing.
  - Extremes: anchors far outside the visible window, anchors at the series edge, prices near tick-size granularity, timestamps at DST-free UTC boundaries, and `p` values with full instrument precision (no float rounding to 2 dp).
- **Layer 2 — golden persistence tests** in `apps/web/test/drawings/roundtrip.test.ts` + a server-side pack in `tests/api/test_drawings_roundtrip.py`:
  - For each of the 24 tools in the `DrawingInput.tool` enum that E14 ships, create via `POST /api/v1/drawings`, read back, and assert byte-equality of `geometry`, `style`, `locked`, `visible`, `z_index`, `interval_scope`, `layout_id`, `bar_type_binding`.
  - Assert soft-delete semantics: `DELETE` sets `deleted_at`, the row vanishes from `GET`, and an undo re-creates it with identical geometry (new or restored id per `E14-T02`'s documented contract — the test asserts whichever the contract states, and fails if the contract is silent).
  - Assert `anchor_start`/`anchor_end` denormalisation matches the min/max `t` in `geometry.points` for every tool, including single-anchor tools (hline, vline, text) where one may be null.
  - Assert the batch endpoint is transactional: a 3-op batch whose second op is invalid leaves zero rows changed and returns `422`.
  - Forward-compat: `draw-legacy-geometry` (unknown extra key inside `geometry`) round-trips unchanged rather than being silently stripped.
- **View-change matrix test** (the headline): for `draw-mixed-24`, snapshot every drawing's `geometry`, then programmatically apply each of {zoom ×0.25, zoom ×8, pan 500 bars, linear→log, log→percent, inverted on, 1m→1D, time→renko, DPR 1→2, window resize}, and re-read. Any mutation of a stored anchor fails the suite with the diff.
- **CI wiring**: both layers run on every PR touching `packages/chart-engine/src/drawings/**`, `apps/web/src/drawings/**` or the `/drawings` router; the view-change matrix is a required check.

## Out of scope
- Visual rendering correctness (does the trendline look right) — that is design-QA on `E14-S02`/`E14-S03` plus the E2E screenshots in `E14-Q03`.
- FPS and drag latency — `E14-Q05`.
- REST schema conformance against the OpenAPI document — `E14-Q04` (this suite asserts *values*, that one asserts *shape*).
- Cross-user access control — `E14-X02`.
- Anchored-VWAP numerical correctness against the tape; only its anchor persistence is covered here (value correctness lives with `E14-S05`'s own unit tests).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Anchors survive every view change
  Given the draw-mixed-24 fixture is loaded on BTCUSDT
  When the view-change matrix applies all ten transformations in sequence
  Then GET /api/v1/drawings returns geometry byte-identical to the pre-change snapshot
  And no drawing's rendered position relative to its anchor bar and price has changed

Scenario: Every shipped tool round-trips losslessly
  Given one drawing of each shipped tool created via POST /api/v1/drawings
  When each is read back and compared field by field
  Then geometry, style, locked, visible, z_index, interval_scope, layout_id and bar_type_binding all match the request
  And anchor_start and anchor_end match the min and max timestamps in geometry.points

Scenario: Failure case - pixel caching is reintroduced
  Given a build where the drawings layer caches screen coordinates across a scale change
  When the projection property suite runs with mixed linear and logarithmic viewports
  Then at least one round-trip assertion fails with the generated counterexample printed
  And the CI required check blocks the merge

Scenario: Edge case - a partially invalid batch changes nothing
  Given a three-operation batch where the second operation omits geometry
  When POST /api/v1/drawings/batch is called
  Then the response is 422
  And a subsequent GET shows none of the three operations were applied
```

## Technical notes / design
- Property tests use `fast-check` on the frontend/engine side and `hypothesis` on the Python side, matching the property-based testing already mandated for engine scale math in `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4.
- Prices are compared as decimal strings, never floats — the API models `p` as a string precisely so tick precision is not lost, and the suite asserts that contract rather than working around it.
- The view-change matrix drives the engine through its public viewport API in a headless WebGL context (the harness from `E11`), not through Playwright, so it runs in seconds and can be a required PR check.
- Golden files live in `qa/fixtures/drawings/golden/` and are regenerated by an explicit `--update-golden` flag that is refused in CI, so an anchor drift can never be "fixed" by accepting a new golden without a human diff in the PR.
- The suite is written against the tool enum in `DrawingInput`; a tool present in the enum but not exercised fails a meta-test, so adding a tool later forces adding coverage.

## Test plan
- Mutation check: deliberately introduce three seeded regressions (pixel caching on scale change, `anchor_end` computed from the first rather than the last point, batch applying ops before validating all of them) on a scratch branch and confirm each is caught by a distinct assertion.
- Runtime budget: full suite under 90 s on CI hardware; the property layer capped at 500 generated cases per property with a fixed seed recorded in the run log for reproducibility.
- Flake gate: the suite runs 20× consecutively in the nightly job; any non-determinism is a blocking defect in the suite itself.

## Security notes
- Fixtures are created through the authenticated API as the seeded `qa-owner` user; the suite must never write directly to Postgres, so it exercises the same authorisation path production uses.
- Hostile geometry (enormous point arrays, deeply nested JSON, non-numeric `p`) is asserted here only for *rejection with 422*; adversarial depth and payload corpus ownership stay with `E14-X02`.
- Golden files are scrubbed of user ids and session identifiers before commit.

## Accessibility notes
- Not a UI-facing ticket, but the suite includes a case asserting every persisted drawing carries a non-empty derived accessible name (tool + anchor time + price) in the store's projection used by `SCR-036`, because a nameless object is unreachable in the tree and that is an a11y defect detectable at data level.

## Performance notes
- The suite asserts an O(n) bound indirectly: persisting `draw-dense-500` and reading it back must stay under 2 s end to end, which catches an accidental per-drawing round-trip replacing the batch path.
- Query 28 in `21-database-schema.md` §performance budgets ("drawings load per chart < 5 ms") is asserted against the seeded 500-drawing set with the partial index `ix_dr_user_symbol` in place; a missing index shows up as a failed budget rather than a silent slowdown.

## Observability
- Suite emits a JUnit XML plus a machine-readable anchor-diff report published as a CI artefact so a failure can be triaged without rerunning locally.
- The nightly run records suite duration and case count to the CI metrics dashboard alongside the E12 golden suite, making coverage erosion visible.

## Definition of Done
- Both layers merged, green, and wired as required checks on the relevant paths.
- All shipped tools covered; meta-test enforcing enum coverage in place.
- Three seeded regressions demonstrably caught (evidence linked on the ticket).
- Golden-update flag refused in CI, verified by a deliberate attempt.
- Coverage of `packages/chart-engine/src/drawings/**` at or above the 85% engine threshold from `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q01` for the invariants the suite formalises.
- `E14-T03`, `E14-T04` for the drawings layer and hit-test to exist.
- `E14-T01` for the `/drawings` endpoints; reuses the headless engine harness from `E11`.

## Branch
`test/e14-geometry-conformance`

- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3, query budget 28
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`, `DrawingInput`
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (scale modes, projection)
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (property-based testing, golden fixtures)

title: Playwright E2E: drawing lifecycle, object tree and cross-chart sync
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.4 names the R1 E2E gate explicitly: "Playwright web **and** Electron: load chart, switch symbol/timeframe, add indicator, **draw and persist a drawing**, save and restore a workspace". Exit criterion 5 adds that drawings must survive reload, app restart and Electron relaunch with zero loss. Those are E14's obligations to the release, and they can only be discharged by a browser-level test that drives the real canvas, the real store and the real server.

Drawing tools are hostile to naive E2E: the interaction surface is a WebGL canvas with no DOM nodes to click. The suite therefore leans on two stable handles that E14 already owes for other reasons — the object tree `SCR-036` (the a11y-complete alternative, per `14-screens-catalogue.md`) and the keyboard drawing mode from `E14-K01`. Where a pointer path must be exercised, it is driven by deterministic canvas-relative coordinates derived from the engine's own projection helper exposed on a test-only handle, not by hard-coded pixels.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/drawings/` Playwright specs, run in both the web and Electron projects of the existing Playwright config:
  1. **`lifecycle.spec.ts`** — for the tool set shipped by S08 (hline, vline, trendline, ray, rectangle, ellipse, parallel channel, fib retracement, anchored VWAP, text, position tool): select the tool from `CMP-223 DrawingToolbar` by hotkey, place anchors, verify the shape appears in `SCR-036`'s Drawings branch with the expected accessible name, edit a style property in the `CMP-017` properties popover, drag an anchor, delete, undo, redo.
  2. **`persistence.spec.ts`** — create a mixed set, reload the page, assert identical set; restart the Electron app, assert identical set; log in as the same user in a second context, assert identical set; verify the R1 exit-criterion-5 wording literally (zero loss of symbol, timeframe, indicators, drawings, layout).
  3. **`object-tree.spec.ts`** — `SCR-036` operations: rename, toggle visibility, toggle lock, reorder (z-order), multi-select and bulk delete, with assertions that a locked drawing cannot be moved by dragging but remains selectable, per US-DRAW-008.
  4. **`sync.spec.ts`** — US-DRAW-009: two panes on the same symbol at different intervals with level-sync on → a level drawn in one appears in the other without reload; sync off → the drawing stays local and is marked local in the tree; a second symbol's pane never receives it (the "never syncs across different symbols" NFR).
  5. **`templates.spec.ts`** — save a style as a named template, apply it, assert new drawings of that type adopt colour/width/style/label settings; assert a custom fib level set (adding 0.886) becomes the default for new fib drawings.
  6. **`position-tool.spec.ts`** — drag entry/stop/target, assert displayed R:R, USDT risk, USDT reward and implied size match the account-profile sizing maths; choose "send to ticket" and assert the ticket opens pre-filled; with risk over the profile cap, assert the error state and that the action is disabled with a stated reason.
  7. **`keyboard.spec.ts`** — a full mouse-free path: hotkey tool selection (`Alt+T`/`Alt+H`/`Alt+F`/`Alt+R`/`Alt+M`), magnet toggle `Ctrl+M`, anchor placement via the keyboard crosshair stepping with Enter to confirm, arrow-key nudge (1 tick, Shift = 10 ticks), delete, `Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Shift+Z`.
- **Test-only engine handle** (`window.__cvEngine.projectForTest(t, p)`), gated behind the E2E build flag and asserted absent in a production bundle by a dedicated test, so canvas coordinates are computed rather than hard-coded.
- **Deterministic seeding**: each spec starts from a known fixture symbol-day and a known drawing set posted through `POST /api/v1/drawings/batch` in `beforeEach`, and tears down by deleting the seeded user's drawings, so specs are order-independent and parallel-safe.
- **Visual assertions** kept deliberately narrow: masked screenshots of the toolbar and the properties popover only (stable DOM), never of the canvas — canvas pixels are compared nowhere, to avoid GPU-driver flake (`R8`).

## Out of scope
- Anchor-value invariants at data level — `E14-Q02` owns those and runs far faster.
- REST schema conformance — `E14-Q04`.
- Frame-rate and drag-latency measurement — `E14-Q05`.
- Disconnect/conflict behaviour — `E14-Q06`.
- Deep screen-reader transcripts and axe-core sweeps — `E14-Q07` (this suite proves the keyboard path exists and works; it does not judge announcement quality).
- Order placement beyond the ticket pre-fill assertion.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Draw and persist across reload and Electron relaunch
  Given a chart on BTCUSDT with no drawings
  When I create a trendline, a rectangle and a fib retracement and reload the page
  Then all three are present with identical anchors, styles and labels
  And after an Electron app relaunch they are still present and identical

Scenario: Cross-pane sync respects its scope
  Given two panes showing BTCUSDT at 1m and 1h with level-sync enabled
  When I draw a horizontal level in the 1m pane
  Then it appears in the 1h pane at the same price without a reload
  And a third pane showing ETHUSDT does not receive it

Scenario: Failure case - a locked drawing is dragged
  Given a trendline marked locked in the object tree
  When a drag is attempted on its mid-handle
  Then its geometry is unchanged in GET /api/v1/drawings
  And the drawing remains selectable and inspectable

Scenario: Edge case - the entire lifecycle with no mouse
  Given keyboard-only input in the keyboard drawing mode
  When I select the trendline tool with Alt+T, place both anchors with Enter, nudge with Shift+ArrowUp and delete
  Then each step is reflected in the object tree and in the persisted drawing set
  And Ctrl+Z restores the deleted trendline with all properties intact
```

## Technical notes / design
- Specs assert against the object tree's DOM (`role="tree"`, per SCR-036) and against `GET /api/v1/drawings` responses intercepted via Playwright's request API. Two independent oracles per assertion means a UI-only or a server-only regression is distinguishable from the trace.
- Electron coverage reuses the existing Electron Playwright project; only `persistence.spec.ts` and `lifecycle.spec.ts` run there, to keep the required-check runtime bounded — the rest run web-only, with the rationale recorded in the spec header.
- Debounced batch writes (500 ms per the `/drawings/batch` description) are awaited by waiting on the network request, never by `waitForTimeout`, so the suite does not encode the debounce constant.
- Drag interactions use `mouse.move` with intermediate steps so the engine's pointer-move handling and `E14-T04`'s hit-test are genuinely exercised rather than a single teleporting event.
- Each spec is tagged `@e14` so `E14-Q08`'s regression pack can select the whole epic's E2E set in one invocation.

## Test plan
- Determinism: the full suite runs 10× in the nightly job; any spec flaking more than once is quarantined and a fix ticket filed the same day per `03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Cross-browser: Chromium is the required check; a weekly run adds WebKit and Firefox to surface `R8` GPU/driver divergence early, with failures triaged rather than gating.
- Negative control: with `E14-T02`'s persistence deliberately stubbed out on a scratch branch, `persistence.spec.ts` must fail — proving the assertions are load-bearing.

## Security notes
- The `__cvEngine.projectForTest` handle is a deliberate test-only surface; a dedicated spec asserts it is `undefined` in a production build, and the bundler config strips it. This is recorded as a threat in `E14-X01` and its mitigation is this assertion.
- Specs authenticate through the normal login flow with seeded users; no token is written into the repo or into Playwright storage state that is committed.
- `sync.spec.ts` includes a benign isolation check (a second seeded user's drawings are not visible); the adversarial version lives in `E14-X02`.

## Accessibility notes
- `keyboard.spec.ts` is the executable proof of R1 exit criterion 9's drawing clause and is a required check, not an optional one.
- Every lifecycle assertion goes through the object tree's accessible name, so a drawing that renders but has no name fails the functional suite.
- Focus management is asserted at the coarse level: after closing the properties popover, focus returns to the invoking toolbar button; deeper focus-order review is `E14-Q07`.

## Performance notes
- The suite is not a benchmark, but it fails fast on pathological slowness: each spec has a hard 60 s budget and the seeded set is capped at 24 drawings so a timeout means a real regression, not a heavy fixture.
- `draw-dense-500` is deliberately *not* used here; it belongs to `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- Traces, videos and the intercepted `/drawings` payloads are retained for every failure as CI artefacts.
- The suite asserts the SCR-037 analytics events (`drawing.created`, `drawing.edited`, `drawing.deleted`, `drawing.cloned_to_synced_charts`) fire with the expected properties, closing the gap where analytics silently break.

## Definition of Done
- All seven specs merged and green on Chromium web and on Electron for the two designated specs.
- Wired into the PR-required E2E job for paths under `apps/web/src/drawings/**` and into the nightly full run.
- Flake rate below the `03-testing-strategy.md` threshold over 10 consecutive nightly runs.
- Negative-control demonstration evidence linked on the ticket.
- Production-bundle assertion for the test handle passing.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q01` (cases to automate), `E14-S03` and `E14-S04` (zone and projection tools exist), `E14-S10` (toolbar), `E14-K01` (keyboard pattern decided).
- Object tree surface from the E13/E14 shared `SCR-036` implementation.
- Position-tool spec additionally depends on the profile sizing implementation shared with US-PROF-002.

## Branch
`test/e14-e2e-drawings`

## References
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 5 and 9, §5.4 E2E gate
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037 (hotkeys, analytics events)

title: Contract tests for the /drawings REST surface including batch
body:
## Context
`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires interface-first contracts for every backend↔frontend story, and `03-testing-strategy.md` makes contract tests a distinct pyramid layer: the OpenAPI document is normative, and the implementation must be provably identical to it. E14 adds four operations to that document — `listDrawings`, `createDrawing`, `batchUpsertDrawings`, `updateDrawing`, `deleteDrawing` — plus the `DrawingInput`/`Drawing` schemas with a 24-value `tool` enum and a free-form `geometry` object.

The batch endpoint deserves special attention. It is the hot path (the engine debounces drag mutations at 500 ms and sends one call carrying every affected shape), it is transactional, it is capped at `maxItems: 500`, and it accepts an `Idempotency-Key`. Each of those is a contract promise that is easy to implement approximately and expensive to get wrong: a non-transactional batch corrupts a trader's chart mid-drag, and a non-idempotent retry duplicates every shape on a flaky connection.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/contract/test_drawings_contract.py` driven by the generated client / schema validator already used for the R0 contract pack:
  - **Schema conformance both ways**: every response validated against `#/components/schemas/Drawing` and `Page`; every request fixture validated against `DrawingInput` before being sent, so the tests cannot drift from the document.
  - **`additionalProperties: false` enforcement**: `DrawingInput` declares it — an unknown top-level field must yield `422`, not be silently ignored.
  - **Tool enum**: each of the 24 enum values is accepted (for shipped tools) or rejected with a documented reason (for tools descoped per `30-release-roadmap.md` §12, e.g. pitchfork/gann_fan); a value outside the enum yields `422`.
  - **Required fields**: missing `symbol`, `tool` or `geometry` → `422` with the standard error envelope.
  - **Pagination**: `GET /drawings` honours `cursor` and `limit`, returns `meta.next_cursor`/`has_more`/`count` consistently, and a cursor from a different symbol's page is rejected rather than silently reinterpreted.
  - **`layout_id` filter**: narrows to pane-scoped drawings; an unknown layout id yields `404` per the documented responses.
  - **Status-code matrix**: `201` on create, `200` on replace and batch, `204` on delete, `401` unauthenticated, `403` for a principal lacking `workspaces:write`, `404` for an unknown or soft-deleted `drawingId`, `422` for validation.
  - **RBAC annotations honoured**: `x-rbac: { permissions: [workspaces:read|write], scope: self }` is asserted behaviourally — a Viewer role can read its own and cannot write; a Manager cannot read the Owner's drawings by id.
- **Batch-specific pack**:
  - Mixed `create`/`update`/`delete` in one call applied **in order**, with the response's `created`/`updated`/`deleted` arrays matching exactly.
  - Transactionality: any single failing op rolls the whole batch back (asserted by a `GET` diff, not by trusting the response).
  - `maxItems: 500` boundary: 500 ops succeed, 501 ops yield `422` before any write.
  - `update`/`delete` without `id` → `422`; `create` with an `id` → `422`.
  - Idempotency: the same `Idempotency-Key` replayed returns the original result and creates nothing new; a different body with the same key is rejected per the platform's idempotency contract.
- **Spec-drift guard**: a CI check that diffs the live app's generated OpenAPI against `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` for the `/drawings*` paths and fails on any difference, mirroring the WS-freeze discipline in `E17`.

## Out of scope
- Value-level persistence fidelity and anchor invariants — `E14-Q02`.
- UI behaviour — `E14-Q03`.
- Load characteristics of the batch endpoint — `E14-Q05`.
- Adversarial payloads (XSS in labels, JSON bombs, IDOR fuzzing) — `E14-X02`; this pack asserts the documented rejections only.
- Database-level retention/purge of soft-deleted rows (90 d per `21-database-schema.md`) — owned by E16's lifecycle work.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The implementation matches the published contract
  Given the application's generated OpenAPI document
  When the /drawings, /drawings/batch and /drawings/{drawingId} paths are diffed against 22-api-openapi.yaml
  Then there is no difference in paths, parameters, schemas or response codes
  And the check is a required CI gate on the drawings router

Scenario: A partially invalid batch is fully rejected
  Given a batch of 3 operations where the second has op=update and no id
  When POST /api/v1/drawings/batch is called
  Then the response is 422 with the standard error envelope
  And a subsequent GET /api/v1/drawings shows none of the three operations were applied

Scenario: Failure case - an unknown field is silently accepted
  Given a DrawingInput body carrying an undeclared field "pixels"
  When POST /api/v1/drawings is called
  Then the response is 422 because DrawingInput declares additionalProperties: false
  And no row is created

Scenario: Edge case - a replayed idempotency key
  Given a 200-operation batch submitted with Idempotency-Key K that succeeded
  When the identical request is replayed with the same key after a client timeout
  Then the original response is returned
  And GET shows exactly 200 drawings, not 400
```

## Technical notes / design
- The pack runs against the real FastAPI app with a real Postgres (testcontainers), not mocks, because transactionality and the partial indexes are part of what is being asserted.
- Request fixtures are generated from the schema where possible (schema-derived example generation) so a schema change automatically widens coverage instead of silently leaving the pack behind.
- The status-code matrix is table-driven: one parametrised test over `(method, path, principal, body) → expected status`, making the RBAC rows readable next to the `x-rbac` annotations they encode.
- Soft-deleted rows must be indistinguishable from never-existing rows at the API boundary (`404`), which also avoids an enumeration oracle — this is asserted here and re-checked adversarially in `E14-X02`.
- The drift guard compares a normalised (key-sorted, example-stripped) subtree so cosmetic YAML churn does not produce false failures.

## Test plan
- Self-testing: introduce, on a scratch branch, (a) a non-transactional batch, (b) an off-by-one at the 500 cap, (c) `403` returned where `404` is documented — and confirm three distinct assertions fail.
- Runtime under 60 s including container start, so it can sit on the PR path for the drawings router.
- Contract pack runs in the same CI job as the R0 contract tests to keep one reporting surface.

## Security notes
- RBAC assertions are functional contract checks here and adversarial cases in `E14-X02`; both exist because `04-security-program.md` treats broken object-level authorisation as a top-tier risk and `scope: self` is the only thing standing between users' private chart annotations.
- The pack asserts error bodies never echo another user's data, a row id that was not supplied, or a stack trace.
- `Idempotency-Key` handling is asserted not to leak across principals: the same key used by a different user must not return the first user's result.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A for the API surface itself. The one a11y-relevant contract assertion kept here: `label` is returned verbatim so the client can derive an accessible name; a server that trims or normalises `label` would break `SCR-036` naming, so round-trip equality of `label` is asserted.

## Performance notes
- Not a load test, but the pack asserts the `GET /drawings?symbol=` path uses the partial index by checking the query plan in a debug-mode assertion against budget 28 (< 5 ms) from `21-database-schema.md` §performance.
- A 500-op batch must complete within 1 s locally as a smoke bound; the real profile is `E14-Q05`.

## Observability
- Every request in the pack carries an `X-Request-Id`; failures attach the correlated server log lines, so a contract failure is triageable from the CI artefact alone.
- The drift guard publishes the normalised diff as an artefact when it fails, so the reviewer sees exactly which promise moved.

## Definition of Done
- Contract pack merged and green; drift guard wired as a required check on `apps/api/**/drawings*`.
- Status-code and RBAC matrix complete for all five operations.
- Batch transactionality, cap and idempotency all asserted.
- Seeded-regression evidence linked on the ticket.
- Backend coverage for the drawings router at or above the 85% threshold.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T01` (migration + endpoints). Reuses the contract-test harness and idempotency conventions established in R0.

## Branch
`test/e14-drawings-contract`

## References
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/drawings`, `/drawings/batch`, `/drawings/{drawingId}`, `DrawingInput`, `Drawing`, `Page`, `IdempotencyKey`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.8.3, migration `0011_workspace`, query budget 28, retention row for soft-deleted config rows
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 interface-first, §4
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (contract layer)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` (object-level authorisation)

title: Performance pack: drag FPS with 200 drawings, dense tree and batch write load
body:
## Context
Drawings are the most common way a user makes the chart slow. `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 sets the budget explicitly: "drawings render on a separate canvas layer above the price layer; dragging a drawing must not re-render the price/footprint layers (target: drag at >=58 fps with 200 drawings on the chart)". `30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 2 adds the floor for the worst case: 30 fps with a 6-chart layout, all indicators and **all drawings**, using the documented degradation ladder — and trading-critical overlays must never be the thing shed. US-DRAW-005 pins an additional numeric budget (anchored VWAP incremental update ≤2 ms) and US-DRAW-008 pins a structural one (object tree virtualised for ≥500 objects).

Those numbers exist in prose. This ticket turns them into scripts that run, record and fail. It is the E14 contribution to the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` regime and to risk `R2 Render performance`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Engine benchmarks** in `packages/chart-engine/bench/drawings/`, run on the existing seeded-dataset harness from E11:
  1. `drag-200.bench.ts` — 200 mixed drawings on a 100k-bar series; scripted drag of one trendline across 600 frames; records p50/p95/p99 frame time and asserts p95 ≤ 17.2 ms (58 fps) on reference hardware.
  2. `layer-isolation.bench.ts` — asserts the price/footprint layers issue **zero** draw calls during a drawing-only drag, using the engine's render-pass counters. This is the structural guarantee behind the FPS number; if it breaks, the FPS number is luck.
  3. `hit-test.bench.ts` — `E14-T04`'s index queried at pointer-move rate against 500 drawings; asserts p95 query ≤ 0.5 ms and that cost is sub-linear in object count (500 objects must not cost 10× the 50-object case).
  4. `avwap-incremental.bench.ts` — anchored VWAP with σ bands updated tick-by-tick over a recorded dense fixture; asserts ≤2 ms per update per anchored VWAP and asserts the update cost is independent of the distance from the anchor (i.e. genuinely incremental, not a re-scan).
  5. `worst-case-ladder.bench.ts` — the roadmap's worst case: 6 panes, full R1 indicator set, `draw-dense-500`; asserts the 30 fps floor holds and records which degradation-ladder rungs engaged, asserting drawings and trading-critical overlays are not shed before decorative work.
- **Frontend/DOM benchmarks**:
  6. `object-tree.bench.ts` — `SCR-036` with 500 objects: initial render, scroll, filter, multi-select-all and bulk-delete; asserts virtualisation (DOM node count bounded, not 500) and interaction latency p95 ≤ 100 ms.
- **API load scripts** in `load/k6/drawings/`:
  7. `batch-write.js` — sustained drag-like traffic: N virtual users each posting a 50-op `POST /drawings/batch` every 500 ms for 10 minutes; asserts p95 server time and that Postgres write amplification stays bounded; includes a 500-op max-size scenario.
  8. `list-read.js` — `GET /drawings?symbol=` against a user with 500 drawings; asserts budget 28 from `21-database-schema.md` (< 5 ms query) and p95 API latency within the `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` REST budget.
- **Reporting**: all results written to the standard benchmark JSON consumed by the CI perf dashboard; the drag and layer-isolation benchmarks are wired as **required checks** with the roadmap's >10% regression rule failing the build.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of what is drawn — `E14-Q02`, `E14-Q03`.
- Chaos/failure behaviour under load (disconnects mid-batch) — `E14-Q06`.
- Whole-application perf hardening — E46.
- Footprint/heatmap render budgets — E18/E21 own theirs; only their *coexistence* with drawings is exercised in the worst-case ladder.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Drag stays above the SCR-037 budget
  Given 200 mixed drawings on a 100k-bar BTCUSDT series on reference hardware
  When a trendline anchor is dragged across 600 scripted frames
  Then p95 frame time is at most 17.2 ms
  And the price and footprint layers issue zero draw calls during the drag

Scenario: Anchored VWAP updates incrementally
  Given an anchored VWAP with three standard-deviation bands anchored 50 000 prints back
  When 10 000 further prints are applied one at a time
  Then each update completes within 2 ms
  And the per-update cost does not grow with distance from the anchor

Scenario: Failure case - a regression exceeds the tolerance
  Given a change that makes the drawings layer re-upload all geometry each frame
  When drag-200.bench.ts runs in CI
  Then p95 frame time exceeds the budget by more than 10 percent
  And the required perf check fails the pull request with the before and after numbers

Scenario: Edge case - worst case falls back gracefully, not arbitrarily
  Given a 6-pane layout with the full R1 indicator set and 500 drawings
  When the worst-case ladder benchmark runs
  Then frame rate never drops below 30 fps
  And the engaged degradation rungs exclude drawings and trading-critical overlays
```

## Technical notes / design
- "Reference hardware" is the machine class already defined for the E11 benchmark harness; results from any other machine are recorded but never gate, to keep the gate meaningful.
- Frame timings come from the engine's own instrumentation (a monotonic per-frame timer around the render-pass scheduler), not `requestAnimationFrame` deltas, so a benchmark machine's vsync does not mask a slow frame.
- Layer isolation is asserted via counters rather than by pixel comparison; counters are cheap, exact and stable across GPUs (important for `R8`).
- Hit-test sub-linearity is asserted as a ratio rather than an absolute, so the test survives hardware upgrades.
- The k6 scripts run against a dedicated staging instance with a seeded 500-drawing user; they are nightly, not per-PR, because they need real Postgres and 10 minutes.
- Every benchmark records the fixture, seed, commit SHA and hardware tag into its result JSON so historical comparison is valid.

## Test plan
- Calibration run on three consecutive commits of `main` to establish baselines and measure run-to-run variance; the regression threshold is set above measured noise, and the variance figure is recorded in the ticket.
- Seeded-regression validation: introduce per-frame geometry re-upload, a linear-scan hit test, and a full-recompute VWAP on a scratch branch; confirm each is caught by its own benchmark and by no other (precision of attribution matters for triage).
- Tree benchmark validated by disabling virtualisation on a scratch branch and confirming the DOM-node-count assertion fires.

## Security notes
- Load scripts run only against staging with seeded users, never production or live-connected environments; the k6 config pins the base URL and refuses a host outside the allowlist, so a mistyped target cannot become an unintentional DoS against a real deployment.
- The 500-op batch scenario doubles as a resource-exhaustion probe; any observed unbounded memory growth is reported to `E14-X01` as a DoS finding rather than only as a perf number.
- Benchmark artefacts contain no user data; fixtures are synthetic.

## Accessibility notes
- The object-tree benchmark measures the surface that `SCR-036` designates as the accessible alternative to canvas manipulation. A tree that is slow at 500 objects is an accessibility failure, not just a performance one, because it is the only path available to a keyboard or screen-reader user — this framing is recorded in the benchmark's header and its failures are routed to the a11y specialist as well as the perf owner.
- Keyboard nudge latency (arrow key → visible move) is measured in the tree benchmark file and budgeted at ≤100 ms so the keyboard path is not second-class.

## Performance notes
- Budgets asserted: SCR-037 drag ≥58 fps with 200 drawings; roadmap 30 fps floor at worst case; US-DRAW-005 ≤2 ms per anchored-VWAP update; US-DRAW-008 tree virtualised at ≥500 objects; `21-database-schema.md` budget 28 < 5 ms for the drawings query; plus the global frame budget #1 (≤16.6 ms p95) which the drag benchmark must not itself violate at rest.
- Any budget met only by degradation is recorded as *met with degradation* and reported separately, so the headline number never hides a shed feature.

## Observability
- Results published to the CI perf dashboard alongside E11/E12 benchmarks; a per-epic view shows E14's four gating numbers over time.
- k6 runs export to the same Prometheus/Grafana stack as the API load profiles, so drawings write load is visible next to general API load during soak weeks.

## Definition of Done
- All eight scripts merged and producing results; baselines recorded with measured variance.
- `drag-200` and `layer-isolation` wired as required CI checks with the >10% rule.
- Seeded-regression attribution evidence linked.
- Results for all budgets recorded against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and referenced from the E14 epic ticket for its DoD perf rollup.
- Nightly k6 job scheduled and green for three consecutive nights.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T03` (drawings render layer), `E14-T04` (hit-test index), `E14-S03` (zone tools, needed for a representative mixed set), `E14-S05` (anchored VWAP) for benchmark 4.
- E11 benchmark harness and reference-hardware definition; E13 indicator set for the worst-case ladder.

## Branch
`test/e14-perf-pack`

## References
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-037 performance clause, SCR-036 performance clause
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 1 and 2, §5.4 perf gate
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-005 NFR, US-DRAW-008 NFR
- `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` budgets #1, #2
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` query budget 28
- `docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md` (render passes, degradation ladder)


## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. docs/plan/26-chart-engine-design.md §3.9/§3.11 (hit-testing, interaction)
2. docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md (relevant SCR entries)
3. docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md (relevant CMP entries)
4. docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md §3.1.6/§4 (no drag-only, keyboard path)
5. This ticket's own **Context**, **Scope / Deliverables**, **Out of scope**, **Technical notes / design** and **Dependencies** sections above — they are ticket-specific and override the generic reading list where they conflict.

- packages/chart-engine/src/layers/drawings/**, apps/web/src/** (drawing toolbar/UI bindings), packages/ui/** (shared controls)
- Update package README/TSDoc or module docstrings for any new public symbol introduced.
- Add/extend tests under the corresponding `test/`, `tests/`, or `e2e/` directory named above.

title: Chaos scenarios for drawings: offline edits, conflicts and partial batch failure
body:
## Context
`E14-T02` gives the client an optimistic store with debounced batch writes and a local undo stack. That design is right for interaction latency and wrong by default for durability: every optimistic system has a failure mode where the user believes something is saved and it is not. Because a drawing is a trader's record of a decision, a silently lost level is a correctness failure with real consequences, and `30-release-roadmap.md` exit criterion 5 requires zero loss across reload, restart and relaunch.

`docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` mandates chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate limiting) as a distinct layer. This ticket applies that discipline to the drawings write path: what happens when the network dies mid-drag, when two sessions edit the same shape, when the server rejects half a batch, when the browser is closed before the debounce fires.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `e2e/drawings/chaos/` scenarios, executed with Playwright network interception plus a toxiproxy-style fault layer on the staging API:
  1. **Offline during drag** — go offline mid-drag, complete the drag, come back online. Expected: the mutation is retried and lands; the UI shows an unsaved/pending state while offline (never a silent success); the final server state matches the final on-screen geometry.
  2. **Offline permanently** — offline, create three drawings, reload without reconnecting. Expected: the user was warned before losing them (explicit unsaved indicator and a beforeunload-class guard), and the documented behaviour (loss vs local queue) is what actually happens — the scenario asserts the *documented* contract and fails if the contract is unwritten.
  3. **Close before debounce** — mutate and close the tab within the 500 ms debounce window. Expected: a flush on pagehide/visibilitychange, or an explicitly documented acceptance of the loss window. Silent loss without either is a defect.
  4. **Server 500 on batch** — the batch endpoint returns `500` for the first two attempts and succeeds on the third. Expected: bounded exponential retry, no duplicate shapes, no lost shapes, the user informed if retries exhaust.
  5. **Server 422 on batch (poison op)** — one operation in the batch is permanently invalid. Expected: because the batch is transactional, the whole batch fails; the client must not retry forever, must isolate the poison operation, must not roll the user's canvas back to a state they did not ask for without telling them, and must surface an actionable error.
  6. **Rate limited (429)** — rapid dragging triggers API rate limiting. Expected: backoff, coalescing of pending mutations into fewer batches, and no dropped final state.
  7. **Concurrent edit, two sessions** — the same drawing moved in session A and deleted in session B. Expected: the documented conflict policy (last-write-wins with `updated_at`, per the schema's `updated_at` column) is applied deterministically, both sessions converge, and the losing session is told rather than silently overwritten.
  8. **Concurrent edit, same session two panes** — the same symbol-scoped drawing edited from two synced panes simultaneously; expected convergence with no duplicate rows.
  9. **Clock skew** — a client whose clock is 10 minutes ahead writes a drawing; expected: server-assigned `updated_at` governs ordering and a skewed client cannot win a conflict it should lose.
  10. **Undo across a failed write** — delete a drawing, the delete fails at the server, then `Ctrl+Z`. Expected: the undo stack and the server state converge to one coherent outcome, with no phantom restore of a drawing that was never deleted, and no orphan.
  11. **Postgres unavailable** — the database is down for 30 s. Expected: `503` with the standard envelope, the client queues or reports, no client crash, full recovery without user action beyond a retry.
  12. **Soft-delete/restore race** — restoring via undo while the retention purge job targets the same soft-deleted row (retention: soft-deleted config rows purged after 90 d per `21-database-schema.md`). Expected: either a clean restore or a clean, explained failure — never a dangling reference from `alert_id` or from a synced pane.
- **A written failure-mode table** in `qa/plans/e14-drawings-chaos.md`: fault, injection method, expected observable behaviour, the contract clause it comes from, and the ticket that owns the fix if behaviour is undefined.

## Out of scope
- Engine-level WebGL context loss (owned by E11's chaos work), though scenario 13 cross-references it to confirm drawings are restored with the scene.
- Exchange-side faults; drawings do not touch the exchange.
- Perf under fault (`E14-Q05` covers clean-path load).
- Security-motivated fault injection (replay, forged ids) — `E14-X02`.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A drag completed offline is not silently lost
  Given a trendline being dragged when the network drops
  When the drag completes and connectivity is restored within the retry window
  Then the final geometry is persisted exactly once
  And an unsaved-state indicator was visible for the whole offline period

Scenario: A poison operation does not wedge the client
  Given a batch containing one permanently invalid operation
  When the client receives 422 three times
  Then the client stops retrying, isolates the invalid operation and surfaces an actionable error
  And the remaining valid mutations are re-submitted successfully in a subsequent batch

Scenario: Failure case - concurrent edit produces divergence
  Given session A moves a drawing while session B deletes it
  When both mutations settle
  Then both sessions display the same final state after refresh
  And the session whose change was discarded was notified

Scenario: Edge case - the database is unavailable mid-session
  Given Postgres is stopped for 30 seconds
  When the user creates two drawings and continues working
  Then the API returns 503 with the standard error envelope and the client does not crash
  And after recovery the two drawings exist exactly once each with correct geometry
```

## Technical notes / design
- Faults are injected at two levels: Playwright route interception (status codes, latency, offline) for client-behaviour scenarios, and a proxy/container control for infrastructure scenarios (Postgres down, 429 from the gateway). Each scenario names its level so it can be run in the right environment.
- Every scenario ends with a **convergence assertion**: reload both sessions and compare `GET /drawings` payloads; "looks right on screen" is never sufficient.
- Duplicate detection uses drawing ids plus a geometry hash, catching both the classic "retry created two rows" and the subtler "retry created one row with stale geometry".
- Where behaviour is currently undefined (notably scenarios 2, 3 and 7), this ticket's job is to force a decision: the scenario file records the decision, the owning ticket implements it, and the test then asserts it. An undocumented behaviour is itself a finding, recorded on `E14-T02`.
- Scenarios are tagged `@e14 @chaos` and excluded from the PR-required set; they run nightly and before the R1 PRR.

## Test plan
- Each scenario runs 5× to shake out timing-dependent passes; a scenario that passes only sometimes is treated as a product defect, not a flaky test, until proven otherwise.
- A control run with no faults injected must pass every convergence assertion, proving the assertions are not fault-dependent.
- Results feed the R1 PRR evidence pack per `07-release-and-prr.md`.

## Security notes
- Retry logic is checked for unbounded amplification: a client that retries a 500-op batch without backoff is a self-inflicted DoS vector and is reported to `E14-X01`.
- Scenario 7 and 9 confirm that conflict resolution relies on server-assigned timestamps, so a malicious or broken client cannot win a write race by lying about time — a tampering mitigation the threat model claims.
- Offline queues must not persist drawing payloads in plaintext beyond the session in a way that outlives logout; scenario 2 checks that logging out clears any queued mutations.

## Accessibility notes
- Every error and pending state introduced by these scenarios must be announced, not only coloured: unsaved/pending indicators and failure messages are asserted to be exposed via a polite live region per `05-accessibility-standard.md`, so a screen-reader user learns their level was not saved.
- Scenario 10 (undo across a failed write) is asserted through the object tree as well as the canvas, since the tree is the accessible surface.

## Performance notes
- Retry/backoff must not degrade interaction: during scenarios 4 and 6, frame time is sampled and must stay within the SCR-037 drag budget — a retry storm on the main thread would show up here.
- Coalescing is asserted quantitatively in scenario 6: N rapid mutations must produce fewer than N batches.

## Observability
- Each scenario asserts the expected server-side log and metric signature: failed batch counter, retry counter, conflict counter. A fault that is invisible in telemetry is reported as an observability gap against `E14-T01`/`E14-T02`.
- Client console errors are captured; an unhandled promise rejection during any scenario fails it.

## Definition of Done
- All twelve scenarios implemented, with the failure-mode table merged at `qa/plans/e14-drawings-chaos.md`.
- Every previously undefined behaviour now documented, with the owning ticket linked and the assertion in place.
- Nightly job green for three consecutive runs; results attached to the R1 PRR evidence pack.
- No unhandled client exceptions in any scenario.

## Dependencies
- `E14-T02` (optimistic store, retry, undo), `E14-Q04` (contract behaviour the chaos cases assume), `E14-T01` (endpoints).
- Fault-injection tooling shared with E08's chaos work.

`test/e14-chaos-drawings`

title: Accessibility audit of the drawing surface, toolbar and object tree
body:
## Context
R1 exit criterion 9 in `30-release-roadmap.md` is unambiguous: "every chart is operable without a mouse — keyboard data cursor reads OHLCV per bar, **drawings can be created and adjusted by keyboard**, and a screen-reader pass is signed off by the a11y specialist". The §5.4 gate adds "axe-core zero violations on all R1 routes; manual NVDA + VoiceOver pass on chart and **drawing flows**".

Drawings are the hardest a11y problem in the product, because the primary surface is a WebGL canvas with no semantics at all. `14-screens-catalogue.md` resolves this by designating `SCR-036` (the object tree, `role="tree"`) as "the a11y-complete alternative to manipulating canvas objects by mouse" and requiring that "every canvas object is reachable and editable here by keyboard". SCR-037 adds that "each drawing has an accessible name and is listed in SCR-036" and that drawings can be created entirely by keyboard via SCR-045's grid. `E14-K01` chose the concrete pattern.

This ticket is the audit that proves the claim, or produces the defect list that makes it true before R1 ships.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated sweep**: axe-core runs (via the existing CI integration) on every state of SCR-037 and SCR-036 — toolbar idle, tool armed, properties popover open for each tool family, template menu open, tree empty, tree populated, tree with 500 objects, multi-select active, error states from `E14-Q06`. Target: zero violations; any accepted exception is recorded with a rationale and an owner, per `05-accessibility-standard.md`.
- **Keyboard-only conformance matrix**: every operation in US-DRAW-001..009 × {achievable by keyboard? via which path? how many keystrokes?}. Operations achievable only via the canvas with a pointer are defects. Explicitly covered: tool selection (`Alt+T/H/F/R/M`), magnet toggle (`Ctrl+M`), anchor placement, anchor re-adjust, nudge (arrow = 1 tick, Shift+arrow = 10 ticks), multi-select, group move, lock, hide, reorder, style edit, template apply, delete, undo/redo, send-to-ticket from the position tool.
- **Screen-reader passes**, scripted and recorded, on NVDA + Firefox, NVDA + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari, and VoiceOver + the Electron shell:
  - Create a trendline end to end and confirm each anchor placement is announced with its time and price.
  - Navigate the tree, confirm each item announces type, anchor time, anchor price, visibility and lock state (the SCR-036 contract).
  - Nudge a level and confirm the new price is announced (politely, debounced — not per keypress spam).
  - Open and complete the properties popover as a standard form.
  - Encounter an error (poison batch from `E14-Q06`) and confirm it is announced.
- **Focus management review**: focus visible at all times per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; focus returns to the invoking control when a popover closes; no focus trap in the popover except the intended modal-style trap; the tree's roving tabindex behaves per the `role="tree"` pattern; arming a tool never steals focus into the canvas without an escape route (`Esc` disarms and returns focus).
- **Contrast and non-colour encoding review**: drawing colours from `CMP-031 ColorSwatch` tokens meet WCAG 2.2 AA against both themes; selected/hover/locked states are distinguishable without colour alone (US-DRAW-003's "fills must respect the minimum contrast of candles drawn over them" is verified with the flatten-opacity toggle both on and off); the magnet-snap highlight is perceivable non-visually (announced) as well as visually.
- **Target sizes**: WCAG 2.2 AA target-size checks on toolbar buttons, popover controls and tree row controls; grab handles verified ≥24 px per US-DRAW-001's NFR at 100/150/200% zoom and at 200% browser text scaling.
- **Reduced-motion and zoom**: `prefers-reduced-motion` respected by any drawing animation; the whole surface usable at 200% zoom and at 320 px-equivalent reflow without loss of function.
- **Deliverable**: `qa/a11y/e14-drawings-audit.md` — findings list with severity, WCAG success-criterion reference, reproduction, screenshot/recording, and an owning ticket for each; plus a sign-off section for the a11y specialist.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the defects found (each becomes a Bug against the owning story; blockers must be fixed before the epic's DoD).
- The chart data cursor and OHLCV announcements (E11 owns those).
- Indicator manager rows that are not drawings (E13 owns those, though the shared tree is audited once here and the finding routed).
- Full-product a11y certification — E43/E46 own the programme-level pass.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every drawing operation is reachable without a mouse
  Given the keyboard-only conformance matrix covering US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009
  When each operation is attempted with the keyboard alone on NVDA and on VoiceOver
  Then every operation completes successfully by at least one documented path
  And any operation that cannot is filed as a blocking defect against its story

Scenario: Every drawing is discoverable and named
  Given a chart with one drawing of each shipped tool
  When the object tree is navigated with a screen reader
  Then every drawing is announced with its type, anchor time, anchor price, visibility and lock state
  And no drawing exists on the canvas that is absent from the tree

Scenario: Failure case - an unnamed drawing ships
  Given a build where the text annotation tool creates objects without an accessible name
  When the audit's naming check runs
  Then the finding is recorded as a blocking WCAG 4.1.2 defect with a reproduction
  And the epic cannot reach Done until it is fixed or waived by the a11y specialist in writing

Scenario: Edge case - nudging does not flood the screen reader
  Given a level being nudged with 20 rapid Shift+ArrowUp presses
  When the announcements are captured
  Then the final price is announced via a debounced polite live region
  And the user is not read 20 consecutive interruptions
```

## Technical notes / design
- The audit runs against the S09 staging build with all S07-S08 drawing stories merged, so it judges the shipped surface rather than a prototype.
- axe-core states are driven by the `E14-Q03` Playwright specs with an axe step injected, reusing existing navigation code rather than duplicating it.
- Screen-reader passes are recorded (audio + screen) and the transcripts are attached, because "NVDA said something" is not evidence — the exact utterance is the artefact the specialist signs off.
- Announcement volume is measured, not just presence: the audit counts live-region utterances per interaction, since over-announcement is as disabling as silence (the `CMP-010`/`CMP-008` precedent in `15-component-catalogue.md` already debounces to ~250 ms).
- Findings use the standard severity ladder from `05-accessibility-standard.md`; anything that makes an operation impossible without a pointer is automatically blocking for R1 given exit criterion 9.

## Test plan
- Two auditors work independently on the keyboard matrix and reconcile, to reduce the chance a habitual path hides a gap.
- Each finding is reproduced by a second person before filing.
- After fixes land, a targeted re-test of every blocking finding is performed and recorded before sign-off; the axe sweep is re-run in full.

## Security notes
- Screen and audio recordings are scrubbed of any credentials typed during login and stored in the internal QA artefact store, not in the repository.
- The audit confirms that accessible names derived from user-entered text (annotation labels) are rendered as text content and never as markup — an accessible-name path is an injection path, and the corpus from `E14-X02` is used for the naming check on the tree.

## Accessibility notes
- Standard: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`. Success criteria in explicit scope: 1.4.3 contrast, 1.4.11 non-text contrast, 1.4.12 text spacing, 1.4.13 content on hover/focus (the properties popover), 2.1.1/2.1.2 keyboard and no trap, 2.4.3 focus order, 2.4.7 focus visible, 2.4.11 focus not obscured, 2.5.7 dragging movements (**the key one for E14 — every drag must have a non-dragging alternative**), 2.5.8 target size, 3.3.1 error identification, 4.1.2 name/role/value, 4.1.3 status messages.
- SC 2.5.7 is called out because drawing is fundamentally a dragging interaction; the audit's core question is whether the keyboard placement mode and the tree together constitute a complete single-pointer-free alternative.

## Performance notes
- The 500-object tree state is audited for responsiveness as well as semantics; if virtualisation removes off-screen items from the accessibility tree in a way that breaks navigation, that is a finding, not an optimisation.
- Screen-reader interaction latency (keypress → announcement) is sampled; over ~500 ms is filed as a usability defect.

## Observability
- Findings tracked in the standard a11y defect view with the `a11y` label so the epic DoD rollup can show zero open blockers.
- axe results published as CI artefacts per run so a regression after fixes is visible without re-auditing manually.

## Definition of Done
- `qa/a11y/e14-drawings-audit.md` merged with the conformance matrix, findings, recordings and the WCAG mapping.
- axe-core zero violations across all audited states (or written, owner-approved exceptions).
- All blocking findings fixed and re-tested, or waived in writing by the a11y specialist with a follow-up ticket.
- Manual NVDA and VoiceOver passes signed off by the a11y specialist, satisfying the §5.4 R1 gate for drawing flows.
- Result linked from the E14 epic ticket's a11y DoD item.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q03` (navigation code and keyboard spec), `E14-S04`/`E14-S05` (the last of the S08 tools), `E14-S10` (toolbar), `E14-K01` (the keyboard pattern being audited), and the shared `SCR-036` tree from E13/E14.

## Branch
`test/e14-a11y-audit`

## References
- `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criterion 9, §5.4 a11y gate
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-036, SCR-037 (a11y clauses, hotkeys)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-223, CMP-224, CMP-017, CMP-031, CMP-008, CMP-010, CMP-022
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-DRAW-001 (handle size, nudge), US-DRAW-006 (screen-reader scenario), US-DRAW-008 (tree navigable by keyboard)
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` row 2568 (accessible canvas alternatives)

title: Exploratory charters, E14 regression pack and epic QA sign-off
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires, for an Epic to be Done, that "an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass [is] executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA", alongside a zero-open-P0/P1 condition and a demo to the Owner. E14 is the last R1 charting epic with a large human-facing interaction surface, and scripted tests by construction only find what someone thought to write down. Drawing tools are famously rich in emergent bugs — a shape dragged onto a collapsed pane, a fib drawn backwards on an inverted log scale, a template applied to a locked object, 300 shapes pasted onto a symbol with 3 days of history.

This ticket provides the two things that close the epic: time-boxed exploratory charters aimed at exactly those seams, and the assembled regression pack that every later train re-runs so drawings do not rot while E18-E46 are built on top.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Exploratory charters** (session-based, 90 minutes each, recorded per `03-testing-strategy.md`), at minimum:
  1. *Scale and geometry abuse* — explore drawings across log/percent/inverted scales, extreme zoom, 100k-bar history, and bar-type switches, to find anchoring drift the automated matrix missed.
  2. *Density and legibility* — 200-500 overlapping zones, fills, fib grids and labels; hunt for unreadable price action, unclickable handles and label collisions; exercise the flatten-opacity toggle.
  3. *Object management under stress* — deep undo/redo chains beyond the 50-op NFR, interleaved with lock/hide/delete-all, multi-select and template application; hunt for stack corruption and orphans.
  4. *Sync and layout interactions* — drawings across sync groups, multi-pane layouts, pane close/reopen, workspace save/load (E15 seam), symbol switch mid-drag.
  5. *Position tool and the trading seam* — R:R maths at edge sizes, tick/lot rounding, profile caps, send-to-ticket with a changed profile between drag and send.
  6. *Annotation content* — long text, RTL text, emoji, multi-line, pasted rich text, and text at extreme zoom; overlaps with `E14-X02` for hostile input but from a usability angle.
  7. *Keyboard-first day in the life* — an entire analysis session with no mouse at all, hunting for the operation that quietly requires one.
  8. *Persistence paranoia* — reload, relaunch, second device, second session, slow network, at every point in the drawing lifecycle.
- Each charter produces: a session sheet (charter, duration, areas covered, bugs found, notes, follow-up charters), filed under `qa/exploratory/e14/`.
- **E14 regression pack**: a curated, tagged selection (`@e14-regression`) drawn from `E14-Q02` (view-change matrix), `E14-Q03` (lifecycle, persistence, sync, keyboard), `E14-Q04` (contract + drift guard) and the highest-value chaos scenarios, plus a short manual checklist for what remains unautomatable. Runtime budget ≤20 minutes so it can run per-release, and it is registered in the release checklist of `07-release-and-prr.md` and re-run at R2-R5 as an inherited pack.
- **Bug triage and closure**: every finding filed with severity per `03-testing-strategy.md` §11.3; anchoring drift and persistence loss are P0 by the `E14-Q01` convention; a triage session with the E14 lead produces fix-now / fix-later dispositions, and every fix-later carries an explicit owner and target train.
- **Epic QA sign-off record** on the E14 epic ticket: pass/fail per story group, coverage numbers for `packages/chart-engine/src/drawings/**` and `apps/web/src/drawings/**` against the 85%/80% thresholds, the perf numbers from `E14-Q05`, the a11y sign-off from `E14-Q07`, the security sign-off from `E14-X02`, the open-defect list, and an explicit statement that R1 exit criteria 5 and 9 are satisfied for drawings.

## Out of scope
- Writing new automation for findings (each becomes its own ticket; the pack only assembles what exists).
- The R1 PRR itself (`07-release-and-prr.md`) — this feeds it.
- Indicator, layout or recorder regression packs (E13, E15, E16 own theirs); the E14 pack references the shared workspace save/load case rather than duplicating it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All charters executed and recorded
  Given the eight exploratory charters for E14
  When each is executed as a time-boxed session
  Then a session sheet exists for each under qa/exploratory/e14/
  And every bug found is filed with severity, reproduction and an owning story

Scenario: The regression pack runs inside its budget
  Given the @e14-regression selection
  When it is executed on a clean staging build
  Then it completes within 20 minutes
  And it covers at least one case from every US-DRAW-001 through US-DRAW-009 story

Scenario: Failure case - an open P0 blocks the epic
  Given an unresolved anchoring-drift defect found during the scale-abuse charter
  When epic QA sign-off is attempted
  Then sign-off is refused and recorded as refused with the blocking defect linked
  And the epic stays out of Done until the defect is fixed or explicitly waived by the Owner

Scenario: Edge case - a descoped tool is encountered during exploration
  Given pitchfork and Fibonacci time-zone tools were descoped per the roadmap descoping ladder
  When a charter encounters their toolbar entries
  Then their absence or disabled state is verified as intentional against the descope record
  And a visible half-implemented tool is filed as a defect rather than accepted
```

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are genuinely exploratory: no step-by-step scripts, but each has a stated mission, a risk it is hunting, and a defined area, per session-based test management.
- Charter 7 (keyboard-first day) is run by someone who is not the a11y auditor, so it finds usability gaps rather than re-finding known conformance issues.
- The regression pack is assembled by tag, not by copying tests, so it cannot drift from the suites it selects from; a CI job asserts the tag selection is non-empty for each source suite.
- The manual remainder of the pack is deliberately short and each item carries a note on why it is not automated and what would be needed — this is the input to the next train's automation backlog.

## Test plan
- The pack is dry-run twice: once on a known-good build (must be fully green) and once on a build with a deliberately reverted drawing persistence commit (must fail, proving sensitivity).
- Charter coverage is reviewed against the story list so no story group goes unexplored.
- Sign-off is peer-reviewed by a second QA engineer before being posted.

## Security notes
- Charter 6 escalates any input-handling anomaly to `E14-X02` rather than filing it as a cosmetic bug, so a rendering oddity caused by an injection vector is not mis-triaged.
- The sign-off record explicitly requires the `E14-X02` security sign-off to be present; QA cannot sign the epic off without it, per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2.
- Exploratory sessions run against staging with seeded users only; no production data is touched.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 7 is mandatory, not optional, and its findings are routed to the a11y specialist as well as the E14 lead.
- The regression pack includes the `keyboard.spec.ts` suite from `E14-Q03` permanently, so the R1 keyboard guarantee is re-verified at every later release rather than being a one-time R1 achievement.

## Performance notes
- Charters 2 and 3 are explicitly perf-adjacent: any jank observed is reported with a trace and cross-referenced to `E14-Q05`'s benchmarks so it is either a known budgeted cost or a new finding.
- The sign-off record carries the four gating perf numbers verbatim, so a later regression has an unambiguous baseline.

## Observability
- Session sheets, bug links, pack runtime and the sign-off record are all linked from the E14 epic ticket, giving one place to audit the epic's quality evidence.
- The regression pack publishes a per-run summary to the CI dashboard with the `@e14-regression` tag so its health is trackable across trains.

## Definition of Done
- All eight charters executed, recorded and triaged.
- Regression pack assembled, tagged, runtime-verified, dry-run in both directions, and registered in the release checklist.
- Zero open P0/P1 defects against E14 scope, or explicit Owner-signed acceptances.
- Epic QA sign-off comment posted on E14 with coverage, perf, a11y and security evidence, including an explicit statement on R1 exit criteria 5 and 9.
- Follow-up automation tickets filed for every manual-only pack item.

## Dependencies
- `E14-Q02`, `E14-Q03`, `E14-Q05`, `E14-Q06`, `E14-Q07` must be complete; `E14-X02`'s sign-off is required before the final comment is posted.
- All E14 stories (`E14-S01`..`E14-S10`) merged.

## Branch
`test/e14-regression-and-signoff`

## References
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 Epic DoD
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` (exploratory/session-based testing, severity ladder)
- `docs/plan/07-release-and-prr.md` (release checklist, PRR evidence)
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5.3 criteria 5 and 9, §12 descoping ladder
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §6 DRAW
- `qa/plans/e14-drawing-tools-test-plan.md`
